**17.1.4b Polaron Persistence Under Substrate Turnover [Tier 3]**

A naive reading of §17.1.4 invites an obvious objection: β-tubulin is not a permanent fixture. Dynamic axonal microtubules undergo catastrophe and rescue on timescales of minutes; dendritic tubulin pools exchange with a half-life of approximately one day; even the more stable acetylated/detyrosinated sub-population turns over on the order of hours to days (Gornstein & Schwarz 2014; Janke & Magiera 2020; Kapitein & Hoogenraad 2015). Personal identity, by contrast, persists across years and decades, and waking conscious attention persists across hours. If the Identity Polaron were *constituted by* a specific set of tubulin molecules, it would be dissolved and reassembled many times per day, and the phenomenology of continuous selfhood would be unintelligible.

GCT offers a conditional route within the holographic-restriction framework already established in §17.1.2b and §17.1.4: the Polaron is **not** an aggregate of specific dimers, but a proposed topological restriction of the phason field $\Phi_\perp$ to a network *site*. No unique physical topological invariant has yet been derived for that restriction. The candidate $N=144$ dodecahedral water-clathrate motif concerns the scaffold geometry (Tier 3 conditional pending O.33 MD/NMR/free-energy validation); it does not by itself choose a defect configuration space or prove persistence. Three distinct stability principles are therefore proposed to cooperate on the positive O.16/O.21/O.33 branch:

1. **Topological-sector persistence (Tier 1 conditional mathematics; Tier 3 Polaron adoption and biological-continuity premise).** Two candidate integer charges must be kept distinct. (a) *Vortex branch:* if a non-vanishing $S^1$-valued phason phase is defined on the exterior of a line core, its meridional winding $q_{\rm vor} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\oint d\theta \in \pi_1(S^1) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ is the type of invariant defined by the phase-vortex line integral used elsewhere in GCT; it is not a $\pi_3$ texture charge. (b) *Texture branch:* if instead the physical order parameter is a continuous map from compactified space $S^3$ into a target $M = S^3$ or $S^3/2I$ (the local icosahedral orientation manifold), then $\pi_3(M) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ supplies a texture degree $w$ (V3 Ch7 §7.1). Either charge is stable only while the field stays in the declared admissible configuration space; amplitude zeros, core reconnection, boundary escape, or scaffold dissolution can change it. GCT has not yet supplied the physical order parameter, target, boundary conditions, or a stabilizing action: the quadratic continuum elastic energy alone obeys Derrick scaling, $E_2[U_\lambda] = \lambda E_2[U]$, and permits collapse as $\lambda \to 0$, so lattice pinning, a higher-derivative term, or another stabilizing constraint must be derived. The biological premise that a tubulin replacement event preserves the relevant lattice site, chirality, Trp orientation, and charge is Tier 3 pending assembled-MT turnover and O.21 validation; only under all of these premises would the Polaron flow through tubulin turnover the way a persistent field pattern flows through molecular replacement.

2. **Stable Sub-Network Anchoring (Tier 3).** The Polaron does not require *every* microtubule in the network to be persistent. The acetylated/detyrosinated stable MT sub-population provides a long-correlation-time scaffold sufficient to bridge waking-state attentional persistence: direct measurements and reviews support a stable acetylated/detyrosinated sub-population on hours-to-day cellular timescales (Webster & Borisy 1989 *J. Cell Sci.* 92:57–65 — acetylated microtubule domains turn over slowly; Janke & Magiera 2020 *Nat. Rev. Mol. Cell Biol.* 21:307 — review with neuronal-tissue extrapolations; Aillaud, Bosc, Saoudi et al. 2017 *Science* 358:1448 — TTL/VASH detyrosination kinetics; Tas et al. 2017 *Neuron* 96:1264 and Katrukha et al. 2021 *eLife* 10:e67925 — neuronal microtubule array mapping / modification localization; Andreu-Carbó, Egoldt, Velluz & Aumeier 2024 *Nat. Commun.* 15:2029 — acetylation-gradient measurements around microtubule damage). Dynamic MTs ($\tau \sim$ minutes; Mitchison & Kirschner 1984; Gornstein & Schwarz 2014) couple into and out of this stable backbone but are not load-bearing for identity continuity. This is consistent with the empirical observation that microtubule-stabilizing post-translational modifications track with neuronal maturation and long-term memory consolidation (Penazzi, Bakota & Brandt 2016 *Int. Rev. Cell Mol. Biol.* 321:89).

3. **Network Redundancy and Holographic Restriction (Tier 3).** Per the holographic restriction principle (§17.1.2b), the Polaron is the *same* candidate topological restriction of $\Phi_\perp$ evaluated at every Trp site in the coherent network — not $N$ independent copies summed. The information content is encoded in the relative phases of the network, not in any single dimer. If the O.21 assembled-MT lumen-axis screen closes positively, $\sim 1.6\times10^9$ candidate Trp residues per neuron would make per-dimer replacement an $\mathcal{O}(1/N)$ perturbation and therefore negligible against the coherent ensemble. Under the current 6DPU local wall-patch screen, this remains a Tier 3 sensitivity case pending O.21 closure rather than an assembled-MT proof.

**Material and functional tests.** This account proposes three experimentally accessible claims; none is presently a Level-II test:

(a) **Stabilization pharmacology and attention-related function.** Compare pharmacological stabilization of dynamic microtubules (e.g., low-dose paclitaxel, parthenolide) with selective perturbation of the acetylated/detyrosinated sub-population (e.g., via HDAC6 overexpression or tubulin-tyrosine-ligase modulation). The Tier 3 candidate model predicts different effects on registered spin/coherence proxies and attention-related behaviour across turnover timescales. Existing HDAC6-inhibitor and TTL-knockout literature (Aillaud et al. 2017) provides partial biological context, not a consciousness verdict.

(b) **Anaesthesia material-proxy comparison.** For volatile anaesthetics proposed to bind a tubulin pocket (Craddock et al. 2017), test whether Trp radical-pair and lattice-coherence proxies change without microtubule dismantling and recover on seconds rather than tubulin-resynthesis (hours-days) timescales. Clinical reversibility motivates the timescale comparison, but a proxy change or recovery does not identify an Identity Polaron or explain phenomenal loss.

**17.1.5 Glial and Cerebellar Candidate-Control Comparisons [Tier 3]**

A complete substrate theory would have to determine whether an Identity-Polaron construction is physically realized in any tubulin-bearing network. The present Tier-3 program instead compares two useful candidate-control architectures without assigning a substrate verdict: **glia** (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, which contain tubulin and form extensive networks) and **the cerebellum** (~50 billion granule cells with massively parallel feedforward architecture, minimal recurrent integration). The typed coupling, Identity-Polaron construction, and independent phenomenal bridge remain open in every tissue.

**17.1.5a Glial Candidate-Control Comparison**

Astrocytes are active participants in neural computation (tripartite synapses, calcium signaling, gliotransmission; Araque et al. 1999 *Trends Neurosci.* 22:208; Araque et al. 2014 *Neuron* 81:728; Bazargani & Attwell 2016 *Nat. Neurosci.* 19:182 on astrocyte calcium signalling in cortical circuits; Poskanzer & Yuste 2016 *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 113:E2675 on astrocyte regulation of cortical state; Khakh & Sofroniew 2015 *Nat. Neurosci.* 18:942 on diversity of astrocyte forms and functions). They contain tubulin and form connected networks, making them a comparative preparation for testing candidate spin/coherence observables rather than an assumed Identity-Polaron-negative class.

The Tier-3 GCT research program (V3 Ch13 §13.2; §16.2.6) tracks three candidate conditions without treating them as necessary or sufficient for Polaron formation:
1. **Non-zero nuclear spin density.** Both neurons and astrocytes contain Trp-bearing β-tubulin; satisfied equally.
2. **Chiral molecular environment generating CISS torque.** β-tubulin chirality is identical between neurons and astrocytes; satisfied equally.
3. **Candidate coherence-bearing sub-network.** O.21/O.23/O.34 remain open, and $\eta_{Zeno}$ is only conditional external-rate arithmetic.

The discriminator is **microtubule network connectivity and post-translational modification density** [Tier 3 — comparative-architecture argument; the specific quantitative ratios below are calibrated estimates, not first-principles derivations]. Pyramidal neurons in cortical layers II/III and V have:
(a) extensive axonal MT bundles with high acetylated-MT fraction (stable sub-population, see §17.1.4b; cf. Janke & Magiera 2020 *Nat. Rev. Mol. Cell Biol.* 21:307 on neuronal MT post-translational modifications);
(b) long axonal MT arrays (cryo-ET architecture of mammalian sensory axons: Foster, Ventura Santos & Carter 2022 *J. Cell Biol.* 221:e202103154; the study measures architecture, not coherence);
(c) high local ATP flux from neuronal mitochondrial density (dominated by synaptic ion-pumping demand; Harris, Jolivet & Attwell 2012 *Neuron* 75:762 review synaptic energy use and supply), treated here as a candidate control for the proposed radical-pair response.

Astrocytes have:
(a) shorter, less-bundled MT networks compared to neuronal axonal tracts (Maccioni & Cambiazo 1995 *Physiol. Rev.* 75:835); the acetylated-MT fraction in astrocytes is lower than in neurons but the specific ratio in cortical tissue remains a [Tier 3 calibration target];
(b) MT orientation primarily local (process-stabilizing, not long-range);
(c) lower ATP flux density than pyramidal neurons (typical estimates place astrocyte oxidative metabolism at ~30-50% of neuronal levels per unit volume, e.g., Hyder et al. 2013 *J. Cereb. Blood Flow Metab.* 33:339 — a ~2-3× factor; direct microtubule-network-localised ATP measurement remains a [Tier 3 calibration target]).

**Tier-3 candidate-control comparison:** Astrocyte and neuron preparations can test whether the proposed spin/coherence response covaries with network architecture. Any difference constrains the mechanism; it does not assign either tissue a Level-II verdict.

**Empirical test (Protocol A, tissue arm):** Comparative spin-echo measurements on cultured astrocytes vs cortical neurons within the registered $[32, 200)$ MHz scan. The model's response ratio (neuron/astrocyte) is a ratio of radical-pair signal amplitude or yield, not of an intrinsic dephasing time $T_2$: ATP flux and acetylation could change radical-pair population or yield, but no derived route takes them into $T_2$. The ratio is composed of three multiplicative factors:
- **ATP-flux factor (~2-3×)** — astrocyte oxidative metabolism at 30-50% of neuronal levels per unit volume (Hyder et al. 2013);
- **Acetylated-MT-fraction factor (~2-3×)** — neuronal axonal MT bundles are stable-fraction-enriched relative to astrocytic processes (Janke & Magiera 2020; specific ratio in cortical tissue remains a Tier 3 calibration target);
- **Network-architecture factor (~2-3×)** — long-range bundled MT architecture in pyramidal axons is modeled as favoring the candidate response relative to astrocytic local-process orientation; cryo-ET does not itself measure coherence (Foster et al. 2022).

Composing these three factors gives a Tier 3 model estimate of the response ratio (neuron/astrocyte) $\approx 4\text{-}10\times$ within the registered scan band — broad-banded because the three calibration estimates each carry factor-2 uncertainty *and are not independent in vivo* (ATP flux, MT acetylation, and network coherence all co-vary with neuronal activity state; multiplicative composition therefore over-states the central estimate and the reported band is ~4-10× rather than 8-30×). **Rejection rule for the model:** a measured ratio below ~2× would reject the three-factor decomposition (one factor alone cannot account for any positive prediction); a measured ratio within the 4-10× envelope would be consistent with, but not confirm, the composite mechanism. Each of the three factors is individually a Tier 3 calibration target whose direct measurement (decorrelating ATP / acetylation / network-coherence contributions independently) would tighten the prediction. A further limitation is that none of the three sources reports a coherence time. They report cryo-ET architecture, neuronal energy consumption per unit volume, and relative oxidative metabolism; the step from those quantities to a response ratio is a modelling assumption of this framework and is not carried by the citations. The predicted envelope is therefore weaker than the individual measurements it is built from, and no part of it should be attributed to the cited work.

**Oligodendrocytes and microglia.** These provide additional candidate-control preparations for testing whether any spin/coherence response covaries with microtubule architecture and ATP flux. No categorical Polaron or Level-II inference is licensed; O.16 and O.21/O.23/O.34 remain open.

**17.1.5b Cerebellar Architecture as a Matched Functional/Material Control**

The cerebellum contains ~50 billion granule cells, ~10 million Purkinje cells, and a strongly feedforward-dominated architecture (Marr 1969 *J. Physiol.* 202:437; Ito 2008 *Nat. Rev. Neurosci.* 9:304). Those anatomical facts motivate comparisons with recurrent cortical tissue and are often read as implying low integrated information under IIT. They do not establish that an isolated cerebellum has zero integrated cause–effect structure at every IIT grain, lacks broadcast through every pathway, or realizes a local phenomenal subject. Table 17.5 accordingly records the isolated-cerebellum row as a Block-style comparison with Level II open (Tier 3; no validated substrate criterion yet).

**GCT reading via the §16.2.8d $P$- vs $A$-consciousness framework:** The cerebellum's tubulin-bearing Purkinje-cell network supplies candidate chirality and nuclear-spin controls, while its feedforward architecture gives a distinct broadcast comparison. These descriptors do not establish an Identity Polaron, $P$-consciousness, or Level II. The program therefore distinguishes:
- **Level I (universal proto-experience):** trivially, like all Field configurations;
- **Level IIA (Polaron $P$-consciousness without $A$-broadcast):** a Tier-3 interpretive possibility only if the complete physical and phenomenal-bridge program closes; no current tissue verdict follows;
- **Level IIB ($P$- + $A$-consciousness):** broadcast access is modeled as unavailable in the isolated feedforward preparation; this is not a phenomenal-status verdict.

**Current disposition:** Level IIA, Level IIB, and subject-count assignments for an isolated cerebellum are **open (Tier 3)**: no validated substrate criterion exists yet. Block's $P$-without-$A$ category (Block 2007) remains a useful conceptual comparison, not evidence for cerebellar phenomenal consciousness, and it does not assert local Purkinje-cell Polaron formation or a phenomenal state. Protocol A tissue measurements (and the abiotic Protocol A-Prime surrogate) can constrain the proposed mechanism but cannot execute that boundary.

**Falsifiable predictions:**
1. **Cerebellar tubulin Trp response test:** Protocol A (the in-vitro/tissue arm) can compare isolated cerebellar tissue with cortical-neuron preparations. The Tier-3 architecture model assigns a provisional response (amplitude/yield) ratio of ~0.3–0.7× from ATP-flux, microtubule-orientation, and acetylation inputs, but none of the cited measurements establishes coherence or a Polaron. A ratio at or above cortical-neuron level would falsify this sub-unity response model; any result would remain mechanistic rather than phenomenal.
2. **Targeted cerebellar stimulation phenomenology:** Direct cerebellar-stimulation reports can be collected alongside candidate response measures, but neither reports nor correlations establish a local Polaron or a $P$/$A$ boundary [Tier 3/Tier 4 exploratory comparison].
3. **Cerebellar agenesis / atrophy clinical data:** clinical outcomes constrain broadcast and functional models; they do not by themselves classify cortical or cerebellar $P$-consciousness (Schmahmann & Sherman 1998 *Brain* 121:561).

**Status:** Tier 3 candidate-control hypothesis. Comparative Protocol A tissue measurements can constrain a proposed spin/coherence mechanism, but the current program does not exclude or affirm Level II in cerebellar or glial tissue.

**17.2 Network Dynamics**

**17.2.1 Multi-Agent Theory and Interaction**

As a Tier 3 phenomenological network analogy, one may model compatibility among $N$ declared apertures with a **Topological Interaction** functional. The variables called phason overlap (**Topological Friction**), aligned selection (**Constructive Interference**), and misaligned selection (**Consensus Resistance**) are uncalibrated descriptors. No established Identity Polarons, physical $\mathcal{F}_{sel}$ operators, owner/subject count, or interpersonal phason interaction realizes them; shared reality is not thereby shown to be a simulation managed by such a network. [Tier 3 — Phenomenological Framework]

**17.2.2 Resonance Clusters**

A **Resonance Cluster** (Topological Lineage) may be modeled as a set of apertures with a measured physical coupling kernel. If a separate address-assignment bridge gives them Solenoid labels, and a filtration is chosen, they may also share a coarse cylinder. The ansatz $\kappa_{ij}=\kappa_0 e^{-\lambda_c d_H(i,j)}$ is Tier 3: $d_H$ measures shared address resolution only, and neither the topology nor a common prefix derives low metabolic cost, synchronization of renders, kinship, synchronicity, or non-local correlation. Those stronger readings ("Shared Realities") remain Tier 4 until a physical coupling and outcome model are supplied. [Tier 3 ansatz; Tier 4 — synchronicity and non-local correlation readings]

**17.2.3 Consensus Reality as Nash Equilibrium**

This subsection offers a Tier 3 network analogy for cross-perspectival stability. In its functional taxonomy:
* **Class 0 Patterns** (Rocks, stars) label relatively stable constraints.
* **Class 2 Agents** (Observers) label recursive response systems.

These labels do not prove that rocks lack every possible Selection Operator or that observers physically generate renders. The phrase **Nash Equilibrium of the Rendering Network** names a phenomenological model in which many coupled constraints stabilize public regularities. [Tier 3 — Phenomenological Framework] The expression $\sum_{j \neq i} \kappa_{ij} \cdot \Gamma_j$ is an uncalibrated aggregate-coupling ansatz; it does not derive a collective Zeno lock, a metabolic override threshold, divergent physical resistance to an individual Agent, or a universe-wide optimization of renders.

**17.2.4 The Suppression of Anomalies**

The **Topological Clamp** language is a Tier 4 speculative Psi analogy. No accepted data or derived interaction shows that observation exerts a force, that an environment carries a cumulative Zeno lock, or that an Agent can produce anomalous lattice perturbations. At most, ordinary social and measurement contexts can change behaviour, inference, noise, and reporting; a vacuum-clamping mechanism is not established. [Tier 4 — Speculative]

**17.3 Physical Basis of Directed Attention**

GCT proposes a Tier 3 research bridge between directed attention and chiral spin dynamics (CISS; §17.1.3). The field-typing analysis of §17.1.3 shows that the former vector Rashba-phason contraction is not an icosahedral scalar and that the present action supplies no type-correct, action-normalized spin–phason coupling. Ordinary CISS is a material spin response, whereas a GCT attention mechanism would require a matched, normalized coupling to $\Phi_\perp$ plus an independent bridge from that field response to intentional selection.

**17.3.1 Candidate Chiral-Spin Attention Bridge**
CISS-mediated currents may produce handedness-dependent ordinary spin polarization in a declared material. The further claims that current direction fixes a GCT winding vector **w** in E⊥ space and that this vector constitutes an Agent's intentional focus are unclosed Tier 3 hypotheses. They require a type-correct coupling with a non-zero coefficient (§17.1.3), source-derived spinor and material vertices, a material-to-vacuum field map, matched kinetic/mode/chirality normalization, sector-writing matrix elements, and a cognitive/phenomenal forward model.

**17.3.2 Testability (Protocol A-Prime)**
A CISS chirality-reversal experiment (V3 Ch13 §13.3.5.A) can test an enantiomer-odd material spin response. Reversing a biomimetic chiral cap (L→R) does not yet test reversal of an intentional axis. That stronger test becomes meaningful only after the material response is linked prospectively to a normalized GCT coordinate and a separately specified attention readout. Positive and null results presently constrain the proxy branch only: neither outcome is a verdict on GCT as a whole, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it (§17.1.3).

**17.4 States of Consciousness (Synthesis)**

We distinguish the modes of experience by four descriptors: the **Focus Manifold**, the **Coupling Coefficient** ($\kappa_{ext}$), **Dynamics**, and **Experience**. All entries below are a Tier 3 phenomenological classification unless marked Tier 4.

**17.4.1 Waking**
* **Manifold:** $E_\parallel$ (Physical Projection).
* **Coupling:** High ($\kappa_{ext} \approx 1$) [Tier 3 — uncalibrated phenomenological label; the former $e^{-\lambda_c d_H}$ address law is an unclosed optional ansatz].
* **Dynamics:** Modeled high Consensus Viscosity and stable cortical/sensorimotor broadcast; no established Identity-Polaron, Zeno-lock, or Level-II verdict follows from the waking-state label.
* **Experience:** Rigid, objective world; linear time; high effort to deviate.

**17.4.2 Dreaming**
* **Manifold:** $\Sigma_{local}$ — an internally generated model/render subspace (a private physical/cognitive aperture, not an intrinsic Solenoid branch).
* **Coupling:** Zero or strongly reduced external coupling ($\kappa_{ext} \to 0$) [Tier 3 — uncalibrated phenomenological label; first-principles dynamics deferred].
* **Dynamics:** Zero External Friction; Focus withdraws from the physical screen.
* **Experience:** Fluid, autopoietic reality; symbolic logic; zero effort to transform.

**17.4.3 Lucid Dreaming**
* **Manifold:** $\Sigma_{local}$ — an internally generated model/render subspace.
* **Coupling:** Zero or strongly reduced external coupling ($\kappa_{ext} \to 0$) [Tier 3 — uncalibrated phenomenological label; first-principles dynamics deferred].
* **Dynamics (surrogate):** Increased metacognitive control over internally generated content; **Volitional Torque** is an uncalibrated model label.
* **Experience:** Reports of recognizing the dream and altering its content. This does not show that an Agent applies physical torque, operates a renderer, or overrides a vacuum-lattice state.

**17.4.4 Deep Meditation**
* **Manifold:** Coarse-grained internal model states. If an address-assignment bridge gives them Solenoid labels and a filtration is chosen, selected cylinders may represent their address resolution.
* **Coupling:** Variable ($\kappa_{ext}$ decreasing toward zero) [Tier 3 — uncalibrated phenomenological label; first-principles dynamics deferred].
* **Dynamics:** **Attentional coarse-graining**. A cylinder projection ("P-adic Truncation") is one optional mathematical representation, not a literal movement toward an intrinsic Solenoid root.
* **Experience:** The reported reduction of fine self/world distinctions ("expansion", "dissolution of boundaries", "Unified Awareness") is modeled as progressive coarse-graining of the active physical/cognitive state. This phenomenological description does not certify a DMC-qualified substrate or a Selection Operator. Nested cylinders supply a membership analogy only: a coarse cylinder is not a parent observer, and one child does not thereby experience its siblings or the whole [Tier 3 phenomenological model; Level II open (Tier 3) — no validated substrate criterion yet].

**17.4.5 Orthogonal Navigation (Astral / NDE)**
* **Manifold:** $E_\perp$ (Internal Manifold).
* **Coupling:** Weak ($\kappa_{ext} \ll 1$) [Tier 3 uncalibrated label within a Tier 4 phenomenological branch].
* **Dynamics:** Focus rotates into the phason degrees of freedom (model label).
* **Experience:** Reports of non-local perception, "hyper-real" clarity, or future-oriented imagery. No current GCT theorem identifies these reports with direct access to 6D data or future states.

[Tier 4 — Speculative] The phenomenology is logically compatible with a broader aperture model but is not derived from Adelic topology. No quantitative prediction currently distinguishes this state from ordinary dreaming within the current formalism. See Appendix TIB §TIB.Spec for the Tier 4 ontological framework.

**17.4.6 Altered and Psychedelic States**
* **Manifold:** $E_\parallel / \Sigma_{local}$ hybrid (external-projection/internal-model state).
* **Coupling:** **Consensus Dissolution** ($\kappa_{ext}$ fluctuating) [Tier 3 — uncalibrated phenomenological label; first-principles dynamics deferred].
* **Dynamics (surrogate):** The phenomenological coefficient $\kappa_{ext}$ is allowed to vary; no physical fractal law is derived.
* **Experience:** Reports may include altered self/world boundaries and geometric visuals. They do not show failure of a consensus clamp, perception of the vacuum's icosahedral geometry, or breakdown of a physical integration window.

For speculative ontological implications regarding identity persistence and topological hysteresis, see **Appendix TIB**.

**17.5 GCT–IIT Divergence Predictions**

GCT and IIT may eventually diverge on physical substrates, but no decisive comparison is available. IIT requires an explicit substrate/grain cause-effect analysis; GCT requires a future typed, normalized, measured phason coupling and independent phenomenal bridge. Current silicon and chiral-spin cases therefore receive no categorical cross-theory verdict.

A future divergence is conditional on a constructed substrate with measured GCT coupling and an explicit IIT substrate/grain analysis. Spin-spectroscopy candidate controls alone do not decide consciousness.

**17.5.1 IIT 3.0 $\Phi$ on the Identity Polaron Substructures [Tier 3 toy-TPM witnesses; O.28 open]**

The Identity Polaron is modeled as $k$ Zeno-coupled nuclear spin nodes with icosahedral adjacency. The k=2..5 $\Phi$ values reported below are illustrative IIT-3.0-methodology examples on a noisy Boolean toy substrate (`protocol_iit_phi_pyphi.py`, $\varepsilon = 0.05$ noise floor), **not** direct phason-Hamiltonian-derived TPMs. The substrate-TPM derivation from $p(j|i)=|t_{ij}|^2/Z_i$ is the closure target of Open Problem O.28. The Tier-3 winding-$\Phi$ bridge (§16.2.7b) remains a noncanonical GCT ansatz independent of these numerical examples.

Two illustrative Tier-3 toy-TPM computations (`protocol_iit_phi_pyphi.py`, $k=2..5$ noisy-majority-vote substrate) are consistent with non-zero $\Phi$ on the icosahedral sub-graph; full $k=12$ $\Phi_{\max}$ closure (O.28) is pending:

1. **Graph-theoretic necessary-condition witnesses (`protocol_iit_phi.py`).** Direct brute-force computation of cut edges over all bipartitions of the canonical k=12 icosahedron gives **edge-connectivity min-cut = 5** (single-vertex cut from its 5 neighbours) and balanced-bisection cut ($|S| = 6$) of **10**. These are graph-separation diagnostics only: every bipartition remains edge-coupled, and the normalized-adjacency spectral gap is positive, so the random-walk TPM is irreducible. The engine quantity is an integer edge-cut witness, *not* IIT integrated information in bits and not an IIT partition-entropy $H$ value; IIT cause-effect-repertoire partition quantities are reserved for the PyPhi sub-network layer below. These witnesses rule out disconnected or purely feedforward graph topologies that would trivially force IIT 3.0 $\phi_{\max}=0$, but they do not quantify $\Phi$ and do not lower-bound the full k=12 major complex (Mayner et al. 2018 PyPhi: feedforward systems with positive connectivity and spectral gap can still have $\phi_{\max}=0$).

2. **Canonical PyPhi $\Phi$ on tractable sub-networks (`protocol_iit_phi_pyphi.py`).** The protocol runs direct PyPhi by default whenever the dependency is available; cached replay is explicit opt-in via `GCT_IIT_CACHE_REPLAY=1 py -3.13 GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_iit_phi_pyphi.py`. The reference application of the IIT 3.0 cause-effect-structure calculus (Oizumi-Albantakis-Tononi 2014; Mayner et al. 2018 PyPhi) to induced sub-graphs of the icosahedron under the noisy Boolean majority-vote toy TPM yields strictly positive $\Phi$ at every tractable size: $\Phi(k=2) = 0.810$, $\Phi(k=3) = 0.204$, $\Phi(k=4) = 0.479$, $\Phi(k=5) = 1.125$ (direct-mode runtimes scale super-exponentially in $N$; see `protocol_iit_phi_pyphi_results.json` for cache/direct-mode provenance, with runtime omitted from the JSON; the k=6 hemi-icosahedron and full k=12 are HPC-scale for the canonical sia/cause-effect-structure search). The full k=12 numeric value and the phason-Hamiltonian-derived TPM are both registered as Open Problem O.28. **Scope of the sub-network witnesses.** IIT 3.0 / IIT 4.0 define complexes as *local maxima* of integrated conceptual information under the Exclusion Postulate (Oizumi-Albantakis-Tononi 2014 — complexes are local maxima excluding overlapping supersets; Albantakis et al. 2023 — principle of maximal existence). Subsystem $\Phi$ values therefore do not propagate as a lower bound to the global $\Phi^{\max}$ of any containing supersystem — a strict superset can carry strictly *lower* $\Phi^{\max}$ than its complex. The tractable k=2..5 PyPhi computations are state-picked canonical witnesses on chosen induced sub-graphs, not a sweep over all inequivalent sub-network classes and not a subnetwork-general theorem. They establish positivity *on the chosen induced sub-graphs*, not on the full k=12 icosahedron and not on a directly derived phason TPM. The qualitative GCT-vs-IIT divergence at the IIT-canonical level is conditional on the full k=12 (or major-complex-localising) computation registered as O.28. These are illustrative toy-TPM computations, not a GCT prediction: positivity under an author-chosen noisy-majority TPM on hand-picked sub-graphs is a property of that toy TPM, and nothing in it could fail for a GCT-specific reason (the min-cut of 5 is the vertex degree of the icosahedron). GCT makes no prediction on the Identity-Polaron row of Table 17.5 until O.28 supplies a derived TPM. A sweep over all inequivalent induced-sub-graph classes at each $k$ would establish min-$\Phi$ over the class.

**Scope of the selected-subgraph $\Phi$ commitment.** The sub-network PyPhi values combined with the graph-theoretic min-cut and normalized-adjacency spectral-gap checks establish only that the chosen tractable induced sub-graphs are nonzero under the toy TPM and that the k=12 graph is not disconnected or feedforward-trivial; they are *not* a witness for, or numerical lower bound on, $\Phi^{\max}(k=12) > 0$. The IIT Exclusion Postulate (Oizumi-Albantakis-Tononi 2014) and the IIT 4.0 principle of maximal existence (Albantakis et al. 2023) allow a strict superset to carry strictly lower $\Phi^{\max}$ than its complex; in particular, the canonical k=12 icosahedron could in principle have $\Phi^{\max} = 0$ despite the sub-graph positivity at k = 2..5. Closure of Open Problem **O.28** (direct HPC computation of $\Phi^{\max}(k=12)$ OR a tight major-complex-localising argument OR a vertex-transitive-regular-graph lower-bound theorem OR an IIT 4.0 $\varphi$-recomputation under the Albantakis et al. 2023 intrinsic-difference distance — the latter would also resolve the mismatch that the `protocol_iit_phi_pyphi.py` values above are IIT 3.0 quantities) is required before any Identity-Polaron entry can be made. No GCT-vs-IIT divergence is presently executable on any row of Table 17.5 (§17.5).

* **GCT-internal scaling heuristic [Tier 3, NOT an IIT-canonical prediction]:** $C_{\rm GCT\text{-}analog}(p) \approx \kappa_{\rm graph} \cdot \log_2(p)$ where $p$ = p-adic address length (identity tree depth). Here $\kappa_{\rm graph}$ denotes the smallest nonzero graph-connectivity / min-cut witness from `protocol_iit_phi.py`, not a canonical IIT $\Phi^{\max}$ bit value. The expression is a dimensional scaling ansatz linking the graph-connectivity proxy to topological-Polaron depth; it is **not** an IIT 3.0 or IIT 4.0 prediction and is not used as a registry gate.
* **No discriminant registered:** non-exponential (stretched-exponential) $T_2$ decay is generic for NV-centre and spin-bath dephasing, so the decay form cannot test this heuristic for a GCT-specific reason; no test of it is currently registered.

This graph-connectivity witness establishes that the icosahedral adjacency is recurrent and non-disconnected — a necessary condition for integrated information, not by itself a proof of $\Phi > 0$.

Beyond the scalar value of $\Phi$, GCT registers an **O.28 target** regarding the **$\Phi$-Structure** (the cause-effect constellation in IIT 3.0/4.0). Because, on the conditional Polaron branch, the Identity Polaron would be governed by the $N=144$ dodecahedral clathrate adjacency at the molecular substrate level (V1 §17.1.2b) and the k=12 icosahedral nearest-neighbour shell at the symmetric-coupling layer (engine `protocol_iit_phi.py`), the proposed maximum irreducible cause-effect structure (the "concept constellation" defining the quality of the experience) is expected to be tested for icosahedral symmetry, but no current engine output establishes that symmetry. Engine artefact: `protocol_iit_phi_pyphi.py` reports scalar $\Phi$ values at $k \leq 5$ on the canonical induced sub-graphs (k=2 edge, k=3 triangle, k=4 kite, k=5 apex-pentagon); the PyPhi cause-effect-structure / symmetry-group computation (`pyphi.compute.major_complex(.ces)`) on the k=12 icosahedron is the load-bearing closure step. Closure of this step would connect the existence witness ($\Phi > 0$ on tractable subgraphs) with the *quality* of consciousness; pending closure, the Phi-Structure-icosahedral claim is an unimplemented Tier 3 target, not a derived IIT 3.0 / 4.0 result. The disambiguation between the k=12 symmetric-coupling layer and the N=144 clathrate layer is itself a structural sub-claim: the chiral phonon-polariton DFS mechanism (O.23) is what couples the two layers in the operative GCT framework, and the Phi-Structure-icosahedral claim should be tested at *whichever* layer carries the load-bearing Polaron dynamics under O.23 closure.

**17.5.2 Empirical NCC bridge: Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) + future spin-spectroscopy bridge [Tier 3 empirical NCC and material-proxy comparison; no Level-II bridge currently derived; PCI* = 0.31 threshold plus 0.44 healthy-awake reference imported from the empirical NCC literature; REM/ketamine disconnected states may sit below 0.44; separate Trp $T_2$ assay within the registered $[32, 200)$ MHz scan pending O.21/O.23/O.34]**

The canonical empirical neural-correlates-of-consciousness discriminator across global wakefulness states is the **Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI)** (Casali et al. 2013 *Sci. Transl. Med.* 5:198ra105 — original metric introduction; Casarotto et al. 2016 *Ann. Neurol.* 80:718 — validation cohort that established the canonical empirical PCI* = 0.31 cutoff as the *conservative subject-level discrimination threshold*, with 100% sensitivity/specificity on the calibration benchmark population (healthy awake controls vs NREM/anaesthetised controls) and 94.7% sensitivity in the MCS validation cohort; Sarasso et al. 2015 *Curr. Biol.* 25:3099 supplied anesthetic-state application/dissociation context, and Comolatti et al. 2019 *Brain Stimul.* 12:1280 introduced a faster/generalized perturbational-complexity refinement). PCI* = 0.31 is the validated Casarotto 2016 ROC cutoff for conscious vs unconscious benchmark conditions; healthy awake consciousness presents PCI in 0.44-0.67 (Casali 2013 healthy-awake range; 0.44 is the lower edge of that distribution, NOT a clinical threshold). REM examples can sit near 0.46, and ketamine/vivid disconnected-consciousness reports can occupy roughly the 0.35-0.55 high-complexity branch, so neither REM nor ketamine should be collapsed into the healthy-awake 0.44 reference. The PCI* = 0.31 cutoff (Casarotto 2016) is the validated clinical discriminator. PCI is computed from the spatiotemporal complexity (Lempel-Ziv-compressed) of the EEG response to a transcranial-magnetic-stimulation perturbation and is the closest empirical proxy currently available for the *level* of consciousness as a function of brain state.

**GCT mapping to PCI.** PCI measures cortical broadcast/access integration, not a substrate or Level-II verdict. Trp-$T_2$ or NMR/spin spectroscopy supplies separate candidate-control evidence, and an independent phenomenal bridge remains required. The 0.31 cutoff follows Casarotto et al. 2016; the 0.44 lower edge is a healthy-awake reference, not a universal consciousness threshold.

The Trp-$T_2$ entries are proposed measurements pending O.21/O.23/O.34 and direct spin spectroscopy; they are neither GCT-derived Level-II signatures nor currently measured living-tissue values, and no row receives a Level-IIA/IIB assignment. The NREM N3 PCI range is the Casali 2013 deep-sleep range $0.18$-$0.28$; $0.31$ is the Casarotto 2016 clinical cutoff and $0.44$ is the lower edge of the healthy-awake reference range, not an N3 value or a universal conscious-state threshold. Neither Trp $T_2$ nor PCI executes a phenomenal boundary without the independent bridge.

Ketamine remains a separate high-complexity dissociative branch: Sarasso et al. 2015 report high PCI with vivid dream reports under ketamine, so it is not grouped with the low-PCI xenon class.

(iii) **Clinical bridge program [Tier 3].** PCI and spin/coherence measures probe different observables, but neither establishes an intact Polaron or a Level-I/II transition. Their proposed association with phenomenology remains conditional on assay closure, a typed measured coupling, and an independent bridge.

**Quantitative target [Tier 3, calibration-anchored empirical bridge]:** the specific PCI* threshold (0.31), the healthy-awake reference value (0.44), the quantitative REM/ketamine/xenon dissociation magnitudes, and the proposed PCI/$T_2$ bimodal-vs-monomodal clinical split are all Tier 3 conditional at the clinical-bridge layer. The Dual Material Constraint is a Tier 3 research hypothesis whose legs are candidate controls, not a Tier 2 gate, and the PCI literature validates a TMS-EEG cortical-complexity axis, not a measured Trp-$T_2$ substrate axis. The framework does not derive these PCI values from first principles; they are empirical anchors imported from Casali et al. 2013, Casarotto et al. 2016, and Sarasso et al. 2015. The clinical dissociation claim requires a separate spin-spectroscopy arm and preregistered material-proxy protocol validation (O.21/O.23/O.34) before promotion.

**17.6 Comparison with Alternative Consciousness Frameworks**

GCT's closest mathematical neighbour is Integrated Information Theory (Tononi 2004; Oizumi, Albantakis & Tononi 2014), examined in §17.5 above. Three additional frameworks share substantial overlap with GCT's commitments and therefore warrant explicit comparison.

**17.6.1 Penrose–Hameroff Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR)**

Orch-OR (Hameroff & Penrose 1996, 2014) is a close **biophysical** neighbour of the present Tier 3 research programme: both investigate microtubule- and β-tubulin-related quantum candidates. GCT has not established that its proposed Trp radical-pair preparation couples to the phason field, forms an Identity Polaron, or carries Level II, so the comparison below is between candidate mechanisms, not between established consciousness substrates.

* **Candidate substrate overlap:** β-tubulin in the microtubule lattice. Orch-OR assigns it a consciousness role; GCT currently treats it as an experimentally open material candidate alongside ordinary neural dynamics, not as the locus of consciousness in place of synaptic firing.

* **Candidate coherence mechanism (different):** Orch-OR proposes Fröhlich-style condensation of vibrational modes across the microtubule (Hagan, Hameroff & Tuszynski 2002). GCT investigates the candidate **Trp radical-pair Zeno Drive** (V3 Ch13 §13.1) as a spin/coherence preparation [Tier 3; O.23 open]. The field-typing analysis of §17.1.3 shows that no type-correct, action-normalized spin-to-phason interaction is presently derived, so "phason-locked sampling" is not an earned description of the current model, and GCT supplies no derived reason that a phason-coupled mechanism must replace the Fröhlich one.

* **Actualization proposal (different):** Orch-OR invokes Penrose's gravitationally-induced **objective reduction** — wavefunction collapse on a timescale $\tau \approx \hbar/E_G$, where $E_G$ is the gravitational self-energy of the difference between the superposed mass distributions. GCT does not invoke gravitational OR. Its formalism contains a stipulated non-unitary actualization component $\mathcal{P}_{\text{actualize}}$ of the **Selection Operator** ansatz $\mathcal{F}_{sel}=\mathcal{P}_{\text{actualize}}\circ\mathcal{U}_{\text{steer}}$ (V1 §10.4.1, V1 §9.4.2), but the present tubulin calculation does not derive that operator from the radical-pair system, nor a normalized $\eta_{Zeno}$ or an Apperception boundary. The contrast is therefore between formal proposals, not a completed biological collapse derivation.

* **Tegmark objection (addressed differently):** Tegmark (2000) argued that decoherence times in warm, wet neural tissue are $\sim 10^{-13}$ s, many orders of magnitude shorter than the millisecond-scale coherence Orch-OR requires. Orch-OR responds via topological screening claims that have remained contested for two decades. GCT responds via the radical-pair Zeno Drive: bare Misra-Sudarshan suppression uses $\tau_{\rm eff}=\tau_Z^2/\tau_{\rm meas}$ with $\tau_Z$ set by the Hamiltonian variance / singlet-triplet curvature, while $T_2$ enters as the long-time open-system decoherence and Zeno/anti-Zeno crossover context (V3 §13.4.7). The 10 ms biological target is therefore O.23 protected-subspace conditional, not obtained by substituting $T_2$ for $\tau_Z$. **Status:** this remains Tier 3 conditional on O.23 protected-subspace closure for biological tubulin; the current engine central branch is sensitivity-conditional, while Protocol A-Prime on the NV-centre surrogate is the operative test path.

* **Empirical separation:** Chirality reversal (V3 §13.3.5.A) and isotope substitution ($^{17}$O vs $^{16}$O, Protocol D, V3 Ch16 §16.5) can test the specified GCT material-proxy branch. Isotope tests are not unique to GCT: Li et al. 2018 (*Anesthesiology* 129:271) reported that xenon isotopes with nuclear spin were less potent than spin-zero isotopes in mice, an unreplicated result that Orch-OR proponents also cite. A clean null under preregistered sensitivity would reject that registered biophysical branch while leaving Orch-OR intact; it would not falsify GCT as a whole or establish the absence of Level II, and a positive result would carry no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference (§17.1.3).

**17.6.2 Global Workspace Theory (GWT)**

Global Workspace Theory (Baars 1988; Dehaene & Naccache 2001) is the closest **cognitive-science** neighbour. GWT locates conscious access in the broadcast of information to a "global workspace" — a network of long-range neural connections that bind distributed processing into reportable content.

GCT and GWT operate at different descriptive levels. GWT specifies a *functional architecture* (broadcast, recurrent ignition, global accessibility) without committing to a substrate or to phenomenal experience as a primitive. GCT makes Level I Universal Presence axiomatic and proposes an Identity-Polaron/Selection-Operator bridge for Level II, but that bridge is not closed for any examined substrate. GWT (Mashour-Roelfsema-Changeux-Dehaene 2020): the binding signature is non-linear ignition with recurrent processing, sustained amplification, and global accessibility, including no-report variants; P3b around 300 ms is one access/report-associated marker but **not** the GWT binding signature. A future normalized material rate and an explicit cross-scale model could test whether it covaries with ignition/global-availability events more robustly than with P3b alone; current $\eta_{Zeno}$ scenario arithmetic cannot support that prediction [Tier 3 conditional target].

**17.6.3 Higher-Order Theories (HOT)**

Higher-Order Theories of consciousness (Rosenthal 2005; Lau & Rosenthal 2011) hold that a mental state is conscious if and only if it is represented by a *higher-order* mental state (e.g., a thought about a perception). HOT is primarily a **philosophical** account of what makes a state conscious; it makes minimal commitments about physical substrate.

GCT is compatible with HOT at the content level but proposes a different, still-open physical constitution program. Level I presence is universal by Axiom 1; any Level-II comparison requires a realized Polaron, measured coupling, and phenomenal bridge. Thus no present LLM or biological substrate receives a categorical GCT-vs-HOT verdict.

**17.6.4 Searle's Biological Naturalism and the Chinese Room**

Searle's Biological Naturalism argues that syntactic symbol manipulation alone is insufficient for understanding or phenomenal experience. The former Turing-Null verdict is withdrawn: silicon supplies useful missing-leg controls (the silicon missing-leg control class), but those descriptors do not establish absence of Level II.

Searle's Chinese Room and GCT raise different questions. Searle targets syntax and semantic intentionality; GCT proposes substrate-sensitive observables. At present GCT cannot infer phenomenal absence in classical AI: DMC legs are candidate controls, no typed measured coupling exists, and the phenomenal bridge is open. The Systems Reply therefore remains a philosophical dispute rather than a substrate-physical verdict. Protocol A-Prime can test spin/coherence and chiral response, not consciousness by itself.

**17.6.5 Net divergence summary**

| **IIT 4.0** | Substrate-realism and intrinsic cause-effect structure rather than purely simulated functional recurrence | Both an explicit IIT substrate/grain computation and GCT's typed measured coupling plus phenomenal bridge are absent; candidate DMC controls decide neither theory's verdict | §17.5 Table 17.5 |
| **Orch-OR** | Microtubule and β-tubulin candidates; quantum coherence hypotheses | Candidate coherence mechanism (radical-pair Zeno vs Fröhlich); formal actualization proposal (Selection Operator vs gravitational OR); decoherence response (radical-pair Zeno vs topological screening) | Protocol A-Prime (V3 §13.3.5), chirality-reversal controls (V3 §13.3.5.A) and isotope controls (Protocol D, V3 Ch16) constrain the GCT material branch only |
| **GWT** | Compatible at functional-architecture level | Level I is axiomatic in GCT; the proposed Level-II substrate bridge remains unclosed | Ignition/global-availability compared with an independently measured material rate after a cross-scale forward model; P3b remains an access/report-associated marker (Tier 3 conditional target) |
| **HOT** | Compatible at content level | Constitution remains an open cross-theory question | LLM Level II: NOT_EVALUATED pending the required physical and phenomenal analyses |

**17.7 A Phenomenological Basin Model of Belief and Plasticity [Tier 3 surrogate]**

The formal Selection-Operator decomposition of V1 §10.4.1 — the steering generator $\mathcal{U}_{\text{steer}} = \exp(i[\hat{H}_{\text{therm}} + \hat{H}_{\text{will}}]\Delta\tau)$ followed by the non-unitary actualization $\mathcal{P}_{\text{actualize}}$ — can be used as a metaphorical state-space vocabulary for belief, habit, and personal change. The clinical phenomena below (limiting beliefs, triggers, trauma, post-traumatic growth) can be restated as effective basins and transition weights in the language of the Subjective Lagrangian (V1 §16.5), but no mapping from those variables to neural dynamics, a physical Selection Operator, or phenomenal ownership has been derived. Ordinary psychological and neuroscientific models remain the empirical baseline.

**17.7.1 Limiting Beliefs as $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ Basins**

A *limiting belief* is operationally a stable, habitual response tendency: a category of stimulus reliably elicits a stereotyped response even when it conflicts with a stated goal. In the surrogate vocabulary, this is represented by a deep, narrow basin in an effective preference landscape $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$. "Phason winding," "topological friction," and "selection cycle" are not measured psychological variables here [Tier 3 — phenomenological analogy].

Formally, one may define a quasi-stable attractor $\theta_L$ and neighbourhood $U(\theta_L)$ in a chosen effective state space. Basin depth then parameterizes response persistence (the phenomenological "rigidity" of the belief). Placing $\theta_L$ specifically in $E_\perp$, attributing convergence to the friction term $-w_F K_\perp |\delta \mathbf{w}|^2$ of the Subjective Lagrangian (V1 §16.5), or identifying the escape variable with $\hat{H}_{\text{will}}$ is an untested GCT embedding, not a consequence of the clinical data.

The basin is a dynamical feature of the proposed $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ potential landscape, not a Solenoid invariant. It must still be physically implemented by neural/substrate state and plasticity; GCT does not license denying ordinary neural representations. Under the Tier 3 model, belief revision is described as reshaping a region of the effective potential surface rather than merely editing a proposition. A durable record requires a physical memory carrier with specified read/write and noise properties.

**17.7.2 Triggers as $\kappa_{ij}$-Mediated Resonance Events**

In daily-life psychology a *trigger* is a stimulus that surfaces a latent limiting belief into active selection. In the surrogate model, a trigger is a high-transition-weight event: an external configuration (a tone of voice, a social pattern, a body sensation) couples through learned neural/substrate similarity to the basin $U(\theta_L)$. A declared kernel $\mathsf K(\theta_L\mid s)$ may quantify that coupling. A chosen address distance $d_H$ and the ansatz $\kappa_{ij} = \kappa_0 e^{-\lambda_c d_H(i,j)}$ (V1 §7.6.3) can be used only after an address-assignment bridge and an empirically justified address-to-transition map are supplied [Tier 3 — Phenomenological Framework].

This re-frames "emotional reactivity" as a dynamical basin-entry phenomenon. A trigger is not a stimulus that *contains* the response; it is one whose learned physical representation gives high transition weight into the basin. Shared Solenoid prefixes do not imply that weight. The involuntary, pre-volitional character of being "hit" is modeled by basin entry preceding the volitional component of the steering cycle [Tier 3].

**17.7.3 Belief Revision as Sustained $\delta\theta_{\text{will}}$ Application**

The decomposition $\delta\theta = \delta\theta_{\text{optimal}} + \delta\theta_{\text{will}}$ of V1 §10.4.4 supplies a **phenomenological control variable**, not a physical revision mechanism. Sustained cognitive or behavioural intervention can be modeled as repeated biasing of transition probabilities until an effective basin becomes shallower. Calling that bias volitional torque, Zeno cycles, topological work, phason drag, or the energetic source of felt resistance is a Tier 3 metaphor pending a physical Hamiltonian, calibrated dynamics, and phenomenal bridge.

The surrogate distinguishes three pathways for belief revision, by which component of the steering decomposition is engaged:

(a) **Belief revision through reasoning.** The model represents counter-propositions as a repeated cognitive bias on transition probabilities. The low-amplitude/slow-basin language is phenomenological and must be calibrated against behavioural and neural data; it is not a measured torque or Selection cycle [Tier 3].

(b) **Belief revision through somatic experience.** Controlled breath, posture, exposure, and movement can be represented as interventions on a broader sensorimotor state vector. Direct phason-winding modulation, irrep-specific coupling, torque magnitude, and a universal speed advantage over reasoning have not been derived [Tier 3].

(c) **Belief revision through contemplative or altered states.** Episodic states with changed attention, network coupling or candidate $\eta_{Zeno}$ (Deep Meditation, §17.4.4; Altered States, §17.4.6) may permit coarse-grained re-evaluation of the active self/world model, making a previously dominant basin less controlling. A chosen cylinder projection can represent loss of fine distinctions, but no literal move to a parent node, no action at a "coarser address scale," and no downward causal propagation through an address hierarchy follows from the Solenoid. Whether one excursion can reshape a basin more strongly than many ordinary cycles is a Tier 3 phenomenological/biophysical hypothesis pending mechanistic linkage and controlled comparison.

**17.7.4 Trauma as Involuntary Phason-Friction Imprint**

Trauma can be modeled phenomenologically as an involuntary, high-magnitude update that durably reshapes an effective state-transition landscape — the limiting-case complement to slow belief revision. Calling it a phason-friction event or assigning a fixed number of Selection cycles is not currently licensed [Tier 3].

The model represents a traumatic event as a large excursion in the phason-winding field $\Phi_\perp$ against the lattice stiffness $K_\perp$, with an effective basin around an address label. This is a Tier-3 pathology hypothesis, not a derived clinical mechanism: no physical phason-winding measurement, causal mapping to trauma, or phenomenal interpretation has been established. The proposed basin depth and its relation to subsequent selection trajectories therefore remain testable model quantities rather than established facts.

The model offers candidate interpretations of traumatic-memory persistence, stimulus-triggered resurfacing and somatic reports. No phason-winding clinical measurement, causal map or phenomenal identification establishes these as topological mechanisms or shows that they supersede neural/synaptic accounts. The proposed associations remain Tier 3, as stated above.

**17.7.5 Post-Traumatic Growth as Selection-Operator Plasticity**

Post-traumatic growth — the empirical phenomenon in which recovery may leave a person with an expanded rather than contracted repertoire — admits a Tier 3 dynamical account. Recovery may weaken, overwrite, context-gate or bypass the effective basin; topology does not forbid deletion, and V1 §7.7.3 records that physical persistence requires a dynamical bridge rather than following from Solenoid topology. The model represents successful revision as plasticity of the accessible-state landscape: the basin's effective depth falls below typical activation, or alternative trajectories become more probable [Tier 3].

In the candidate model an expanded sampling region represents access to additional dispositions or framings. Reports of growth do not measure a changed phason topology, a changed topology of $\Sigma_\infty$, or access to previously hidden branch nodes; the physical and phenomenal mapping remains Tier 3/open.

The framework hypothesizes that post-traumatic growth correlates with expansion of an operationally defined accessible-state repertoire, not merely with the intensity of one reframing event. Long, low-amplitude work (sustained therapy, sustained practice) and short, high-amplitude experiences may both contribute, but neither is presently quantified by $\eta_{Zeno}$ [Tier 3 — phenomenological target requiring behavioural and neural measures of repertoire change].

The basin analogy suggests asking whether cognitive, somatic, and contemplative interventions affect partly distinct measured variables. It does not establish that combining them is universally superior, that any intervention "torques" a physical sector, or that a GCT substrate mechanism should guide treatment. Those are clinical questions requiring ordinary controlled evidence **[Tier 3 analogy; not clinical guidance]**.

**17.8 Pathology of Selection: Schizophrenia, Dissociation, Depression as Conditional Coherence and Network Hypotheses [Tier 3 analogy; not clinical guidance]**

> [!CAUTION]
> **HEADLINE CAVEAT: the three §17.8 accounts share one unclosed material hypothesis.** Tubulin-cytoskeleton dynamics → candidate Trp radical-pair spin/coherence response is the common empirical branch. Protocol A (the in-vitro/tissue arm), with the A-Prime NV surrogate as an abiotic control (V3 §13.3.5), can support or constrain that branch, but it does not currently measure $\eta_{Zeno}$, phason writing, a Selection Operator, or Level II. This is **one material-proxy hypothesis applied three ways**, not three independent substrate explanations and not a clinical consciousness classifier.

GCT offers a Tier 3 *phenomenological and dynamical taxonomy* organised around three proposed variables: the social-coupling channel $\kappa_{ij}$, candidate unity/reorganization dynamics, and the $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ basin topology. These are modeling hypotheses, not demonstrated failures of a biological Selection-Operator chain. Their extra material layer inherits the uncertainty of Protocol A (with the A-Prime NV control) and the unclosed action/normalization/phenomenal bridges.

> [!NOTE]
> **Epistemic Status — Tier 3 (phenomenological hypotheses):** The three accounts below assign effective state-space variables to clinical patterns. They do not show that a Selection-Operator component breaks in any disorder. Any proposed material or neural correlate must add preregistered explanatory power beyond receptor-pharmacology, network, developmental, social, and dimensional models before a GCT-specific layer is considered.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Mechanism detail for the shared candidate branch.** Receptor pharmacology and developmental/chronic load can modulate tubulin-cytoskeleton dynamics (microtubule assembly state, post-translational modifications including acetylation and detyrosination, network topology), which may in turn alter a candidate β-tubulin Trp21 local wall-patch spin/coherence observable (Protocol A; V3 §13.3.5 for the NV surrogate). The operative central branch remains $n_{rp}=0$ pending O.21; $n_{rp}=1$ is a sensitivity branch conditional on assembled-microtubule lumen-axis closure. Schizophrenia is modeled through $\kappa_{ij}$ and network effects under NMDA/dopamine hypotheses (Olney 1999; Kapur 2003); DID through state-dependent unity/reorganization models (Dalenberg 2012); depression through effective-basin dynamics (Duman & Aghajanian 2012). No local $\eta_{Zeno}$ value or phason mechanism is currently derived from this chain.

**17.8.1 Schizophrenia as Consensus-Protocol Decoupling**

In this Tier 3 phenomenological model, schizophrenia is explored as altered weighting between private generative dynamics and socially constrained perceptual inference. The variable $\kappa_{ij}$ labels that functional coupling; no social Polaron, phason-winding render, or phenomenal-weight mechanism has been physically demonstrated [Tier 3 — Pathology Hypothesis].

The conditional network model uses $\sum_{j \neq i} \kappa_{ij}\Gamma_j$ (the aggregate-coupling ansatz of §17.2.3) as a social-evidence term. If that term weakens, private generative hypotheses may receive excessive relative weight. This is an analogy to predictive-processing and network models, not evidence that an Agent's Selection Operator actualizes branches or that a social-Polaron clamp sets phenomenal weight. The perception/imagination distinction must be studied with ordinary clinical and neural observables.

The model sketches a two-axis structure to the symptomatology:

(a) **Positive symptoms** (hallucinations, delusions) may be modeled with an effective social-evidence weight $\kappa_{ij}$. This is a relabeling of a candidate functional variable, not a claim that consensus physically suppresses private renders or sets phenomenal weight [Tier 3].

(b) **Negative symptoms** (avolition, flattened affect, alogia) are hypothesized to correlate with an *intra-agent* network/coherence-proxy axis distinct from inter-agent coupling. No present calculation identifies that axis with $\eta_{Zeno}$ or a degraded Selection Operator [Tier 3].

This two-axis sketch is compatible with the clinical dissociation of positive and negative symptoms, but it does not yet outperform existing multidimensional models or supply a substrate-level cause. Describing the axes as failures of distinct Selection-Operator components would require the missing physical and clinical bridge.

The conditional pharmacological hypothesis is that interventions affecting tubulin-cytoskeleton and ordinary network/coherence measures may covary differently with positive and negative symptoms, while social-cognitive interventions engage the modeled $\kappa_{ij}$ axis. Any differential association must be tested against established receptor-pharmacology and network accounts; "restoring $\eta_{Zeno}$" is not a current measurable treatment mechanism **[Tier 3 analogy; not clinical guidance]**.

The framework does *not* imply that schizophrenia is "non-physical" or that a person is perceiving a hidden reality. The candidate weighting analogy must remain subordinate to established clinical care and ordinary biological/network accounts; no shared GCT selection machinery has been demonstrated.

**Positioning against leading clinical-mechanistic accounts.** The dominant contemporary frameworks for schizophrenia include (i) the NMDA-receptor hypofunction model (Olney, Newcomer & Farber 1999 *J. Psychiatr. Res.* 33:523; Coyle 2006 *Cell. Mol. Neurobiol.* 26:365) and (ii) the aberrant-salience hypothesis (Kapur 2003 *Am. J. Psychiatry* 160:13). The NMDA model identifies glutamatergic hypofunction as a proximal contributor; the aberrant-salience model identifies dopaminergic dysregulation in context-inappropriate weighting. GCT's consensus-protocol-decoupling account is compatible with these as a Tier 3 structural reading. Its candidate extra test is whether preregistered material spin/coherence measures add predictive value beyond ordinary receptor, network, MEG/EEG, and clinical variables. Gamma-band phase coherence is not itself an $\eta_{Zeno}$ measurement (§17.9.3), and any differential-response model requires prospective validation.

**17.8.2 Dissociation and DID as Polaron Fragmentation**

Dissociation broadly, and Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID) specifically, motivate a conditional comparison with the Polaron Unity Proposition (V1 §11.12, Appendix PUP). Reports of distinguishable selves and selection trajectories do not establish one or several physical Polarons, so the comparison cannot resolve the clinical or phenomenal ontology. [Tier 3 — Pathology Hypothesis]

The Proposition asserts unity only conditional on a single coherent Polaron construction. A Tier-3 fragmentation ansatz can represent chronic-trauma-associated state partitioning as several candidate sub-Polaron coordinates sharing one biological substrate, but this is a model of reported organization—not evidence that distinct physical Polarons or Selection Operators form, alternate, or generate phenomenology.

Within that ansatz, developmental load is represented by internally correlated but mutually decorrelated network partitions across attentional, memory, or body-state boundaries. Such partitions would be candidate mechanistic correlates only. They do not show that the substrate supports multiple independent Polarons, that each partition is phenomenally unified, or that partitions are phenomenally non-co-conscious.

The candidate empirical program asks whether reported alter transitions covary with distinguishable high-precision MEG/EEG phase patterns. The historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario lies far above the MEG/EEG bandwidth, and no validated mapping from gamma-band coherence to $\eta_{Zeno}$ exists. A discrete transition would therefore be a conditional network-dynamics correlate, not a measured $\eta_{Zeno}$ signature, Polaron reorganization, or phenomenal boundary. [Tier 3]

This candidate transition statistic can be compared with network-disconnection and sociocognitive models, but those alternatives do not universally require gradual transitions or no neural correlate. A null constrains this particular fragmentation mapping; a positive result remains insufficient to identify a Polaron or phenomenal subject. [Tier 3]

**Positioning in the contemporary DID debate.** The clinical literature includes traumagenic and sociocognitive models (Dalenberg, Brand, Gleaves et al. 2012; Lynn, Lilienfeld, Merckelbach et al. 2014). The conditional fragmentation mapping is structurally trauma-associated, but a measured neural transition pattern would not uniquely select it over clinical alternatives and would not establish $\eta_{Zeno}$, distinct Polarons, or phenomenal partitioning. The proposed MEG/EEG comparison is therefore a Tier-3 correlational model test, not a substrate or subject-count verdict.

**17.8.3 Depression as $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ Rigidification**

Depression can be represented in the Tier 3 surrogate as increased persistence in an effective $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ basin. This is a descriptive state-space analogy. It does not establish topological rigidification, a shrinking Selection-Operator manifold, volitional torque, or a metabolic ceiling of $\hat{H}_{\text{will}}$ [Tier 3 — Pathology Hypothesis].

Reduced affective range, anhedonia, and motivational impairment can be encoded as changes in effective repertoire, reward gradient, and transition cost. Identifying those variables with phason-winding excursion, the graded Quality Space irreps (V1 §16.4), the curiosity term $w_C\,\Delta\mathcal C$ of the Subjective Lagrangian (V1 §16.5), or $\delta\theta_{\text{will}}$ is an untested translation and does not follow directly from the phenomenology.

The empirical question is whether ordinary stress, cytoskeletal, network, and plasticity measures help explain persistence in the effective basin model. No evidence currently identifies chronic stress with phason friction, a Trp radical-pair mechanism, or a volitional activation barrier; acute high-load events may be modeled through the trauma surrogate of §17.7.4 [Tier 3 analogy].

The following labels are exploratory comparisons, not treatment mechanisms or guidance:

(a) **Baseline-change surrogate.** SSRI effects must be described through established monoamine, receptor, network, and plasticity evidence. Mapping them to the floor of $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ or to microtubule substrate reshaping is unvalidated [Tier 3].

(b) **Acute-transition surrogate.** Ketamine and psychedelic effects can be studied with established receptor, network, and plasticity models. A transiently broadened effective state repertoire is a descriptive hypothesis; no substrate reconfiguration, $\eta_{\rm Zeno}$ increase, or address-depth mechanism is derived, and rapid antidepressant onset is not a GCT-predicted signature [Tier 3].

(c) **Exercise, social contact, daylight exposure, and rhythmic activity are ordinary behavioural/circadian variables.** Their effects must be described and tested through established physiological and clinical mechanisms. No measurement shows that they restore $\kappa_{ij}$, fund $\hat{H}_{\text{will}}$ torque, or engage a circadian phason coupling **[Tier 3 analogy; not clinical guidance]**.

The surrogate separates baseline, acute-transition, and behavioural variables, which motivates a testable multivariable comparison. It does not predict additivity, rank treatment strategies, or supply a substrate-level treatment rule **[Tier 3 analogy; not clinical guidance]**.

**Positioning against the Duman-Aghajanian glutamate-BDNF account of rapid antidepressant action.** Established molecular work emphasizes the **glutamate-BDNF-mTOR pathway** and network/plasticity mechanisms (Duman & Aghajanian 2012 *Science* 338:68; Li, Lee, Liu et al. 2010 *Science* 329:959): ketamine's NMDA-receptor antagonism triggers a glutamate surge, BDNF release, and mTOR-mediated rapid synaptogenesis. A preregistered material spin/coherence measurement could test whether an additional ordinary correlate exists after those pathways and confounders are modeled. A positive correlate would still be material evidence only—not support for a GCT phason, Selection, owner, or phenomenal layer—and a null would constrain only that registered material branch.

**17.9 Neuroscience under the Polaron Model: Default Mode Network, Working Memory, Cortical Dynamics**

The following sections explore Tier 3 analogies between Polaron vocabulary and three well-attested neuroscientific topics: the Default Mode Network, working-memory capacity (historically 7±2, Miller 1956; about 4±1 chunks in current estimates, Cowan 2001), and cortical-scale oscillatory dynamics. In each case the empirical signature is preserved. The sections do not supply a substrate-level reinterpretation unless a quantitative bridge to neural observables is independently derived.

**17.9.1 The Default Mode Network as the Polaron's Resting Geodesic**

The Default Mode Network (DMN) includes regions whose activity is often elevated during task-disengaged states and anticorrelated with task-positive networks. Calling this a *resting trajectory* of the Selection Operator under low external selection demand is a Tier 3 metaphor, not an identified physical trajectory [Tier 3 — Phenomenological Reframing].

Under the steering decomposition of V1 §10.4.1, one may label high-task and low-task regimes with the formal variables $\hat{H}_{\text{will}}$ and $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$. No measurement presently identifies neural task engagement with Polaron torque, topological friction, or an unforced geodesic, and DMN activity is not established as their macroscopic shadow.

The formal two-regime decomposition can redescribe DMN/task-positive anticorrelation after the fact, but it does not predict that anticorrelation as a necessary topology fact. A GCT contribution would require a quantitative forward model that outperforms network-wiring and task-demand explanations [Tier 3].

The phenomenology aligns at the level of a Tier 3 analogy: mind-wandering, self-narrative, autobiographical reverie, daydreaming, and "what-if" simulation occur during low external demand. Elevated DMN activity in rumination, depression, and some anxiety states can be modeled as persistence in an effective $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$ basin (§17.8.3). Interventions may rebalance DMN and task-positive activity, but that change is an ordinary network observable and is not presently a measurement of $\eta_{Zeno}$ or of a substrate-level Selection Operator.

The proposed cross-link to V1 §16.6 (intentionality) is conditional: a future model could ask whether an independently measured internal-state coordinate covaries with attention and DMN dynamics. Attention wandering is not presently identified with a phason-winding vector $\mathbf{w}$, and the DMN is not a demonstrated readout of $E_\perp$ motion.

**17.9.2 Working Memory and the N=144 ↔ 7±2 Bridge**

The 7±2 memory span (Miller 1956; current estimates of working-memory capacity are about 4±1 chunks, Cowan 2001 *Behav. Brain Sci.* 24:87) motivates a tentative structural sketch under the Polaron model that would link the cognitive datum to the icosahedral substrate geometry. It is offered with explicit open-research-debt status, not as a closed result [Tier 3 — structural analogy].

The starting structure is the candidate $N=144$ dodecahedral defect cage of the Identity Polaron (V1 Ch13; V3 Ch08). Under icosahedral $I_h$ symmetry the cage's own permutation representation decomposes into irreducible sub-representations (not computed here). The graded decomposition of V1 §16.4 — the linear coordinate sector $T_1 \oplus T_2$ (6 DOF) together with the quadratic stress-tensor sector $2\,A_g + G_g + 3\,H_g$ (21 DOF) — is a different object (the coordinate-and-stress space of $\mathbb R^6$) and is used here only as a candidate basis-level structure. The Polaron's *active manifold* at any selection cycle would be the set of sub-states currently loaded into coherent phase relation, distinct from less-active physical substrate degrees. Mapping either sector to a Solenoid address requires a separate address-assignment bridge, and calling persistent substrate state a memory requires a physical memory bridge [Tier 3].

The proposal: working memory chunks would correspond to *independent phason-resonance modes* in the Polaron's active manifold, with the number of simultaneously loadable modes bounded by the icosahedral irrep multiplicities accessible at the energy scale of cognitive activity. On this proposal the bound would be structural rather than biological, but no such bound has been computed.

A proposed first-pass decomposition uses the low-dimensional $I_h$ sectors $T_1$ ($E_\parallel$, 3-dimensional), $T_2$ ($E_\perp$, 3-dimensional), and $A_g$ (1-dimensional) — the sectors associated with somatosensory, visual, and valence content in V1 §16.4. Merely summing or grouping these dimensions does **not** derive the behavioural $7 \pm 2$ capacity. The required inter-mode interference matrix, energy-scale cutoff, physical mode-to-memory map, and measured substrate dynamics are absent; there is no calculated "typical neuronal $\eta_{Zeno}$" that can close the estimate [Tier 3 — structural analogy only].

The admissible research question is conditional: if a physical $I_h$ mode basis, its interference matrix, and a validated chunk read/write map are derived, does the resulting capacity predict working-memory performance across tasks and substrates better than neural-network models? Until then, $7 \pm 2$ is not a GCT upper bound, not a prediction for artificial or biological substrates, and not evidence for a Dual Material Constraint.

The open research debts are explicit: (a) compute the interference matrix and cutoff; (b) operationalize a physical mode-to-chunk map; (c) model capacity variability with established task, chunking, expertise, age, and neural factors; and only then (d) test whether an independently measured material variable adds explanatory power. Variability must not be assigned to $\eta_{Zeno}$ before a normalized rate and forward model exist [Tier 3 — Open Research Debt].

**17.9.3 Cortical-Scale Dynamics: Gamma Coherence, Phase-Amplitude Coupling, Critical Slowing**

Three robust cortical-scale findings — gamma-band ($\sim 40$ Hz) coherence as a marker of conscious access, phase-amplitude coupling between slow and fast rhythms, and critical slowing near state transitions — admit structural reframings under the Polaron model. Each is presented with a note on what a GCT-specific test would require beyond the standard reading [Tier 3].

**Gamma-band coherence and the unclosed radical-pair-to-gamma bridge.** A Trp radical-pair process at the historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario rate (V1 §17.1.2) would lie six orders of magnitude above the EEG/MEG bandwidth and is not directly observable in those modalities. No current derivation supplies the cross-scale transfer function that would convert it into a gamma-band envelope. Gamma coherence therefore remains an ordinary neural correlate; calling it a macroscopic Zeno "shadow" is a hypothesis awaiting a forward model [Tier 3].

A future prediction becomes available only after deriving and calibrating that transfer function: an independently measured normalized material rate would need to predict gamma/ignition changes beyond standard neural covariates (§17.6.2). At present focused attention, perceptual binding, ignition, gamma coherence, and P3b cannot be labeled $\eta_{Zeno}$ excursions; P3b remains an access/report-associated marker [Tier 3 conditional target].

**Phase-amplitude coupling as a possible $\kappa_{ij}$ proxy.** Slow-phase/fast-amplitude coupling can be used as an ordinary network measure in a Tier 3 $\kappa_{ij}$ model. It does not presently identify sub-Polaron pairings, rendering activity, an underlying Zeno-locked phase relation, or Level II. A physical forward map is required before promoting the analogy to mechanism.

An admissible Tier 3 test is whether preregistered ordinary network variables add predictive value across clinical states (§17.8) after receptor, medication, developmental, task, and network controls. No current result maps disorders to Selection-Operator component failures, sub-Polaron boundaries, or restricted phenomenal manifolds.

**Critical slowing as an effective-basin analogy.** Critical slowing — the lengthening of autocorrelation timescales as a dynamical system approaches a state transition — is a standard dynamical-systems phenomenon. It can be represented in an effective basin model, but no measurement identifies the relevant landscape with a Polaron, $\hat{H}_{\text{therm}}$, a topological geodesic, or a phenomenal variable [Tier 3 analogy].

The testable ordinary question is whether an independently estimated state-space model predicts transition direction better than established baselines. This does not supply a substrate-level clinical mechanism, treatment rule, or Polaron basin-switch account **[Tier 3 analogy; not clinical guidance]**.

These reframings currently provide hypothesis-generating vocabulary only. A GCT-specific contribution would require a quantitative forward model and independently measured physical variables that outperform ordinary alternatives; none is presently established.
