## Part III Astrophysics

## **PART III: ASTROPHYSICAL TESTS**

### **Chapter 11: The 3.55 keV Anomaly (Dark Matter)**

The search for the particulate identity of Dark Matter remains the most significant unresolved endeavor in modern physics. For decades, the "Cold Dark Matter" paradigm has postulated a cold, collisionless component occupying galactic halos (Weakly Interacting Massive Particles, WIMPs, being one candidate). Geometric Consciousness Theory (GCT) instead models Dark Matter as the **Topological Glass** state of the vacuum substrate. The stress-gated lattice-fracture mechanism is Tier 3 (it rests on the Tier 3 Topological Glass model and is conditional on the adopted architecture), and the absolute centroid $E_{vac}=m_e/144\approx3.5486$ keV is Tier 3 because it inherits the O.38 $N_{\rm cage}=144$ posit. The empirical status is Under Test pending deeper XRISM observations (see §11.4.4 + App PSC §PSC.8 + App PRG P.3).

---

**11.1 The Signal**

**11.1.1 Observations: Perseus, Coma, and Andromeda**

Tier discipline before the empirical conflict: the stress-gated triboluminescence mechanism is Tier 3 (it rests on the Tier 3 glass model and is conditional on the adopted cage architecture); the absolute centroid inherits the Tier 3 O.38 cage posit, and the cluster-line identification plus $\sigma_{\rm crit}$ bracket are Tier 3 empirical postdictions pending the XRISM/stacked-cluster tests.

In 2014, an unidentified emission line was detected in the X-ray spectra of several massive galaxy clusters and the Andromeda galaxy (M31). Initially reported by Bulbul et al. (using stacked XMM-Newton data) and independently confirmed by Boyarsky et al., the signal was subsequently probed by Chandra, Suzaku, and the Hitomi satellite — the Hitomi observation of Perseus reported a high-significance non-detection of the anomalously bright Perseus-core flux (Hitomi Collaboration 2017 *ApJL* 837:L15, DOI 10.3847/2041-8213/aa61fa, 99.7% tension on a narrow-line interpretation in Perseus), creating a live observational tension. Protocol C reserves its falsification aperture for stacked above-$\sigma_{\rm crit}$ cluster regions (§15.1.3); whether the Perseus core is rheologically below threshold is a declared open programme (§11.1.4), so the Hitomi null is not counted as support for the stress gate.

Unlike known atomic transitions, the reported flux pattern is not explained by baryonic gas parameters alone. In GCT the candidate signal intensity is treated as stress-gated rather than as tracking the density profile (§11.4.6). GCT proposes [Tier 3] this line as a candidate direct observation of the vacuum microstructure.

**11.1.2 Energy: 3.55 ± 0.03 keV**

The commonly quoted centroid is the weighted mean of the Perseus cluster core, the stacked cluster sample, and the Galactic Center:
$$E_{obs} \approx 3.55 \pm 0.03 \text{ keV}$$
This centroid is not consistent with GCT's own stress gate. Two of its three inputs come from regions the gate does not count as emitting: the Perseus core lies outside the Protocol C pressure aperture (and its rheology is open, §11.1.4), and the Galactic Center lies in the Milky-Way environment that the stress-gating account treats as low-shear (a treatment not yet computed, §11.1.4). A centroid built only from above-$\sigma_{crit}$ apertures has not been computed, because the per-region centroids are not tabulated here. The 3.55 keV figure is therefore quoted as context only; it is never counted as a pass for GCT.
Sterile-neutrino decay fits of this line are in tension with the non-detections in specific environments (§11.1.3–§11.1.4); this is a constraint on that model, not an impossibility.

**11.1.3 The Draco Paradox and the Threshold of Critical Stress**

A critical anomaly within the data is the **Draco Null Result**. High-exposure observations of the Draco Dwarf Spheroidal galaxy failed to detect the 3.55 keV line despite its high dark matter density. GCT offers a postdictive account via the **Threshold of Critical Shear Stress ($\sigma_{crit}$)**. 

We define the qualitative fracture condition from icosahedral tiling mechanics; the numerical Vacuum Yield Strength ($\sigma_{crit}$) remains a calibrated cluster-scale stress bracket until the phason-stiffness normalization is derived in absolute pressure units.

> **Proposal: Yield Strain from Tiling Flip Condition [Tier 3]**
> 
> In the AKN icosahedral tiling, a phason flip — a discrete rearrangement of tiles that releases stored strain — occurs when the perpendicular-space displacement $u_\perp$ of a tile vertex exceeds the width of the acceptance window in that direction. The proposal takes the characteristic half-width to be the short diagonal of a rhombic acceptance cell, scaling as $\phi^{-1} \times a_\perp$ (where $a_\perp$ is the perpendicular lattice constant). This is an input, not a derived quantity: the AKN acceptance window is a rhombic triacontahedron, and a "short diagonal of the rhombic acceptance cell" is not yet given a geometric definition as a half-width of that window. The strain at which this flip occurs is then:
> 
> $$ \epsilon_y = \frac{\Delta u_\perp}{\xi_{\rm DS}} = \frac{\phi^{-1} \cdot a_\perp}{\phi^4 \cdot a_\perp} = \phi^{-5} \approx 0.0902 $$
> 
> where $\xi_{\rm DS} = \phi^4 \cdot a_\perp$ is the dark-sector phason coherence scale, distinct in symbol, definition, and magnitude from the biological polaron healing length $\xi_{\rm pol}=a_0/\alpha\approx7.25$ nm of V1 Ch07, and the factor arises from the four-generation Fibonacci inflation of the lattice scale [Tier 3].
> 
> Numerically: $\epsilon_y = \phi^{-5} \approx 0.090$ [Tier 3 — conditional on two Tier 3 inputs: the coherence scale $\xi_{\rm DS}=\phi^4a_\perp$ and the acceptance-window half-width $\phi^{-1}a_\perp$]
>

$$ \sigma_{crit} = K_\perp \times \epsilon_y = K_\perp \times \phi^{-5} $$

The Draco stress-gating prediction has no continuous fit parameter in the qualitative fracture morphology: $\epsilon_y$ is fixed by the Tier 3 tiling-flip proposal and $K_\perp$ is inherited from the phason-stiffness hierarchy. * **XRISM stacked clusters:** The registered Protocol C stress-aperture rule is the **mass-weighted stress-gated region above $\sigma_{crit}$** within the XRISM stacked-cluster sample: cluster outskirts, merger shocks, and high-shear ICM cells. The Perseus core falls below the frozen pressure cut and is **not** a falsification aperture. The comparison is not yet defined quantitatively: $\sigma_{crit}$ is set in ICM thermal-pressure units (§11.1.4), and a gas-poor dSph has no such pressure, so a stress proxy usable in gas-poor systems must be specified before this is a computed check. 
This stress-gating mechanism is offered as a postdictive account of the non-detection in dwarf spheroidal galaxies; it remains postdiction-status until the cluster-by-cluster pressure/shear map is frozen before line-residual inspection (§11.1.4).

**11.2 The Mechanism: Vacuum Triboluminescence**

**11.2.1 Dark Matter as Supersolid Topological Glass**

In the GCT hardware, the galactic halo consists of **Frozen Phason Strain** ($w_{ij}$) in the internal dimensions ($E_\perp$). It is a **Topological Glass**—a solid state where icosahedral tiles are pinned in high-energy orientations. Critically, because the vacuum is a **Supersolid**, it possesses **Off-Diagonal Long-Range Order** (global phase coherence). This phase-locking ensures that the "Unit of Strain" is identical across the entire universe, preventing the spectral smearing common to classical glasses.

**11.2.2 The Vorton and the Quantized Snap**

We define the fundamental excitation of the glass as a **Vorton**: a closed loop of phason strain pinned to the matching rules of the icosahedral tiling. In the conditional lattice-fracture model, stress above $\sigma_{crit}$ drives **Vacuum Creep** and releases one modeled binding-energy unit. The mechanism form is Tier 3 (conditional on the adopted architecture and the glass model); the numerical **Vacuum Quantum**, $E_{vac}=3.5486$ keV, is Tier 3 because it uses the O.38 $N_{\rm cage}=144$ input.

**11.2.3 Global Phase Rigidity and Mössbauer Suppression (open)**

**Declared open programme [Tier 3]: emitter kinematics and line width.** The model claimed that the 3.55 keV line is exceptionally narrow: emitters bound in a coherent supersolid lattice would hand the recoil to the coherence volume set by $\xi_{\rm DS}=\phi^4a_\perp$ (§11.1.3), a **Mössbauer Suppression** of Doppler broadening, with **Global Phase Rigidity** keeping the emission monochromatic. The defect: emission occurs only in the fractured phase, where V2 Ch13 §13.1.2 describes the emitters as unpinned debris moving freely. Free emitters at cluster virial speeds ($\sigma_v\sim1000$–$1300$ km/s) give a Doppler FWHM of $\sim28$–$36$ eV, inside the $W_{int}>20$ eV band that Protocol C treats as falsifying. Closure needs an explicit fractured-phase emitter model (lattice-bound with a derived recoil-free fraction, or free debris with a derived velocity distribution) and the $W_{int}$ it implies. Until then the narrow-line expectation is unsupported, and nothing downstream uses it as support.

**11.3 Experimental Match: The Binding Energy $E_{vac}$**

**11.3.1 Postdiction: Lattice Release Centroid [Tier 3 conditional mechanics; Tier 3 O.38-dependent centroid]**

The most direct postdiction-status alignment is between the unidentified X-ray line at 3.55 keV and the conditional **Vacuum Binding Energy ($E_{vac}$)** evaluated from the Chapter 7 cage posit. This is context for Protocol C, not validation or an independent derivation of $N_{\rm cage}$.

Conditional on the Tier 3 $N=144$ electron-cage posit, the arithmetic gives $E_{vac} = m_e / 144 \approx 3.5486$ keV. We *then* compare this Tier 3 postdiction to the observed X-ray line ($3.55 \pm 0.03$ keV). The result is a centroid coincidence within a crowded-line forest, reported as context only because the quoted centroid draws on regions the stress gate does not count as emitting (§11.1.2); its statistical significance is bounded by line-blending systematics rather than functioning as a clean confirmation of the lattice geometry.

**11.4 Falsification and Predictions**

**11.4.1 Line Shape, Morphology, and Background Model**

The operative test for GCT lies in the joint **line profile, morphology, flux, and background model** of the emission.
* **Sterile Neutrino Model:** The decay line is intrinsically narrow; the observed profile is set by cluster-virial broadening, instrument response, stacking, morphology, and background/atomic-line modelling. A $\sim 36$ eV FWHM scale is a cluster-environment diagnostic, not a standalone particle-DM theorem.
* **GCT Model:** A narrow **Lorentzian** intrinsic profile ($\Gamma \ll 1$ eV) holds only for lattice-bound emitters, which is the open emitter-kinematics programme of §11.2.3; the profile is convolved with the same instrumental response and foreground/background model, with morphology and flux consistency carrying equal decision weight.

**11.4.2 Dark Matter Evaporation [Tier 3; not observable]**

If fracture converts strain energy into photons, stressed regions slowly lose effective dark mass (**Dark Matter Evaporation**). If the 3.55 keV luminosity is the energy channel, the fractional mass-loss rate equals the line decay rate, $\Gamma \approx 2\times10^{-28}$ s⁻¹ (Bulbul normalisation, §11.1.4). Over 10 Gyr ($3.2\times10^{17}$ s) this gives $\Gamma t \approx 6\times10^{-11}$, roughly eight orders of magnitude below percent-level lensing or dynamical mass measurements. The effect is therefore not an observable test and is not used as one.

**11.4.3 XRISM Protocol C**

The **XRISM** Resolve microcalorimeter provides $\sim$5 eV resolution. Protocol C (Chapter 15) defines the preregistered decision framework for the XRISM line-shape audit. The operative verdict is not a standalone Lorentzian-vs-Gaussian split; it is the joint profile, flux, morphology, background-line, and cluster-virial-broadening comparison at the sensitivity required to resolve the signal.

**11.4.4 XRISM Early-Data Status**

XRISM has stacked **3.75 Megaseconds** of early science data across ten galaxy clusters. Key results:

* **Non-detection:** XRISM's early data did **not** resolve the 3.55 keV line.
* **Upper Limit:** The 3σ upper limit on the photon decay rate is $\Gamma \lesssim 1.0 \times 10^{-27}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$.
* **Sensitivity Gap:** This upper limit is **5 times weaker** than the decay rate implied by the original Bulbul et al. XMM-Newton detection. XRISM's early data has therefore **not yet reached the sensitivity required** to confirm or rule out the signal.
* **Physical Conclusion:** The early XRISM data is **physically inconclusive**. It is consistent with both the GCT stress-gated branch and the standard sterile neutrino model. The null result does **not** reject the registered Protocol C branch; that branch requires photon statistics beyond the current 3.75 Ms stacking depth.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **GCT Stress-Gated Branch Under Test.** The current XRISM non-detection is sensitivity-limited and does not adjudicate the frozen above-$\sigma_{crit}$ aperture. A definitive terminal no-line verdict requires the Bulbul-level Protocol C floor $\Gamma \lesssim 2.0 \times 10^{-28}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ in the mass-weighted stress-gated regions of the stacked XRISM cluster sample; the 26 Ms / $\Gamma\lesssim3.8\times10^{-28}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ stack is the morphology-linewidth milestone. The Perseus core alone lies outside the frozen pressure aperture and is not a Protocol C falsification point (its rheology is open, §11.1.4).

**11.4.5 HBT Photon Bunching [Tier 3 theoretical target; detector-level prediction open]**

The proposed lattice-fracture cascade motivates a second-order photon-correlation target for the 3.55 keV signal. A detector-level prediction requires the source mode count, cascade multiplicity, line profile, and timing response to be specified together.

> **Physical Argument:**
> The single-mode reference values are distinct: a thermal or chaotic field gives $g^{(2)}(0)=2$, a coherent field gives $1$, and an ideal single-photon emitter gives $0$ (Mandel & Wolf 1961, *Phys. Rev.* 124:1696). A large ensemble of independent emitters with random phases is a chaotic source and therefore exhibits the Hanbury-Brown-Twiss bunching limit in a resolved mode; independence does not by itself imply coherent-state Poisson statistics.
>
> The GCT mechanism proposes that a Vorton collapse triggers adjacent bond snaps within a phason-relaxation window $\tau_{relax}\sim10^{-23}$ s [Tier 3]. If that cascade produces correlated photon clusters, the relevant observable is the excess detector-integrated correlation above the null-source expectation. For $M$ independently detected spatio-temporal modes, chaotic bunching is diluted according to
> $$g^{(2)}_{\rm meas}(0)-1\sim\frac{g^{(2)}_{\rm single}(0)-1}{M},$$
> so both the particle-decay null and the cascade hypothesis approach unity under strong mode averaging. The discriminant is the difference between their finite-$M$ correlation functions, not the isolated single-mode value $g^{(2)}(0)=2$.

This prediction has the following properties:
* **Discriminant and its conditions:** A sharp threshold requires a source model for both hypotheses, including cascade multiplicity, emission-time statistics, spatio-temporal mode structure, astrophysical thermal components, and the detector response. These ingredients determine $g^{(2)}_{\rm meas}(\tau)$ and its shot-noise floor. The test remains a theoretical target until that forward model exists.
* **Instrument requirements:** The registered cascade window is $\tau_{relax}\sim10^{-23}$ s [Tier 3]. For a detector resolution $\tau_{res}\gg\tau_{relax}$, an unresolved correlation is diluted by approximately $\tau_{relax}/\tau_{res}$. XRISM Resolve samples pulse shapes at $80\,\mu$s and assigns arrival times with approximately $5\,\mu$s interpolation precision (XRISM HEASARC *Resolve* instrument specification), so even the more favorable interpolation scale gives a contrast no larger than order $10^{-18}$. A hypothetical $1$ ps coincidence system would still be $10^{11}$ times coarser than the proposed cascade window.
 > **Instrument scope:** The zero-delay test is not executable with present or foreseeable direct X-ray timing. A viable reformulation would require either a cascade mechanism with a substantially longer correlation time or a spectral-domain intensity-interferometry observable integrated against the line profile. Deriving one of those routes is the closure target.
* **Independent of line shape:** Even if the line-profile/morphology/background audit remains inconclusive due to source confusion, the bunching test would provide an orthogonal axis once a forward model exists; at present it defines no falsifier (see Status).
* **Status:** XRISM does not test this correlation target. The current proposal is non-executable and does not yet define an observational falsifier [Tier 3].

**11.4.6 The Spatial Cross-Correlation Mapping: Shear Gradient vs. Density Squared**

Standard annihilating dark matter models demand that the flux of a line signal follows the line-of-sight integral of the dark matter density squared ($\rho^2$), while decaying sterile-neutrino models follow the density $\rho$ itself.

GCT predicts a radically different spatial morphology. Because the 3.55 keV emission is **Vacuum Triboluminescence**—the discrete snapping of the topological glass under mechanical stress—the emission rate is governed by the local macroscopic strain. Qualitatively, the X-ray flux would then scale non-linearly with the local gradient of the cluster's gravitational shear stress tensor ($\nabla \sigma_{vir}$), maximizing in active merger shocks and regions of maximum orbital disruption, rather than seamlessly following the smooth $\rho^2$ core density profile. This gradient picture is motivation only; the single registered morphology template is the stress-gated aperture template frozen in Ch15 §15.2 (Ch15 §15.1.3 target cells).

This constitutes a **candidate falsifiable spatial mapping test** for XRISM and Athena follow-up: high-resolution spatial mapping of any confirmed 3.55 keV line should either follow a smooth density profile ($\rho$ for decay, $\rho^2$ for annihilation; either falsifies the GCT morphology at decisive sensitivity) or trace the registered stress-gated aperture template. Protocol C freezes the stress aperture numerically at $\sigma_{crit}=0.53\,{\rm keV\,cm^{-3}}=\sqrt{(0.07)(4.0)}\,{\rm keV\,cm^{-3}}$, using the Perseus-core / Bullet-shock pressure bracket; the target cells are listed in Ch15 §15.1.3 and the morphology power rule in Ch15 §15.2. Current Hitomi/XRISM coverage is insufficient for the stress-gated null; the test becomes definitive only after the XRISM cluster-survey aperture is above this frozen threshold, reaches the Ch15 sensitivity floor, and is followed up with Athena-class spatial/spectral mapping.

**11.4.7 High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Cross-Correlation [Tier 4, non-operative]**

A proposed auxiliary discriminator between decaying particle dark matter (like sterile neutrinos) and GCT's Vacuum Triboluminescence is a **High-Frequency Gravitational Wave (HFGW) Cross-Correlation**.

In this Tier 4 picture, when the topological glass fractures and releases the 3.55 keV Vorton energy, the event would also propagate acoustic phonons through the $\mathbb{Z}^6$ vacuum lattice, which in the 3D projection ($E_\parallel$) might appear as a burst of High-Frequency Gravitational Waves. The 1-100 MHz band is asserted, not derived: no frequency band, strain amplitude or rate has been computed.

Therefore, a 3.55 keV XRISM X-ray line accompanied by a temporally and spatially matched 1-100 MHz HFGW burst would support the mechanical-fracture interpretation as an auxiliary discriminator. A decaying sterile neutrino would emit a 3.55 keV X-ray photon without the correlated gravitational shockwave. HFGW co-detection is not part of the operative P.3 linewidth/morphology gate and cannot by itself validate the geometric-vacuum interpretation; it is a Tier 4/currently non-operative cross-channel check.

**11.4.8 Weak Lensing Shear Discontinuity: Dark Matter Fracture Morphology Target [Tier 3 morphology hypothesis; mechanism open]**

GCT proposes a morphology hypothesis for dark matter in merging galaxy clusters: a topological-glass fracture boundary might produce a weak-lensing feature co-spatial with the stress-gated 3.55 keV emission region. This is a diagnostic target pending both a derivation and an executable lensing-map pipeline, not a closed prediction; the dark-matter-fracture protocol is open.

**Physical Argument.** In GCT, dark matter is modelled [Tier 3] as the **Topological Glass** of the vacuum supersolid (§11.2.1). The ansatz assumes a **first-order fracture transition** when the applied stress exceeds the yield strength $\sigma_{crit} = K_\perp \times \phi^{-5}$ (§11.1.3, itself Tier 3): on one side the glass is intact (elastic regime, no emission); on the other it is fractured (post-yield regime, emitting 3.55 keV). A sharp, coherently propagating boundary is assumed, not derived.

**The Observable: Weak Lensing Convergence.** The weak lensing convergence map $\kappa(\vec{\theta})$ encodes the projected surface mass density $\Sigma(\vec{\theta})$ via $\kappa = \Sigma / \Sigma_{cr}$. The missing step is the fracture → $\Sigma$ map: fracture releases ~keV photons, not mass, and no derivation shows that a vacuum phase change alters the projected surface density at all. The form of any feature is also not derived: even a 3-D density step at $r_f$ projects to $\Sigma(R)$ with a term $\propto\sqrt{r_f^2-R^2}$, whose radial derivative diverges at $R=r_f$, rather than a finite step in $\partial^2\kappa/\partial r^2$.

**Morphology hypothesis [Tier 3; open]:**
> At the fracture boundary of merging galaxy clusters (e.g., El Gordo, ACT-CL J0102-4915; the Bullet Cluster, 1E 0657-56), the weak lensing convergence map would show a sharp feature at the boundary of the shear fracture zone, and its position would coincide with the boundary of the 3.55 keV X-ray emission region.
>
> Collisionless particulate dark matter (NFW, or any smooth halo profile) does not naturally produce this sharp phase-transition feature. NFW profiles are smooth away from the central cusp at $r=0$; their convergence maps have no kinks at finite radius. A detected sharp feature in $\kappa$ co-spatial with the 3.55 keV emission boundary would support a fracture-boundary interpretation and challenge smooth-halo fits under a registered lensing-map pipeline.

**This is a diagnostic morphology target pending executable lensing-map implementation:**
- The position of the feature would be controlled by $\sigma_{crit} = K_\perp \phi^{-5}$, with $\epsilon_y=\phi^{-5}$ from the Tier 3 AKN tiling-flip proposal and the operative cluster-scale normalization of $K_\perp$ / pressure units calibrated by the bracket $0.07 < \sigma_{crit} < 3$–$5$ keV/cm$^3$ in §11.1.4. The existence and morphology of the feature are a Tier 3 hypothesis; the specific cluster-fracture threshold location is Tier 3 calibrated pending XRISM cluster-subclass closure.
- The *existence* of the feature would depend on whether dark matter is a glass (sharp fracture: GCT) or a collisionless gas (smooth: particle DM), and on the underived fracture → $\Sigma$ map above.
- No continuous fit is added to the qualitative discontinuity claim. The numerical boundary location inherits the Tier 3 $\sigma_{crit}$ bracket, and a decisive inference requires a registered lensing-map pipeline with shear calibration, smoothing-kernel, and line-of-sight projection systematics before any binary confirmation/falsification language is operative.

**Instrument Specification:** Current weak lensing data from the Hubble Space Telescope (ACS, WFC3) and Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) for El Gordo and the Bullet Cluster have point-spread functions of $\sim 0.05''$, but the effective resolution of a weak-lensing $\kappa$ map is set by the background-source density (mean spacing $\sim6''$ at $100$ galaxies arcmin$^{-2}$), and such maps are usually smoothed to tens of arcseconds. Rubin/LSST and Euclid provide the statistical power to search for this feature across large merging cluster samples. Deep lensing maps with $> 100$ background source galaxies per arcmin$^2$ would be needed to search for such a feature under a registered pipeline; no detection threshold has been computed.

### **Chapter 12: Dynamic Dark Energy (DESI)**

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier-Disciplined Epistemic Status:**
> - **Equation of State ($w < -1$): stipulated channel-shape template; the phantom direction is Tier 4 as a physical claim.** The written phason action cannot produce $w<-1$ without a ghost, and no ghost-free construction is derived (§12.3.2; V2 Ch14 §14.3.1). **13.1.2b The Registered A-Prime Frequency Window: Magnon-Polaron Avoided Crossing [Tier 1 two-branch model mathematics / Tier 3 realization and value]**

The bare radical-pair variance used by the engine is a declared placeholder, $\Delta_{ST}/h \approx 30$ MHz: it is the plain rms of the three FAD$^{\bullet-}$ couplings listed below ($\sqrt{(42^2+28^2+12^2)/3}\approx30.0$ MHz), not a Trp measurement. It lies within about 10% of the TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ effective hyperfine coupling ($\approx27$ MHz; see "The Trp Hyperfine Anchor" below), and the inverse-Zeno conclusion of §13.4.3 holds for any value from 10 to 40 MHz [Tier 3 imported input]. Protocol A-Prime scans the full half-open interval $[32,200)$ MHz; the post-O.12 protected-subspace scenario windows—primary $112 \pm 10$ MHz if O.12 closes positive and fallback $42 \pm 10$ MHz if O.12 closes negative—are pre-registered hypothesis regions inside that scan. The $150$ MHz point is a sign-unfixed O.23/O.24 mechanism diagnostic outside F1 and the Holm primary family.

**The Magnon-Polaron Avoided Crossing.**
The microtubule is modelled here as supporting candidate **chiral acoustic phonon** modes (dispersion $\omega_{ph}(k) = v_{ph}\,k$, with $v_{ph} \approx 800$ m/s [Tier 3 — unsourced placeholder for a transverse/chiral acoustic mode of the tubulin heterodimer lattice (α/β-tubulin dimer per RCSB 1JFF/6DPU). The thin-bar speed $\sqrt{E/\rho} \sim 850$–$1200$ m/s from a Young's modulus $\sim 1$–$2$ GPa and density $\sim 1.4$ g/cm³ is a longitudinal-type scale; transverse modes scale as $\sqrt{G/\rho}$ with a much smaller shear modulus, and viscous overdamping of MHz microtubule modes in water is not addressed]) and candidate **spin-wave magnon** modes from the Trp radical-pair network (dispersion $\omega_m(k) = \Delta_{ST}/\hbar + Jk^2$, where $\Delta_{ST}$ is the singlet-triplet gap of the Trp radical pair and $J$ is a placeholder inter-radical exchange stiffness: spin-wave dispersion requires an inter-site exchange network, which hyperfine couplings do not supply and which is not specified for sparse, transient radical pairs). Standard two-branch hybridization can produce an avoided crossing, but the required microtubule modes and their coupling are unmeasured, and the former $\hat{H}_{CISS}$ phason bridge of §13.2.3 is an unadopted placeholder; the hybridization is a Tier 3 O.12/O.23 closure target, producing at most a candidate **magnon-polaron** quasi-particle rather than a demonstrated microtubule excitation. $v_{ph}$ enters the avoided-crossing sharpness ($k_c \approx \Delta_{ST}/(\hbar v_{ph})$ controls the crossing wavevector) but does **not** set the operating frequency itself — the operating frequency is set by $\Delta_{ST}/h$ in the Trp hyperfine band together with the Tier 3 O.12 frequency-scale renormalization, independent of $v_{ph}$. Within the supplied model the crossing scale is therefore insensitive to reasonable variation of $v_{ph}$; the model supplies a material-response hypothesis, not a robust 112 MHz prediction.

The **van Hove singularity** in the magnon-polaron joint density of states occurs at the avoided crossing where the phonon and magnon branches meet. Solving $v_{ph}\,k = \Delta_{ST}/\hbar + Jk^2$ in the small-$J$ regime gives $k_c \approx \Delta_{ST}/(\hbar v_{ph})$, and the avoided-crossing frequency on the lower branch is:
$$\nu_{vH} \approx \frac{\Delta_{ST}}{2\pi\hbar} = \frac{\Delta_{ST}}{h}$$

Within the supplied two-branch material model, the crossing scale is governed by the singlet-triplet gap of the Trp radical pair, not by the bare phonon zone-boundary frequency (which lies in the GHz range; the bare ZB formula $\nu = v_{ph}/(2\,\ell_{pitch})$ evaluates to $1.0 \times 10^{11}$ Hz $\approx 100$ GHz for the inserted tubulin parameters and is therefore unrelated to the registered MHz-scale scan windows). This is conditional dispersion algebra, not a measured tubulin mode or a GCT operating frequency.

**The Trp Hyperfine Anchor.**
The canonical radical-pair hyperfine literature (Ritz et al. 2000; Hore & Mouritsen 2016) tabulates the principal couplings for the **FAD$^{\bullet -}$ semiquinone** radical pair of the cryptochrome / avian-magnetoreceptor system at isoalloxazine positions $A_N(N5) \approx 42$ MHz, $A_N(N10) \approx 28$ MHz, $A_H(H5) \approx 12$ MHz, whose plain rms is $\approx 30.0$ MHz (the source of the engine's 30 MHz placeholder; App BEB §BEB.12 gives the singlet-state variance formula). **These FAD values are imported as a literature-anchored *order-of-magnitude reference band* for the singlet-triplet manifold splitting of indole-containing radical pairs at biological temperatures**; the *actual* β-tubulin Trp$^{\bullet +}$ indole hyperfine structure has only one nitrogen (N1) plus aromatic ring protons, so the per-coupling values for the Trp candidate residues (Trp21, Trp103, Trp346, Trp407 per PDB 1JFF/1TUB chain B numbering; Trp21 is only a local-inward wall-patch candidate until the assembled-MT lumen-axis screen of Open Problem O.21 is completed) are not the FAD values above. The Trp-side hyperfine assignment is registered as an open closure target. In the TrpH$^{\bullet +}$ radical the spin density places large isotropic couplings on the $\beta$-CH$_2$ protons as well as on N1 and the ring, so its effective hyperfine coupling is *larger* than FAD$^{\bullet -}$'s, not smaller: the DFT-based isotropic effective couplings of Wong, Benjamin & Hore (2023, *Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.* 25:975–982) are $0.97$ mT ($\approx 27$ MHz) for TrpH$^{\bullet +}$ against $0.70$ mT ($\approx 20$ MHz) for FAD$^{\bullet -}$ [Tier 1 conversion at $g_e\mu_B/h = 28.0$ MHz/mT of imported literature values]. The residual external factor that would move the Trp effective coupling to the registered $\nu_c \approx 112 \pm 10$ MHz window is therefore $\approx 4\times$ ($3.7$–$4.5\times$), and $\approx 6\times$ from the FAD value. The earlier "narrower $10$–$20$ MHz indole band" and the "$6$–$11\times$" factor are withdrawn: they rested on an inverted premise. The $\approx 4\times$ step is an external renormalization scenario for Open Problem O.12 and is not derived by an avoided-crossing identity.

Biophys.* 45:299), FAD/cryptochrome supplies the order-of-magnitude reference band $\sim 20$–$50$ MHz. Phys.* 294:385), which we denote separately and which controls the S↔T mixing rate at *non-zero* applied field. Throughout this manuscript, "$\Delta_{ST}$" without qualifier refers to $\Delta_{ST}^{hf}$.

A residual external factor $\approx 4\times$ ($3.7$–$4.5\times$) would move the TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ effective coupling ($\approx 27$ MHz) to the registered $\nu_c \approx 112 \pm 10$ MHz scan window. This is historical scenario bookkeeping under **Open Problem O.12**, not an enhancement mechanism shared with a valid 38.3 MHz coupling (the ~41$\times$ ratio of §13.1.2 is itself an external scenario input); a first-principles derivation of any such frequency-scale renormalization remains open.

**Units convention guard.** Branch-window frequencies in this chapter are cyclic frequencies (Hz/MHz), whereas Hamiltonian angular frequencies use $\omega=2\pi\nu$ in rad/s. **13.1.3 Historical Topological-Valve and Berry-Phase Hypothesis**

ATP hydrolysis supplies measured biochemical free energy ($0.52$ eV per molecule), whereas a radio-frequency probe does not acquire activation energy merely by repeated application: treating stacked radio-frequency quanta as an activation-energy source would be a dimensional category error. This conservation statement does not establish an Agent as a **Topological Valve**, a defect-energy budget, or any coupling from ATP to a GCT field.

A Berry phase can be calculated only after specifying a cyclic material Hamiltonian, eigenstate bundle, drive path, and coupling to a measured conformational coordinate. None is derived here for tubulin, ATP hydrolysis, or a chiral phonon-polariton mode. The former claim that a Continuous Zeno Drive imparts a Berry phase that breaks the inversion symmetry of local ATP hydrolysis and thereby steers metabolic power into neural firing, with "Intention" read as that geometric steering, is therefore a **Tier 4 narrative**: no physical mechanism is derived, and it is not evidence that intention steers ATP energy.

**13.3 Experimental Signatures and Tests**

**13.3.1 Historical Leakage-Signature Scenario: Coherent THz Emission**

This section preserves a **historical Tier 3 material-emission scenario** for auditability. In that scenario, the bulk of the Polaron's energy vents into the internal dimensions ($E_\perp$) upon unwinding, a phason-phonon coupling ($\Gamma$) returns a non-zero "slosh-back" into the physical manifold, and the termination of a selection event produces a **Super-Radiant Phase Decay**—a coherent, narrow-band electromagnetic burst. None of this currently follows from the action audit (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3): no normalized Polaron energy, phason-to-electromagnetic transfer coefficient, selection-event source or source amplitude has been derived. The proposed burst is therefore an external scenario target, not a present GCT prediction.

**The Effective Topological Field ($B_{topo}$):**
The historical construction represented the target frequency as the **Larmor-like precession** of nuclear spins in an **effective topological field ($B_{topo}$)**, read as the phason potential gradient of the icosahedral curvature of the $N=144$ cage. Neither $B_{topo}$ nor its map from the $N=144$ cage is action-derived. The retained external search window (the "Shadow Pulse" window) is:
$$\nu_{leak} \approx 380 \pm 20 \text{ GHz}$$
**[Tier 3/open — 380 GHz is a $B_{topo}$ heuristic calibrated to an imported Trp hyperfine scale, not a Tier 2 or action-derived GCT frequency. Open Problem O.10 must supply a physical source, coupling, transfer function and radiometric closure before the window becomes a quantitative test.]**
An $N^2$ intensity law (where $N$ is the number of coherent emitters) is available only under an independently demonstrated Dicke-coherence model. It cannot be assumed to turn the hypothesized source into a detectable transient.

**13.3.2 Material-Proxy Search via Temporal Cross-Correlation**

The historical source scenario inserted $10^{-15}$ W and proposed **Temporal Cross-Correlation** as a background-rejection method. The source power is not derived; the method remains useful as an ordinary material-emission search design.
* **Apparatus:** A Transition Edge Sensor (TES) micro-bolometer coupled to a synchronized neural culture via a **Sapphire Waveguide** (acting as a high-Q Fabry-Pérot cavity).
* **Method:** A future preregistration could time-bin THz power against Multi-Electrode Array (MEA) data and test a declared $1$–$2$ ms window following a coherent gamma burst. Any covariance would be an ordinary material/physiological response until a source model distinguishes it from thermal, electromagnetic, motion and neural-state covariates.

**13.3.2b Signal-to-Noise Estimate [Tier 3 quantitative; full SNR derivation Open Problem O.10]**

The SNR audit evaluates the cavity background implied by the declared THz search design. It does not establish a shadow-pulse source, a coherent emitter population or an $N^2$ enhancement.

* **Free-space blackbody background.** At 310 K, 380 GHz the spectral radiance is $B_\nu \approx 1.3 \times 10^{-14}$ W/m²/Hz/sr [Tier 1 — Planck formula]. Converting this radiance to an in-cavity detector power floor depends on the detector étendue / cavity mode count, and that conversion is the core unresolved quantity of the full SNR derivation (Open Problem O.10): the multimode free-field geometry (1 cm² × 40 GHz × 2π sr) gives $P_{th,free} \sim 3 \times 10^{-7}$ W, whereas a mode-matched single-cavity-mode detector ($h\nu\,\bar n\,\Delta\nu$, $\bar n \approx 16.5$) sees only $\sim 1.7 \times 10^{-10}$ W. The two limits differ by $\sim 2000\times$; the floor figures below are order-of-magnitude placeholders bracketed between them, pending the O.10 étendue closure.

* **Cavity background.** A passive cavity in thermal equilibrium cannot deliver more thermal power per mode than the blackbody limit $h\nu\,\bar n\,\Delta\nu$ (second law), so a cavity Q does not multiply the floor. The earlier "$P_{th,cavity} \sim P_{th,free}\times Q$" enhancement (and its $3\times10^{-3}$ W / $10^{-6}$ W floors) is withdrawn. The background floor is therefore the bracket above, $P_{th} \in [1.7\times10^{-10},\,3\times10^{-7}]$ W (mode-matched to multimode) [Tier 1 Planck/radiometry; étendue pending O.10].

* **Conditional Dicke scaling.** If an independently demonstrated ordinary emitter ensemble has a supplied single-emitter power $P_1$, a common radiative mode, phase coherence and a synchronized population $N$, standard Dicke algebra permits an $N^2$ intensity branch. Substituting the historical external values $P_1 \sim 10^{-15}$ W [Tier 4 — order-of-magnitude] and $N \sim 10^3$ (a synchronized microtubule bundle) gives $P_{enhanced} \sim 10^{-9}$ W [Tier 4 — order-of-magnitude]. Neither the source, the coherence nor its identification with Polarons is derived; this is not a Tier 2 GCT emission mechanism.

* **Radiometric SNR comparison.** Before integration, $P_{enhanced}/P_{th} \sim 10^{-9}/(3\times10^{-7}) \approx 3\times10^{-3}$ under the multimode floor and $\sim 10^{-9}/(1.7\times10^{-10}) \approx 6$ under the mode-matched limit. By the radiometer equation the background fluctuation after an integration $\tau$ is $\sigma_{th}=P_{th}/\sqrt{\Delta\nu\,\tau}$; with $\tau \approx 10^{-3}$ s and $\Delta\nu = 40$ GHz, $\sqrt{\Delta\nu\,\tau}\approx 6.3\times10^3$, giving an ideal per-window SNR $\approx 19$ (multimode) to $\approx 4\times10^4$ (mode-matched) [Tier 1 radiometry on a Tier 4 source amplitude]. With the withdrawn ×Q enhancement removed, the thermal floor is not the binding constraint in the ideal-radiometer limit. Detectability is instead set by quantities not budgeted here: the un-derived Tier 4 source amplitude, the coupling of a 310 K culture into the detector mode, detector noise, and gain stability and other systematics outside the radiometer equation (Open Problem O.10). No detectability claim, positive or negative, is made. The closure-path-(b) anaesthetic-modulation differential can improve background rejection, but it tests a declared THz material/physiological proxy only; it is not a framework-level GCT falsifier.

* **Operative scope.** The direct-detection target is not established as specified: the source amplitude is not derived, and the instrument budget beyond the thermal floor is open. Two instrumentation paths remain:

  - **(a) Geometric SNR enhancement.** Partial SNR gains are available via (i) a cryogenic TES + cavity, which suppresses the *detector/instrument* thermal background but **not** the 310 K biological source's own emission — the culture must remain at 310 K to be viable, so its band-limited blackbody emission into the cavity is an irreducible floor that cannot be cooled; moreover in the relevant band-limited Rayleigh–Jeans regime the blackbody power scales $\propto T$ (not $\propto T^3$), so the cryogenic benefit is detector-side only and far smaller than a naïve $(310/4)^3$ would imply; (ii) much-higher-Q (Q $\sim 10^6$) photonic-crystal cavity matched to the 380 GHz line (mode-selectivity gain); or (iii) cross-correlation between independent detectors viewing the same culture (uncorrelated detector-noise cancellation by $\sqrt{N_{det}}$). These reduce detector-limited noise but do not remove the 310 K source's own thermal emission, which stays in the background in every variant; the (b) anaesthetic-modulation differential below cancels its static part. These options motivate instrumentation studies only; they do not validate the historical source amplitude.

  - **(b) Anaesthetic-modulation material discriminator.** The proxy test does not require absolute detection of the THz line; it asks, in a frozen cross-correlation analysis, whether a THz feature covaries with the anaesthetic intervention after systematics (§13.3.3). No disappearance rule is derived. The anaesthetic-modulation differential cancels the static thermal floor, leaving the time-modulated signal against the thermal fluctuation. By the radiometer equation that fluctuation after $N$ cycles of integration $\tau$ is $\sigma_{th}=P_{th}/\sqrt{\Delta\nu\,\tau\,N}$, so the ideal differential SNR is the per-window value above times $\sqrt{N}$. The earlier estimate $\sigma_{th}\sim P_{th}/\sqrt{N_{shots}}\sim10^{-9}$ W at $N_{shots}\sim10^4$ (and the derived "$N_{shots}\gtrsim10^5$" requirement) is withdrawn: that formula omits $\sqrt{\Delta\nu\,\tau}$ and does not give $10^{-9}$ W for either floor. The required cycle count is set by gain stability, slow drifts and physiological covariates, which the radiometer equation does not include, and it must be derived under O.10. Closure path (b) is a **statistical proxy-branch discriminator**, not a single-session direct-detection claim and not a direct phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II measurement.

* **Operative disposition.** With the passive-cavity floor corrected, the thermal background does not by itself exclude the historical source amplitude; detectability rests on the un-derived Tier 4 source amplitude and on an instrument budget that is not yet written (O.10). The P.8b design is a blinded, frozen-pipeline search for anaesthetic-cycle-correlated 360–400 GHz power. Its former $N_{shots} \gtrsim 10^5$ / $>3\sigma$ number is withdrawn (see (b) above); the power calculation must be derived after O.10 freezes the source amplitude, transfer, étendue/radiometry, coherence, controls and power calculation. A positive or null result constrains only the declared material-emission scenario; it is not a verdict on GCT as a whole, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it. The full SNR budget, the cavity background and instrument-noise calculation, and the phase-coherence-budget derivation are registered as **Open Problem O.10** closure targets for Protocol A; the present §13.3.2b is the *Tier 3 quantitative scope* of the headline detectability claim pending O.10 closure.

**13.3.5 Protocol A-Prime: The NV-Center Surrogate Test**

To isolate ordinary chiral-spin and coherence response from biological confounds, GCT proposes a synthetic surrogate experiment using Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. This is a fully abiotic, room-temperature **material-response proxy experiment**, decoupled from the complexity of live neurons; it is not a direct test of phason-spin coupling, because the typed and normalized coupling, the field-to-material map and the sector-writing matrix element remain open (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3). **Naming.** The name Protocol A-Prime is reserved for this abiotic NV-centre surrogate. Measurements on tubulin preparations, intact microtubules or tissue belong to **Protocol A (the in-vitro/tissue arm)**, referred to below as the in-vitro arm of Protocol A.

> **Protocol A-Prime — Experimental Specification:**
>
> * **Setup:** Isotopically pure $^{12}$C diamond (enrichment $> 99.9\%$) with a frozen ensemble design of $N_{\rm caps}=50$ independently prepared chiral h-BN caps, each read out by $N_{\rm NV}=20$ precisely implanted NV centers at depth $\sim 10$ nm below the surface. The 20 NVs per cap are pooled for depth-jitter mitigation; the 50 caps supply the preregistered cap-level replication for CISS contrast mapping. Isotopic purity suppresses $^{13}$C nuclear-spin-bath noise; for NVs about 10 nm deep the limiting $T_2$ channel is then surface spin and electric noise (spin-phonon coupling limits $T_1$, not $T_2$), which is also the main confound for any cap-to-cap comparison. The controls can isolate ordinary CISS, spin-bath and spin-phonon response; similarity of a material channel does not identify it with a GCT phason channel.
>
> * **Drive:** Apply a swept continuous RF field along the NV symmetry axis over the authoritative half-open interval $\nu_d\in[32,200)$ MHz. Branch A $[102,122]$ MHz and Branch B $[32,52]$ MHz are pre-registered hypothesis regions inside the full scan, not substitute scan bands. For measured $T_{2,\rm eff}$, use the effective linewidth $\delta\nu=1/(2\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$ and require $\Delta\nu_{\rm step}\leq\delta\nu/2=1/(4\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$. Thus the nominal $5$ kHz step is valid only for $T_{2,\rm eff}\leq15.915\,\mu\text{s}$; longer coherence requires a finer grid and a recomputed multiplicity/power budget before unblinding. A $5 \text{ MHz}$ step is permitted only as a coarse scouting sweep and never replaces the full adaptive-resolution scan. The $150$ MHz point is retained as a sign-unfixed O.23/O.24 diagnostic outside F1 and Holm primary decisions. Record $T_2(\nu_d)$ as the primary observable. A continuous swept-frequency drive provides a full spectral characterization of $T_2(\nu_d)$, in contrast to a single-frequency binary test. **Sequence specification required.** The scan frequencies $\nu_d$ above are in the tens of MHz, while the NV ground-state spin transition sits near $2.87$ GHz at zero field, so $\nu_d$ is a filter passband, not a carrier. Sensitivity at $\nu_d$ is obtained in one of two declared ways, and a run must state which: either a microwave carrier resonant with the chosen ground-state transition together with a dynamical-decoupling train whose filter-function passband is centred on $\nu_d$ by the pulse spacing $\tau = 1/(2\nu_d)$, or an explicitly specified dressed-state scheme with its Rabi frequency and bias field given. In either case the preregistration must fix the carrier, the Rabi amplitude in rad/s, the pulse count and spacing, and the resulting filter bandwidth, since these determine what $T_2(\nu_d)$ measures. That specification is not supplied here and is a precondition for executing Protocol A-Prime [Tier 3].
>
> * **Registered scenario windows (coherence-peak location):** the proxy hypothesis is that $T_2(\nu_d)$ exhibits a global maximum in a registered branch window: $\nu_c \approx 112 \pm 10$ MHz for O.12-positive or $\nu_c \approx 42 \pm 10$ MHz for O.12-negative. These centers, their amplitude and the $\eta_F$ profile are Tier 3 external/material scenarios pending O.12/O.23/O.24 closure, not Tier 2 GCT predictions; an observed feature must first be interpreted within ordinary driven-spin, phonon, heating, contact and CISS models. The Floquet factor $\eta_F$ of §13.4.6 peaks at $\nu_d=\Delta_{ST}/h\approx30$ MHz, below the scan, so it cannot shape a peak inside Branch A or B; the branch-window line shape is the empirical Lorentzian-vs-flat model of the peak statistic below, not $\eta_F$.
>
> * **Registered proxy hypothesis — Branch Feature and Frequency Diagnostic:** the proxy branch registers a **measurable, chirality-dependent $T_2$ feature** near a registered branch window. The $150$ MHz point samples the off-branch response, but neither registered spectral-density model fixes the sign of $T_2(150\,\mathrm{MHz})-T_2(\mathrm{baseline})$. Its measured sign and any inferred crossover are therefore protected-subspace/O.23/O.24 diagnostics [Tier 3], not unconditional Tier 2 predictions or F1 conjuncts.
>
> * **Decision-tree summary (single proxy-branch gate):**
> The preregistered contrasts can support or reject the specified **material-response scenario**. A positive result measures an ordinary surrogate response needing independent microscopic attribution; a null rejects the registered biophysical branch within the accepted sensitivity. Neither outcome is a verdict on GCT as a whole: the measurement tests an ordinary material proxy, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3).
> * **Supported branch pattern:** $T_2$ exhibits a sharp peak within a registered hypothesis window and carries the chirality contrast after the full scan and S0-S7 acceptance checks. The measured $150$ MHz response is reported separately with no required sign.
> * **Mechanism diagnostic:** The sign and amplitude at $150$ MHz are recorded as an O.23/O.24 diagnostic. No Zeno or anti-Zeno reading is attached to it, because the drive frequency is not a measurement rate (§13.4.7), and it never defines a framework-level gate.
> * **Branch-specific rework:** Enhancement in both the $\nu_c$ window and at $150$ MHz indicates a broadband driven-spin response rather than a localized density-of-states resonance. Absence of enhancement after a valid fine sweep constrains the protected-subspace branch. These outcomes do not create independent rejection gates; they route through the registered §13.3.5/App PRG P.10 joint decision tree.
>
> * **Adaptive linewidth rule:** The effective transform-limited linewidth is $\delta\nu=1/(2\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$. The acquisition step must resolve at least half of that linewidth, $\Delta\nu_{\rm step}\leq1/(4\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$; linewidth and response shape remain empirical O.23/O.24 diagnostics rather than fixed branch-selection criteria.
>
> * **Scan-step requirement (operational).** The 5 kHz baseline satisfies $\Delta\nu_{\rm step}\leq1/(4\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$ only through $T_{2,\rm eff}=15.915\,\mu\text{s}$. The blinded pilot freezes the measured $T_{2,\rm eff}$ and therefore the required resolution before the decisive run. If it requires a step finer than 5 kHz, the complete half-open $[32,200)$ MHz scan—not merely a branch window—is rerun on the finer grid and its bin count, multiplicity, shot total, and runtime are recomputed before unblinding. Branch A and Branch B remain hypothesis regions inside that authoritative full scan; they never substitute for it. A coarse-only sweep or a pilot-localized branch-only rescan is not a valid Protocol A-Prime execution and cannot support an F1 decision.
>
> * **Proton-bath $T_2$ ceiling (operational; in-vitro arm of Protocol A).** The name Protocol A-Prime is reserved for the abiotic NV-centre surrogate above. When the in-vitro arm of Protocol A is run on biological samples (Trp radical pairs in tubulin), the $^1\text{H}$ proton bath of the surrounding water and protein backbone imposes a baseline $T_2$ ceiling typically in the $1$–$3\,\mu\text{s}$ range from dipolar hyperfine broadening (Maeda et al. 2008; Hore & Mouritsen 2016). Any $T_2$ feature in the registered $\nu_c \approx 112 \pm 10$ MHz window must therefore be measured *relative to this proton-bath baseline*, not against an idealised radical-pair $T_2$. The biological-sample spec of the Protocol A in-vitro arm requires either (a) **deuterated tubulin samples** ($^2\text{H}$ substitution at backbone $^1\text{H}$ sites and bound-water $^1\text{H}\to ^2\text{H}$ exchange; only exchangeable sites such as N1–H exchange from solvent, so the large $\beta$-CH$_2$ couplings need biosynthetic deuteration). Hyperfine couplings scale as $A(^2\text{H})=(\gamma_D/\gamma_H)A(^1\text{H})\approx0.154\,A(^1\text{H})$ [Tier 1], but a $\gamma_H/\gamma_D \approx 6.5\times$ lengthening of $T_2$ is only an upper scenario, since room-temperature radical-pair relaxation in proteins is often dominated by motional modulation of anisotropic interactions rather than by proton flip-flops; at most it would take a $1$–$3\,\mu$s ceiling to $6.5$–$19.5\,\mu$s [Tier 3]; deuteration enables measurement of the registered branch-feature plus chirality signature against the deuterated baseline, OR (b) **explicit baseline-bounding**: report the protonated-sample baseline $T_2^{\rm baseline}$ first and quote the feature as the ratio $T_2(\nu_d = \nu_c)/T_2^{\rm baseline}$ rather than against an absolute $T_2$ target. The Decision Matrix outcomes apply to that branch/chirality signature; peak amplitude and the 150 MHz sign are O.23/O.24 diagnostics rather than separately pre-registered Tier 2 quantities.
>
> * **Significance:** This protocol provides a **conditional, verifier-pending abiotic proxy-branch test design** for the registered spin/coherence branch, insulated from biological confounds. It becomes an executable preregistration only when the scan statistic, S0-S7 acceptance checks, synthetic-data validation, and amendment logic are bound to the public verifier package mirrored in App FSM P.8. A positive outcome would establish an ordinary chiral-spin/coherence response; attribution to a phason interaction would still require the typed, normalized coupling of V1 Ch17 §17.1.3, with magnitude and substrate-transfer closure carried by O.12/O.23/O.24.
