Tier: the **specific 38.3 MHz numerical value** is a Tier 3 external scenario input, and the **parametric structure** ($g_{single}^{eff} \propto \mu_{Trp} \cdot \langle\partial\Phi_\perp\rangle$, with the $\phi^{-9}$ stiffness factor of the Tier 3 P3b hypothesis) is a Tier 3 scenario form pending a type-correct, action-normalized coupling (V1 §17.1.3). Therefore the full 38.3 MHz / ~41$\times$ chain is external-scenario input, not a factor-of-three estimate of a GCT coupling and not a closed geometric eigenvalue from the current postulate set; downstream $\eta_{\rm Zeno}$ and $N_{\rm coh}$ quantities use the overlap-propagated branch unless explicitly labelled pre-overlap.

> If one **externally supplies** the pre-overlap scenario value $g_{single} \approx 38.3$ MHz of §13.1.2 (Tier 3; conditional external-rate input), the standard Tavis-Cummings Hamiltonian for $N_{spin}$ coupled spins,
> $$H_{TC} = \omega_0 a^\dagger a + \sum_{j=1}^{N_{spin}} \frac{\omega_{spin}}{2}\sigma_z^j + g_{single}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{spin}}(a^\dagger \sigma_-^j + a\sigma_+^j),$$
> the collective coupling is $g_{coll} = g_{single}\sqrt{N_{spin}}$. For each NV-center readout in the surrogate ensemble ($N_{spin} = 1$ per center), the same external scenario value is used below. Unit convention: $g_{coll}$ is quoted as a cyclic frequency; the NV linewidth is $\kappa_{\rm cyc}=\kappa/(2\pi)\approx1$ MHz. The Rabi-splitting ratio is therefore
> $$2g_{coll}/\kappa_{\rm cyc} \approx 2(38.3\text{ MHz})/(1\text{ MHz}) \approx 76.6,$$
> equivalently $2(2\pi g_{coll})/\kappa\approx76.6$ in angular-rate units. The scalar $\eta_{Zeno}$ table uses the single-$g$ robustness ratio $g/\kappa_{\rm cyc}$ rather than the $2g$ Rabi-splitting convention; its NV-surrogate row uses the more conservative $2.7\times10^7$ Hz scenario value and reports $\eta_{Zeno}\approx27$. This establishes only what follows from the supplied scenario values. It does not show that the real NV system has that coupling, that the coupling is phasonic, or that any substrate crosses a Level-II threshold; the amplitude of any $T_2$ enhancement remains O.23/O.24-conditional.
>
> **Operational signature for the material proxy branch [Tier 3 material scenario / Tier 3 amplitude].** Strong coupling alone does not guarantee a large extension of the bare $T_2$ — in the absence of a protected-subspace mechanism the polariton-manifold dephasing time stays on the order of the bare matter timescale. *[In the canonical equal-weight strong-coupling limit (Tavis-Cummings 1968 *Phys. Rev.* 170:379 collective-coupling Hamiltonian; Plenio-Knight 1998 *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 70:101 quantum-jump methodology for the polariton-sector Lindblad dynamics), $\gamma_{\text{pol}} = (\gamma + \kappa)/2$. If the bare matter convention is $T_2^{\text{bare}} = 1/\gamma$, then $T_2^{\text{pol}}/T_2^{\text{bare}} = 2\gamma/(\gamma+\kappa)$: this can sit below or modestly above unity depending on $\kappa/\gamma$, but it cannot supply the $10^2$-$10^3$ enhancement needed by the biological gate. DFS-style protection mechanisms (which break the symmetric-dephasing assumption by selecting a dark-state subspace) can exceed the canonical polariton scaling, but require an independent symmetry argument (App ORQ Open Problem O.23). The joint qualitative signature with amplitude conditional on O.23 + O.24 therefore inherits the softer order-of-bare-$T_2$ canonical bound rather than a universal numerical coefficient. The explicit GCT-internal derivation of the upper-polariton symmetric-dephasing scaling on the icosahedral $E_\perp$ lattice is an open refinement beyond the closed soft-form bound of O.31.]* The operational signature is a **frequency-resolved $T_2$ feature** with three components: (i) a non-monotonic peak in $T_2(\nu_d)$ inside a registered hypothesis region of the full adaptive-resolution $[32,200)$ MHz scan; (ii) a chirality-dependent contrast at the registered branch center; and (iii) a sign-unfixed $150$ MHz O.23/O.24 diagnostic outside F1 and Holm primary decisions (the former 50 kHz Zeno/anti-Zeno comparison of §13.4.7 is a declared open programme, not part of this signature). The *magnitude* of the $T_2$ peak that the strong-coupling-plus-protected-subspace chain can deliver is the load-bearing question of **App ORQ Open Problem O.24**; it is not predicted by the bare strong-coupling parameter $2g_{coll}/\kappa$ alone. The scan is experimentally meaningful, but attribution of any feature to a GCT phason interaction is unavailable until a typed, normalized coupling, a field-to-material map and a sector-writing matrix element are independently derived (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3).
>
> **Pre-registered Protocol A-Prime proxy specification [Tier 3 material scenario; amplitude conditional on O.23 + O.24]:**
>
> | Component | Pre-registered claim | Theoretical anchor |
> |---|---|---|
> | (a) Non-monotonic $T_2(\nu_d)$ peak in a registered branch window | Branch A: $T_2(112 \pm 10\text{ MHz}) > T_2(\text{off-resonance})$ at $3\sigma$ on chiral substrate; Branch B: $T_2(42 \pm 10\text{ MHz}) > T_2(\text{off-resonance})$ at $3\sigma$ on the geometric-sibling branch. Both scans use $\leq 5$ kHz spacing and the same S0-S7 acceptance checks; F1 requires the three-conjunct proxy-branch null: no Branch A peak, no Branch B peak, and no chirality contrast after acceptance checks. | Tier 3 driven-spin/material scenario (strong-coupling cavity DOS modification) |
> | (b) 150 MHz frequency-control diagnostic | The sign of $T_2(150\text{ MHz})-T_2(\text{baseline})$ is reported, but is not an F1 conjunct: neither registered model fixes it without the O.23 protected-subspace variance and O.24 peak-enhancement amplitude. | Mechanism diagnostic (Tier 3, O.23/O.24-conditional) |
> | (c) Chirality contrast | $T_2(\text{chiral}, \nu_c) > T_2(\text{achiral}, \nu_c)$ at $3\sigma$ | CISS spin selectivity vanishes on achiral substrate (empirical); the phason coupling it would drive is Tier 3 (§13.2.3; V1 Ch17 §17.1.3). **Confounds:** $T_2$ is even in the sign of spin polarization, so it cannot see the handedness-odd CISS signature (and a racemic cap still carries local polarization of both signs); chiral and achiral caps differ in surface chemistry, charge traps and paramagnetic defects, the dominant $T_2$ channels for $\sim$10 nm NVs; and no charge-transfer or photo-excitation drive is specified, whereas CISS requires electron displacement. A chiral-vs-achiral $T_2$ difference is therefore a chirality-correlated contrast, not a CISS attribution; attribution needs an L-vs-R contrast in a handedness-odd observable (for example a bias-field-referenced shift that reverses with field) under a specified electron-transfer drive [design open, Tier 3] |
> | (d) Peak amplitude | Report the measured value without converting it to $g_{single}$ or $\eta_{Zeno}$. The historical scenario associated a positive O.23 closure with $T_2^{\text{enhanced}}/T_2^{\text{base}}$ in $[10^2, 10^3]$ and a negative closure with a feature of order the bare-$T_2$ polariton-dephasing scale; no $10^2$–$10^3$ enhancement or phason attribution is currently licensed | Empirical proxy output; App ORQ Open Problems O.23 + O.24 |
>
![Protocol A-Prime is decided by a frequency-resolved, chirality-dependent $T_2(\nu_d)$ pattern: Branch A, Branch B, and chirality contrast feed the three-conjunct joint null; the 150 MHz point is a mechanism diagnostic.](content/Figures/Volume_3/Figure V3.13.4.svg)

> The registered proxy discriminator is a registered-branch peak plus chirality contrast: a proxy-branch null requires no Branch A peak, no Branch B peak, and no chirality contrast after the frozen acceptance checks. It can distinguish candidate material-response phenomenologies, not GCT from all non-GCT physics. The 150 MHz sign is retained as a mechanism diagnostic because its sign is O.23/O.24-conditional, not an F1 conjunct. The peak *amplitude* is likewise reported as O.23 + O.24 conditional; the bare strong-coupling parameter $2g_{coll}/\kappa$ alone is the strong-coupling signature, not the $T_2$ enhancement.
>
> **Registered scenario-window scan rule:** The authoritative acquisition is the full half-open scan $[32,200)$ MHz with $\Delta\nu_{\rm step}\leq1/(4\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$. Branch A $[102,122]$ MHz and Branch B $[32,52]$ MHz are pre-registered hypothesis regions within that scan, not independently scanned alternatives. Branch A is the primary historical ~100 MHz scenario window; Branch B is the sibling window registered for O.12-negative outcomes. Neither window is a derived GCT frequency, and no $\eta_{\rm Zeno}$ mechanism in the current action shifts one into the other. The $150$ MHz response is sign-unfixed and diagnostic-only. The complete scan, both hypothesis regions, and S0-S7 package are frozen before unblinding; branch selection is not inferred from observed A-Prime data.
>
> **Multiplicity-aware peak statistic:** The primary statistic is a locally weighted likelihood-ratio test comparing a Lorentzian peak model against a flat local baseline for $T_2(\nu_d)$. The physical window is fixed at $\pm100$ kHz around each tested center; it contains 41 grid points only at the 5 kHz baseline and is recomputed on a finer adaptive grid. The baseline half-open grid $[32,200)$ MHz at 5 kHz contains exactly $33{,}600$ samples per cell. The six primary cells are the experimental-design premise $\{\text{L-chiral},\text{R-chiral},\text{achiral/racemic}\}\times\{\text{RF scan},\text{matched sham/no-drive}\}$; bare diamond is an auxiliary calibration outside the multiplier. Hence $M=33{,}600\times6=201{,}600$ baseline bin-cells. The global gate uses $\alpha_{\rm global}=2.7\times10^{-3}$, giving $\alpha_{\rm local}=\alpha_{\rm global}/M\approx1.34\times10^{-8}$. With $z_{\alpha,\rm local}=5.6$, $z_\beta=1.48$, and $\delta_{T_2}=0.10$, the raw requirement is exactly
> $$N_{T_2,\rm scan}^{\rm raw}=\left(\frac{5.6+1.48}{0.10}\right)^2=5012.64$$
> shots per bin-cell and the executable integer ceiling is $5013$. The baseline totals are $1{,}010{,}548{,}224$ raw shots and $1{,}010{,}620{,}800$ executable shots. At 1 kHz they require $280.70784$ h and $280.728$ h, respectively, before acceptance failures, overheads, or re-runs; with the declared per-shot overheads and readout noise the requirement is years, not hours (see the joint-gate calculation below). These totals scale linearly with the declared cell count. If $T_{2,\rm eff}>15.915\,\mu$s, the grid is tightened using $\Delta\nu_{\rm step}\leq1/(4\pi T_{2,\rm eff})$ and the bins, $M$, local threshold, shot count, and runtime are recomputed before unblinding. A scan-level null occurs when the maximum statistic over the full scan remains below the globally corrected threshold; only the accepted three-conjunct Branch A + Branch B + chirality null triggers F1.
>
> **Decision Matrix (pre-registered material-proxy interpretation) — chirality-contrast variant:**
>
> | Outcome | Joint signature | Verdict |
> |---|---|---|
> | **Joint proxy pattern present** | $T_2$ at a registered branch center (Branch A $112 \pm 10$ MHz or Branch B $42 \pm 10$ MHz) exceeds $T_2(\text{off-res})$ at $3\sigma$ on chiral substrate after the full adaptive-resolution scan, AND chirality contrast is present at $3\sigma$ | Material-response scenario supported; microscopic attribution remains open; peak amplitude and the sign-unfixed 150 MHz diagnostic are reported as O.23 + O.24 readouts |
> | **Generic driven-spin response** | Enhancement at $3\sigma$ on both chiral and achiral substrates with no $T_2(\nu_d)$ structure | Chiral proxy not supported; characterize ordinary drive/heating/phonon response |
> | **Frequency-specific, chirality-null** | A registered branch peak is present, but chirality contrast is null after S1 + S6 acceptance checks pass; the 150 MHz diagnostic is reported separately | Frequency-specific material response; no CISS attribution; routes to O.12/O.24 benchmarking |
> | **Chirality-only / branch-null** | Chirality contrast is present, but both registered branch scans are null after RF/systematic controls pass | Ordinary chirality-correlated contrast detected (CISS attribution requires the L-vs-R handedness-odd test of component (c)); no protected-subspace or phason inference; not an F1 null |
> | **Sensitivity-limited mixed outcome** | Any component null before its preregistered acceptance checks pass (RF flatness, cap chirality, NV-depth, or batch reproducibility) | Inconclusive; re-power or re-run the affected component before applying F1 |
> | **Proxy-branch null (F1)** | No non-monotonic peak in Branch A, no non-monotonic peak in Branch B, and no chirality contrast after all acceptance checks pass | F1: reject the registered biophysical branch (chiral phonon-polariton / protected-subspace Zeno branch) at the NV-centre surrogate level, as registered; no verdict on GCT as a whole or on Level II; the 150 MHz sign is diagnostic only |
>
> Neither outcome class is a verdict on GCT as a whole: the measurement tests an ordinary material proxy, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3). A preregistered null meeting the F1 rule above rejects the registered biophysical branch as registered.
>
> **Formal Preregistration Statement — Protocol A-Prime**
>
> The joint signature is a **Tier 3 material-proxy hypothesis**: the branch-feature plus chirality pattern. The peak *amplitude* (whether $T_2^{\text{enhanced}}/T_2^{\text{base}}$ exceeds $10$, $100$, or $1000$) and the sign at 150 MHz are empirical measurements of the closure values of Open Problems O.23 and O.24, not separately registered Tier 2 quantities. The frozen NV ensemble is $N_{\rm NV}=20$ implanted NV centers per cap across $N_{\rm caps}=50$ caps; CISS contrast mapping therefore uses $N_{\rm caps}N_{\rm NV}=1000$ NV-center observations rather than a mutable single-cap ensemble size. Shot noise scales as $1/\sqrt{N_{\rm caps}N_{\rm NV}}$. A clean branch-feature plus chirality signal at $3\sigma$ measures an ordinary chiral-spin/coherence pattern with whatever amplitude the measurement delivers; it does not confirm a chiral phonon-polariton GCT interaction. Mixed outcomes are interpreted per the Decision Matrix, and only the fully accepted three-conjunct joint null triggers F1, which rejects the registered proxy branch only.
>
> **Joint-gate sample-size calculation.** For a normalized single-shot contrast estimate with Gaussian shot noise, a one-component $3\sigma$ gate with 80% marginal power uses
> $$N_{\rm shots}\geq \left(\frac{3+0.84}{\delta}\right)^2,$$
> where $\delta$ is the fractional effect size after the S0-S7 systematic budget. The conservative pre-registered effect sizes are $\delta_{T_2}=0.10$ for the non-monotonic selected-branch peak, $\delta_{\chi}=0.05$ for the chirality contrast after cap-purity, transfer retention, and NV-depth dilution, and $\delta_{150}=0.10$ for powering the sign-unfixed 150 MHz diagnostic response. Therefore:
> $$N_{T_2}\geq 1.48\times10^3,\qquad N_{\chi}\geq 5.90\times10^3,\qquad N_{150}\geq 1.48\times10^3.$$
> These design effect sizes ($\delta_{T_2}$, $\delta_{\chi}$, $\delta_{150}$) are locked by the blinded pilot calibration before unblinding the decisive run. The $\delta_{150}$ and $N_{150}$ entries power the sign-unfixed diagnostic only and never determine F1 or a Holm primary decision. If the pilot lower edge falls below the registered branch-feature or chirality values, that F1 component is sensitivity-limited and must be re-powered rather than treated as a clean F1 proxy rejection. The conservative acquisition design retains 93% marginal power per measured component ($z_\beta \approx 1.48$), giving $N_{T_2}\geq 2.01\times10^3$, $N_{\chi}\geq 8.03\times10^3$, and diagnostic $N_{150}\geq 2.01\times10^3$ per relevant fixed-frequency cell. The full half-open $[32,200)$ MHz adaptive-resolution scan supersedes every fixed-frequency $N_{T_2}$ number. At the 5 kHz baseline $M=201{,}600$ and the multiplicity-aware peak requirement is
> $$N_{T_2,\rm scan}^{\rm raw}=5012.64,\qquad N_{T_2,\rm scan}^{\rm executable}=5013$$
> shots per bin-cell for the same 80% joint-power design. On the baseline 5 kHz grid, $33{,}600$ samples per cell and six enumerated cells give $1{,}010{,}548{,}224$ raw shots or $1{,}010{,}620{,}800$ executable shots, corresponding at 1 kHz to $280.70784$ h or $280.728$ h. The adaptive-linewidth rule and linear cell-count sensitivity stated above govern any re-budgeting. The 1 kHz cadence assumes 1 ms per shot. With the realistic CPMG reset, RF-settling and blinding overheads of $10$–$100$ ms per shot, the same $1.01\times10^9$ shots take $1.0\times10^7$–$1.0\times10^8$ s, i.e. about $0.32$–$3.2$ years. The shot model also takes $\sigma_{\rm meas}$ as one unit per shot; conventional room-temperature single-NV optical readout sits a factor $\sigma_R\approx10$–$80$ above the spin-projection limit (Barry et al. 2020, *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 92:015004, Table 2), which multiplies the required repetitions by $\sigma_R^2\approx10^2$–$6\times10^3$, and each $T_2$ bin needs a fitted decay curve rather than a single shot. As specified, the full-scan acquisition is therefore not feasible: "shot" must be redefined as an averaged $T_2$ estimate with explicit photon statistics and readout contrast, and the scan, cell count or effect size re-budgeted before the design is executable [Tier 3 experimental-design calculation]. The $\delta_{\chi}=0.05$ contrast is a sensitivity-design target locked after the achiral/chiral pilot calibration; if the measured CISS lower edge or transfer-retention factor erases this contrast, the chirality component is sensitivity-limited and the acquisition must be re-powered rather than treated as a clean F1 proxy rejection. Joint power is calculated from the three marginal powers under the independence approximation [Tier 3]; correlations among S0-S7 systematics are reported in the analysis notebook and widen the confidence interval rather than changing the F1 gate.
>
> **Deterministic CISS contrast mapping.** Required shot count uses the frozen ensemble convention: $N_{\rm caps}=50$ caps and $N_{\rm NV}=20$ implanted NV centers per cap contribute $N_{\rm obs}=50\times20=1000$ NV-center observations. The cap-level CISS variable is measured before unblinding by CD/VCD chirality verification plus transport spin-polarimetry per cap, but the clean F1 chirality input is the post-transfer effective product
> $$P_{\rm eff}\equiv r_{\rm transfer}P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net},$$
> and $P_{\rm eff}\ge0.1$ must be established at $\ge5\sigma$ confidence across the 50 caps/witness stacks for a clean F1 run. Shot noise therefore scales as $1/\sqrt{N_{\rm caps}N_{\rm NV}}$ with $\sigma_{\rm meas}=1$ photon-count unit (an idealization; real readout multiplies the counts below by $\sigma_R^2$, see above). The per observation count is
> $$N_{\rm shots}^{\rm per\,obs}=\frac{(z_{1-\alpha/2}+z_{1-\beta})^2\,\sigma_{\rm meas}^2/(N_{\rm caps}N_{\rm NV})}{(P_{\rm eff}\delta\chi)^2}
> =\frac{4.20\times10^{-2}}{(P_{\rm eff}\cdot0.05)^2}
> =\frac{16.8}{P_{\rm eff}^2}.$$
> Equivalently, the total pooled acquisition cycles across the 1000 NV-center observations are
> $$N_{\rm cycles}^{\rm total}=N_{\rm caps}N_{\rm NV}N_{\rm shots}^{\rm per\,obs}=\frac{1.68\times10^4}{P_{\rm eff}^2}.$$
> Here the numerator uses the declared 5σ clean-run gate with the same 93% marginal-power convention as the three-component design, $(5+1.48)^2\approx42.0$; the 95%/80% comparison convention does not set this gate. For effective polarization band $P_{\rm eff}\in[0.05,0.20]$, this gives total cycles $6.72\times10^6$ ($P_{\rm eff}=0.05$), $1.68\times10^6$ ($P_{\rm eff}=0.10$), and $4.20\times10^5$ ($P_{\rm eff}=0.20$), with per-observation counts lower by $10^3$. At the declared $P_{\rm eff}=0.025$ sensitivity floor, the total-cycle requirement is $2.69\times10^7$ (about $2.69\times10^4$ shots per center-observation), still below the $10^9$ cycle ceiling; below this floor the chirality component is sensitivity-limited by cap polarization/systematic reproducibility, not treated as a clean F1 proxy rejection. If only the source-material value $P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net}$ is known, the re-powering uses the retained product: $r_{\rm transfer}=0.5$ increases the shot/cycle requirement by $4\times$, and $r_{\rm transfer}=0.1$ increases it by $100\times$.
>
> **CISS floor interpretation.**
>
> | Measured post-transfer $P_{\rm eff}=r_{\rm transfer}P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net}$ | Interpretation | Action |
> | :--- | :--- | :--- |
> | $\geq 0.1$ | S1 acceptance floor for clean F1 proxy rejection | The declared shot budget can deliver the chirality component of the joint F1 gate. |
> | $0.025 \leq P_{\rm eff} < 0.1$ | Sensitivity-Limited Pending Re-Powering | The run can be re-powered by increasing shots with $N_{\rm shots}\propto1/P_{\rm eff}^2$, but the declared run cannot deliver a clean proxy rejection at the declared shot budget. |
> | $<0.025$ | Sensitivity-limited floor | No proxy verdict; this is not a GCT, phason or Level-II result. |
>
> **Protocol record:** Analysis pipeline specifies (a) NV center depth and isotopic purity, (b) RF drive amplitude and pulse sequence, (c) statistical threshold for significance ($p < 0.003$, corresponding to $3\sigma$), and (d) blinding procedure for the $T_2(\nu_d)$ scan. Any deviation from these parameters constitutes a separate protocol amendment.
>
> **Public preregistration archive.** Before unblinding, the protocol package is deposited in a public timestamped archive (OSF or Zenodo, with optional arXiv protocol note) containing the frozen analysis code, synthetic-data budget, NV-depth/isotopic-purity acceptance files, RF-drive grid, S0-S7 systematic gates, and the amendment ledger. Any parameter change after deposit is recorded as a numbered amendment with timestamp, rationale, and the blinded/unblinded state of the affected data.
>
> **Executable-readiness qualifier.** Protocol A-Prime is a prospective preregistration design until the verifier script, synthetic-data package, analysis-code hash, operating-system/environment manifest, and OSF/Zenodo archive URL are frozen together before unblinding. Before that freeze, P.8 is not an executable decisive test; it is the authoritative design specification for the frozen package. Even after that freeze, P.8 is decisive only for its declared material-response proxy branch, not for GCT as a whole, phason coupling or Level II.
>
> **Proxy-branch decision conditions (two-level, pre-registered):**
>
> **F1 proxy-branch rejection rule (Protocol A-Prime, single rule).** F1 fires, rejecting the registered biophysical branch as registered, if and only if all three conjuncts hold after the frozen S0-S7 acceptance checks pass: (a) NO peak detected in the Branch A $112 \pm 10$ MHz hypothesis region, (b) NO peak detected in the Branch B $42 \pm 10$ MHz hypothesis region of the full adaptive-resolution $[32,200)$ MHz scan, and (c) NO chirality contrast against the achiral control using $> 99.9\%$ isotopically pure $^{12}$C diamond. Branch A is the primary historical ~100 MHz scenario window; Branch B is the sibling window registered for O.12-negative outcomes. A Branch A/B-only null is the peak-subtest null, not an F1 rejection; the F1 gate is the three-part joint null at the required $\delta\chi + N_{\rm shots}$. **This is the sole Protocol A-Prime rejection gate.** It is not a verdict on GCT as a whole: the measurement tests an ordinary material proxy, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3). The $150$ MHz response is a sign-unfixed Tier 3 O.23/O.24 diagnostic outside F1 and Holm primary decisions. S0 systematic floor (in-vitro arm of Protocol A only; the abiotic NV surrogate contains no Trp radical pair, so S0 does not apply to it): $\Delta_{ST}/h$ of the Trp radical pair must lie inside the 5-200 MHz admissible tubulin-EPR band before a biological branch-frequency decision is treated as decisive; outside that band the run is sensitivity-limited or routes to O.12/O.23 branch re-estimation. Under an F1 rejection there is no CISS "classical floor" fallback: ordinary CISS response would constrain the material system only, and no Level II classification follows for any concrete substrate.
>
> **(F2) Peak-amplitude readout (distinct from F1).** Conditional on a positive branch-feature plus chirality signal after the frozen acceptance checks, the peak amplitude and 150 MHz sign are reported as empirical readouts of the joint O.23 + O.24 closure values. They are not separately registered gates. A low-amplitude positive signature would be compatible with a weaker or non-DFS-mediated O.23 scenario; a high-amplitude positive signature would be compatible with a protected-subspace scenario, but no $[10^2,10^3]\times$ enhancement is currently licensed. F2 never translates an amplitude into $g_{single}$, $\eta_{Zeno}$, a protected phason subspace or consciousness.
>
> Between F1 and F2 — any measurement yielding a positive joint signature, across amplitudes from below-bare through the positive-O.23 $[10^2,10^3]\times$ band — the experiment serves as the empirical readout of the joint $(\Omega_{\text{DFS}}, \kappa_{\text{chiral}})$ closure of Open Problems O.23 + O.24, constraining the Tier 3 material inputs; empirical agreement does not promote them to Tier 2. Promotion requires an independent derivation of the relevant DFS/chiral parameters and normalized physical coupling from the declared premises, closing the O.23/O.24 derivational dependencies without fitting the target measurements. Observations then test the resulting claim.
>
> **§13.3.5.S Systematic-Error Budget [pre-registered]**
>
> The Protocol A-Prime pre-registration matches the §16.3.4 Protocol D rigor in disclosing the dominant systematic uncertainties on the branch-feature/chirality gate and the separate 150 MHz diagnostic. Seven systematics are enumerated below; each is paired with the dominant effect it produces, the propagation chain into the F1 proxy gate or diagnostic, and the operational mitigation. The pre-registered systematic budget is committed before unblinding alongside the F1/F2 statements above.
>
> \newpage
>
> **(S1) Chiral h-BN cap chirality-purity**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** Reduces chirality contrast (component c); a partially-racemic cap or post-transfer stack with $P_{\rm eff}=r_{\rm transfer}P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net}<0.1$ collapses the chiral-vs-achiral contrast into the $3\sigma$ noise band, producing false-null on (c) even with a real chirality-dependent material response present at the declared shot budget.
>
> **Magnitude band:** Naaman-Paltiel-Waldeck 2019 *Nat. Rev. Chem.* 3:250 places CISS polarization up to $\sim60\%$ in ordered-helical DNA stress-test substrates, while protein/peptide systems sit in the operative $5$–$20\%$ band; the source cap-substrate $P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net}$ is the *enantiomer excess × per-helix polarization*. $F_{\rm CISS}=2.0$ is a Tier 3 model translation from measured $P_{\rm CISS}$ spin-polarization; see App BEB §BEB.11.1 for the protein-band $P_{\rm CISS}\in[0.05,0.20]$ and DNA-equivalent stress edge $P_{\rm CISS}\approx0.6$. A racemic cap ($ee = 0$) gives $P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net} = 0$; $ee = 50\%$ at the DNA stress edge gives $P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net} \approx 0.3$ before transfer. Effect-size impact scales linearly with the retained product $P_{\rm eff}$.
>
> **Mitigation:** **Inclusion criterion for clean F1:** measured $P_{\rm eff}\geq0.1$ AND $ee \geq 90\%$. Pre-unblinding measurement: spin-polarimetry on the h-BN/NV cap pair using CD/VCD chirality verification plus either Mott polarimetry of transmitted electrons or magnetoresistance with a ferromagnetic electrode, at the operating temperature; CD/VCD is necessary but not sufficient. (The chiral and racemic cap materials themselves still need a concrete definition, since bulk h-BN is achiral.) $P_{\rm eff}$ must be measured $\geq0.1$ with $\geq5\sigma$ confidence before Branch A/B unblinding. For $0.025 \leq P_{\rm eff}<0.1$, the chirality component is Sensitivity-Limited Pending Re-Powering with $N_{\rm shots}\propto1/P_{\rm eff}^2$. For $P_{\rm eff}<0.025$, the result is sensitivity-limited and supplies no proxy verdict. CD/VCD spectroscopic verification of $ee \geq 90\%$ is required before each Protocol A-Prime run; a cap with $ee < 90\%$ is excluded. Achiral control uses CD-confirmed racemic h-BN. **Dominant systematic if the cap is sourced from synthesis without CD verification — invalidates component (c) reproducibility and supplies no proxy, framework or Level-II verdict.**
>
> **(S2) NV depth jitter**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** Modulates the NV–cap distance, which sets the ordinary NV–cap dipolar sensitivity and therefore the measured interface-response amplitude; it does not measure a chiral phonon-polariton or phason coupling. NV depth shifts of $\pm 2$ nm at a nominal 10 nm depth modulate that sensitivity by $+95\%/-42\%$, about $\pm 60\%$ linearized (dipolar $1/r^3$ falloff: $(10/8)^3=1.95$, $(10/12)^3=0.58$).
>
> **Magnitude band:** NV implantation depth standard deviation typically $\sigma_d \in [0.5, 2]$ nm depending on implantation energy and annealing protocol; $\sigma_d = 2$ nm gives a per-sample variation on the joint (a)+(b) amplitude of about $\pm 60\%$.
>
> **Mitigation:** Pre-registration requires NV depth characterization via secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) calibration on a control batch from the same implantation lot, with the $\sigma_d$ reported as the leading systematic on the (a)+(b) amplitude scaling. Statistical pooling across the frozen $N_{\rm NV}=20$ NVs per cap averages the random depth jitter to about $\pm 60/\sqrt{20} \approx 13\%$ before the 50-cap CISS contrast aggregation is applied; pooling does not remove a lot-level bias in mean depth, which is carried as a systematic.
>
> **(S3) RF amplitude calibration drift across the $[32,200)$ MHz sweep**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** Modulates the Rabi-frequency-dependent measurement of $T_2(\nu_d)$, producing apparent $T_2(\nu_d)$ structure that mimics component (a) at the few-percent level if the RF amplitude is not flat across the sweep.
>
> **Magnitude band:** Standard NV-AC-magnetometry pulse-shaping drift across a $[32,200)$ MHz sweep is taken as $\pm 5\%$ in pulse area; this propagates to a $\pm 5\%$ apparent $T_2(\nu_d)$ feature that is *not* a real material-proxy signal.
>
> **Mitigation:** Pre-registration requires an *RF amplitude flatness calibration sweep* on a reference NV (single-NV regime, no chiral cap) before each Protocol A-Prime run, with the residual RF flatness $< 2\%$ as the acceptance condition. The reference-NV sweep is reported with the protocol and subtracted from the chiral-cap measurement at the lock-in stage.
>
> **(S4) Hahn-echo $\pi$-pulse fidelity**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** Stochastic per-pulse loss compounds across the registered CPMG train and can mask or mimic component (a); coherent over-rotation, state-preparation-and-measurement error and intrinsic decoherence require separate nuisance terms.
>
> **Magnitude band:** For the declared independent stochastic-loss model, the surviving contrast is $F_\pi^N$. The acceptance condition is therefore $F_\pi\geq(1-\delta_{\rm allow})^{1/N}$ with $N=2\nu_dT_{\rm int}$. At $\nu_d=112$ MHz, $T_{\rm int}=10\,\mu$s and $\delta_{\rm allow}=0.10$, $N=2240$ and $F_\pi\geq0.999953$; the branch centre at $42$ MHz requires $F_\pi\geq0.999875$. A fixed $0.99$ threshold would leave only $1.7\times10^{-10}$ contrast after 2240 pulses and is inadmissible [Tier 3 experimental-design calculation].
>
> **Mitigation:** Pre-registration must declare $T_{\rm int}$, $\nu_d$, $N$, $\delta_{\rm allow}$ and the stochastic/coherent error model before unblinding. Randomized benchmarking and sequence-level reference runs must establish the resulting branch-specific $F_\pi$ threshold; runs that do not meet it are sensitivity-limited. Baseline correction is fitted jointly from the declared nuisance model rather than obtained by subtracting average gate infidelity.
>
> **(S5) Floquet sideband artefacts**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** An ordinary strongly driven spin system (no magnon-polaron or Zeno source is assumed) can produce Floquet sidebands at $\nu_d \pm n\,\nu_{\rm sideband}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, which can mimic the non-monotonic $T_2(\nu_d)$ peak (component a) at frequencies offset from $\nu_c$ if the sideband structure is not characterized.
>
> **Magnitude band:** Floquet sideband amplitude scales with $(g_{\rm drive}/\omega_d)^2$ and produces apparent $T_2(\nu_d)$ features at $\nu_d \pm \nu_{\rm hyperfine}$ with amplitudes up to $\sim 10\%$ of the main feature for strong drives.
>
> **Mitigation:** Pre-registration requires a *Floquet-sideband characterization scan* on the achiral control substrate first (sidebands appear as $T_2(\nu_d)$ structure independent of chirality), with the sideband positions and amplitudes catalogued before the chiral measurement. The chiral measurement is then masked at the sideband frequencies to prevent false-positive component (a) attribution.
>
> **(S6) Sample-batch chirality reproducibility**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** Run-to-run variation in the CISS-cap synthesis batch produces between-run amplitude variation on component (c) (chirality contrast) at the $10$–$20\%$ level even with $ee \geq 90\%$ per (S1).
>
> **Magnitude band:** Synthesis-batch reproducibility on chiral h-BN under standardized CVD conditions is typically $\pm 15\%$ on the per-helix polarization, propagating to $\pm 15\%$ between-run variation on the chirality-contrast amplitude.
>
> **Mitigation:** Pre-registration requires *three independent synthesis batches* of the chiral cap, each with CD verification, with the chirality-contrast amplitude reported as the mean ± SD across batches. The $3\sigma$ proxy-rejection gate on component (c) is evaluated against the inter-batch SD, not the single-batch SD. **Dominant systematic on the chirality-contrast amplitude reproducibility — analogous to the $^{17}$O enrichment efficiency in Protocol D §16.3.4; a leading material-proxy systematic, not a framework-level one.**
>
> **(S7) Cap-to-NV transfer and post-transfer CISS retention**
>
> **Effect on branch/chirality gate or 150 MHz diagnostic:** A cap that passes standalone chirality/CISS metrology can lose effective spin-selective coupling after transfer, bonding, contamination, strain, or NV-surface processing; this produces a false null on chirality contrast and can reduce the observed $\delta\chi$ without invalidating the pre-transfer cap measurement.
>
> **Magnitude band:** Transfer-induced CISS retention is treated as a multiplicative uncertainty on the chirality term. The retained factor $r_{\rm transfer}$ must be measured on witness h-BN/NV stacks; otherwise $\delta\chi$ is reported with an added transfer-uncertainty multiplier and the run cannot support clean F1.
>
> **Mitigation:** Pre-unblinding acceptance requires witness-stack spin-polarimetry or magnetoresistance on the actual transferred cap/NV process flow, not only on source material. Clean F1 requires $r_{\rm transfer}P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net}\ge0.1$ with $\ge5\sigma$ confidence; $0.025\le r_{\rm transfer}P_{\rm CISS}^{\rm net}<0.1$ is sensitivity-limited and requires re-powering; below $0.025$ no proxy verdict is reported, and no threshold here is a framework or Level-II falsifier.
>
>
> **Dominant systematic identification:** The chiral h-BN cap chirality-purity (S1), sample-batch reproducibility (S6), and cap-to-NV transfer retention (S7) jointly carry the bulk of the systematic uncertainty on the chirality-contrast component (c) of the joint signature. A null on (c) at $3\sigma$ that is *not preceded by S1 + S6 + S7 verification* is interpreted as **inconclusive on the chirality-contrast component, not as an F1 proxy rejection**. Verification of S1 (CD spectroscopy $ee \geq 90\%$), S6 (three-batch reproducibility), and S7 (post-transfer CISS-retention metrology on witness stacks) before the Protocol A-Prime run is the pre-registered acceptance condition for a clean F1 proxy-rejection test on component (c). The (S2), (S3), (S4), (S5) systematics carry the bulk of the uncertainty on components (a) and (b) and are mitigated by the per-run reference-NV calibrations. None of these acceptance conditions creates a GCT, phason or Level-II falsification gate.
>
> *Cross-references:* §16.3.4 (Protocol D systematic-error budget — the rigor template); App NSP §NSP.5 (CISS empirical foundations); App ORQ Open Problem O.23 (chiral phonon-polariton DFS substrate-side closure path); App ORQ Open Problem O.24 (Protocol A-Prime amplitude under O.23 closure).

### §13.3.5.A Protocol A-Prime Extended: Chiral vs. Achiral NV-Centre Comparison

**Objective:** Test whether any $T_2$ feature in the registered $\nu_c \approx 112 \pm 10$ MHz
(or $42 \pm 10$ MHz) scenario window depends on an ordinary chiral material
environment or is substrate-agnostic. This is a CISS/material-control question,
not a direct GCT prediction.

**Physical Setup:**

The experiment compares L-chiral, R-chiral, racemic/achiral and bare-NV controls.
Direct spin-polarimetry, current/contact metrology and $T_2$ are the observables.
The historical proxy scenario expects a sign-positive registered-window feature on
the chiral cap (net CISS, spin-selective transport) and $T_2^{achiral} \approx T_2^{bare}$
on an achiral cap (a racemic cap is not equivalent for the polarization-even
observable $T_2$, since it still carries local polarization of both signs), with any magnitude measured as an empirical readout of O.23/O.24.
Chirality reversal may reverse an ordinary spin-polarization sign; it does not imply a
Zeno Lock. No $10^2$–$10^3$ enhancement or phason attribution is currently licensed,
and the amplitude is **not** a rejection threshold.

| Substrate | Measured CISS response? | $T_2$ scenario expectation at the registered window | Inference ceiling |
|:---|:---:|:---|:---|
| NV in diamond (bare) | Control | Baseline T₂ (reference) | Ordinary NV response |
| NV + achiral h-BN | Must be measured (expected none) | ≈ Baseline T₂; matched interface control | Ordinary interface response |
| NV + L-chiral h-BN | Must be measured | Test for a chirality-correlated non-monotonic registered-window feature; amplitude reported as O.23/O.24 readout | Ordinary CISS/material proxy |
| NV + R-chiral h-BN | Must be measured (opposite hand) | Test handedness reversal/symmetry of the same feature | Ordinary CISS/material proxy |

*Table note.* The joint preregistered rule (registered-branch feature plus
chirality contrast at $3\sigma$, §13.3.5 Decision Matrix) decides only the
material proxy branch. The sign-unfixed 150 MHz response and peak amplitude
are empirical responses, not readouts of a GCT coupling or Level II.

Handedness reversal is a useful material control, but the detailed symmetry of
the measured magnitude depends on contacts, defects, orientation and the
ordinary CISS transport model. It is not a Zeno-locking theorem.

**Why NV Centres:** shallow (~10 nm) NVs have $T_2$ of order $10\,\mu\text{s}$, comparable to
the $1$–$10\,\mu$s Trp radical-pair scenario band (millisecond $T_2$ belongs to bulk NVs); NV array density and spacing are controllable; diamond + h-BN capping
is established nanofabrication technology. Timeline: 2–5 years, executable only after preregistration verifier/package freeze and the S0-S7 acceptance files are locked.

**Public preregistration deposit required before unblinding the chiral vs. achiral comparison.** The OSF/Zenodo timestamp, frozen code hash, synthetic-data budget, S0-S7 acceptance files, and amendment ledger are part of the protocol record.

### §13.3.6 Protocol A-Tertius: Leggett-Garg Test of the Material Coherence Proxy

**Objective (historical).** Protocol A-Tertius proposed a Leggett-Garg Inequality (LGI) test of temporal coherence in a radical-pair or NV material system driven in the registered branch windows. It is now a declared open programme (below); no registered gate remains.

**The Leggett-Garg Framework.** The Leggett-Garg Inequalities (Leggett & Garg, 1985) constrain the temporal correlations of a macroscopic two-state system under the assumptions of **macrorealism** (the system is in a definite state at all times) and **non-invasive measurability** (measurement does not disturb the state). For a dichotomic observable $Q(t) \in \{+1, -1\}$, the temporal correlation functions $C_{ij} = \langle Q(t_i) Q(t_j) \rangle$ must satisfy:

$$K_3 \equiv C_{12} + C_{23} - C_{13} \leq 1 \quad \text{(LGI bound)}$$

Any classical stochastic process satisfies this inequality. **Quantum mechanics allows $K_3 > 1$** (up to a maximum of $K_3^{max} = 3/2$ for a qubit), signaling genuine quantum superposition across the temporal interval.

**Declared open programme [Tier 3/4] — Protocol A-Tertius.** (a) *Claimed:* a three-time LGI test, $K_3(\nu_c)>1$, on the singlet-triplet parity of a single radical pair read by ODMR with quantum-non-demolition weak measurements at $\tau_c=1/\nu_c\approx8.9$ ns spacing, registered as a binary gate (P.8c) for a protected-subspace coherence branch. (b) *Defects:* single-radical-pair singlet/triplet readout with QND measurements at ns spacing does not exist (radical-pair spin state is read destructively, through recombination yield on ensembles, and NV optical readout alone takes about 300 ns); and on the NV surrogate the test is non-diagnostic as designed, because LGI violation by a single NV spin is already established (Waldherr et al. 2011, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107:090401) and any coherently precessing spin gives $K_3>1$ at suitable times. A positive result would therefore say nothing about a protected-subspace branch, and a null would depend on the chosen times. (c) *Closing would need:* an executable ensemble (ideal-negative-measurement) LGI scheme and a branch-specific prediction for $K_3(\nu)$ that differs from that of a bare coherent spin. (d) No decision, scorecard row or downstream claim uses A-Tertius as support; the former $K_3\approx1+\phi^{-9}/\pi$ effect size, sample-size plan and P.8c decision rule are withdrawn.

*Cross-reference: §13.3.5 (T₂ enhancement Protocol A-Prime), §13.4.5 (Lindblad master equation treatment), V1 §17.1.4 (Tubulin Tryptophan aromatic radical network).*

**13.4 Thermodynamic Constraints on Coherence**

**13.4.1 Conditional Landauer Bookkeeping for the Historical Rate Scenario**
Critics of quantum biology correctly identify **Thermal Noise** ($k_B T$) as the primary obstacle. At $310$ K, the decoherence time of a dipole in bulk water is $\tau_{raw} \approx 10^{-13}$ s; this bulk-water scale is a contextual control, not a measured tubulin-Trp $T_2$. Landauer's Principle bounds logically irreversible erasure; applying one erasure cost per hypothesized sampling update is an explicit scenario assumption, not evidence that a Zeno Drive samples, erases or operates at a particular rate.

**13.4.2 Heat-Sink Closure Status**

The thermodynamic heat-sink mechanism for the Zeno energy-balance remains an Open Problem; see App ORQ O.34.
Our thermodynamic audit compares two sampling regimes against the $\sim 1$ nW [Tier 3 — neurophysiology measurement] metabolic budget of a neuron. At $310$ K the Landauer erasure cost is $k_B T\ln 2 \approx 2.97\times10^{-21}$ J, so that budget supports about $3.4\times10^{11}$ logically irreversible bit erasures per second. An electronic-THz architecture that erases one bit per sampled degree of freedom per cycle is excluded even for a single bit. At $10^8$ Hz the same assumption permits at most $N_{\max}\approx3370$ independently erased bits; it does not select 100 MHz over lower frequencies. The 100 MHz figure is the historical material-scan scenario; it is not derived from this budget, nor from the recombination rate of §13.4.4 (a rate in s$^{-1}$, not a cyclic frequency). On the conditional $N_{\rm coop}=1.625\times10^9$ branch, one erasure per oscillator per cycle would require $1.625\times10^{17}$ erasures s$^{-1}$, exceeding the Landauer budget by $4.8\times10^5$. Even replacing the linear count by $\sqrt{N_{\rm coop}}$ would give $4.0\times10^4>3370$ and would not be justified by Landauer's linear bit-erasure accounting. The coherence protocol must therefore establish a QND/reversible implementation with an explicit reset and heat-sink budget; this thermodynamic closure remains open under O.34 [Tier 3].
**13.4.3 Tubulin Tryptophan Aromatic Radical Coherence**

Standard bulk water decoherence timescales ($\sim 10^{-13}$ s) define the thermal decoherence limit for unbound spins. The tubulin Trp radical-pair $T_2 \approx 1$-$10\ \mu$s baseline is a model-derived estimate (Tier 3) extrapolated from cryptochrome FAD-Trp radical-pair magnetoreception studies (Ritz et al. 2000; Hore & Mouritsen 2016) and microtubule radical-pair theoretical models (Zadeh-Haghighi & Simon 2022). Direct EPR/ODMR measurements on intact β-tubulin Trp radical pairs have NOT been performed; this direct measurement is a target of the in-vitro arm of Protocol A (Protocol A-Prime is the abiotic NV surrogate; App ORQ O.24 tracks the A-Prime enhancement amplitude). **Open Problem O.23** in Appendix ORQ asks whether a declared material model can extend a measured baseline toward the historical $\sim 10$ ms stress target (§13.4.4–§13.4.7, V1 §17.1.3c). No extension time is presently required by Selection or Level II.

**The Misra-Sudarshan formula and its applicability range [Tier 1 statement / Tier 3 application to Trp].**

The Misra-Sudarshan quantum Zeno theorem (Misra & Sudarshan 1977, *J. Math. Phys.* 18:756; reviewed in Facchi & Pascazio 2008, *J. Phys. A: Math. Theor.* 41:493001 §2.1) states that, for a quantum system prepared in $|\psi_0\rangle$ and subjected to projective measurements at interval $\tau_{Zeno}$, the effective decay rate in the short-interval limit is

$$\gamma_{\text{eff}}(\tau_{Zeno}) = \tau_{Zeno}/\tau_Z^2 \quad (\tau_{Zeno} \to 0),$$

where the **Zeno time** $\tau_Z$ is defined by the variance of the interaction Hamiltonian in the initial state:

$$\tau_Z^{-2}\equiv\frac{\sigma_H^2}{\hbar^2},\qquad \sigma_H^2\equiv\langle H^2\rangle-\langle H\rangle^2.$$
The survival-probability curvature fixes this time uniquely: $P(t)=1-(\sigma_Ht/\hbar)^2+O(t^4)$, hence $\tau_Z=\hbar/\sigma_H$. If the variance is quoted as a cyclic frequency $\Delta\nu_H\equiv\sigma_H/h$, then $\tau_Z=1/(2\pi\Delta\nu_H)$; using $1/\Delta\nu_H$ in the quadratic formula would inflate every squared-$\tau_Z$ result by $(2\pi)^2\approx39.5$.

Equivalently, the effective coherence time is $\tau_{\text{eff}} = \tau_Z^2/\tau_{Zeno}$. Within the manuscript's quadratic-to-exponential matching diagnostic, the nominal boundary is $\tau_{Zeno}<\tau^*\equiv\tau_Z^2/T_2$. Facchi, Nakazato & Pascazio (2001, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 86:2699, eq. 16) instead obtain $\tau^*\simeq\gamma_0\tau_Z^2$ for a golden-rule population-decay rate $\gamma_0$, while Facchi & Pascazio (2008 §2.2.5, eq. 19) define the crossover implicitly by $\gamma_{\rm eff}(\tau^*)=\gamma$. Identifying $\gamma_0=1/T_2$ is an additional Tier 3 channel-matching assumption, not a result of either source.

The Zeno time $\tau_Z$ and the exponential decoherence time $T_2$ are distinct physical quantities and *cannot in general be identified*: $\tau_Z$ is the convexity scale of the short-time survival probability (set by $\langle H_{int}^2 \rangle$), while $T_2$ is the long-time exponential dephasing rate (set by spin-bath spectral density). The two are related only via the crossover relation $\tau^* = \tau_Z^2/T_2$.

For the Trp radical-pair singlet, the relevant $H_{int}$ is the singlet–triplet hyperfine mixing $H_{hf}$. The engine's declared placeholder for the bare radical-pair variance is $\sigma_H/h = 30$ MHz (the FAD-derived rms of §13.1.2b; the TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ effective coupling $\approx27$ MHz would give $\tau_Z\approx5.85$ ns), so the Zeno time is

$$\tau_Z=\frac{1}{2\pi(30\,\text{MHz})}\approx5.305\ \text{ns}\quad\text{[Tier 3 — imported hyperfine placeholder].}$$

The bare Misra-Sudarshan formula evaluated at the canonical $\tau_{Zeno} = 10$ ns measurement benchmark gives

$$\tau_{\text{eff}}^{\text{bare MS}} = \tau_Z^2/\tau_{Zeno} \approx 2.8\ \text{ns}.$$

This **out-of-quadratic-regime diagnostic extrapolation of the single-pair bare Zeno formula is more than six orders below the $\sim 10$ ms declared stress target** used for Protocol A-Prime (§13.3.5) and Protocol D (Chapter 16), and more than four orders below the auxiliary $100\ \mu$s benchmark. The correct $\hbar/\sigma_H$ definition therefore widens rather than softens the disclosed coherence gap. The Misra-Sudarshan formula applied to the bare radical-pair Hamiltonian alone does *not* generate those declared material times. **Open Problem O.23** retains possible ordinary protected-subspace models (§13.4.5 dissipative-Zeno scaling; V1 §17.1.3c chiral phonon-polariton Decoherence-Free Subspace); none is a required or established GCT mechanism.

### 13.4.4 Spin-Selective Radical Recombination [Tier 3]

The candidate biochemical architecture is an ATP-coupled redox regeneration loop for Tryptophan (Trp) aromatic radical pairs in the β-tubulin hydrophobic pocket. The spin chemistry itself is standard radical-pair physics: the pair oscillates between Singlet (S) and Triplet (T) states via hyperfine coupling $\omega_{hf}$, and recombination back to the ground state is spin-selective, with the Singlet channel recombining at $\Gamma_{rec} \sim 10^8\ \text{s}^{-1}$ (a rate, not a 100 MHz cyclic frequency) while Triplet recombination is suppressed (Steiner & Ulrich 1989 *Chem. Rev.* 89:51). What is **not yet established** is the upstream biochemical pump that repeatedly prepares the Trp radical-pair state in tubulin under physiological conditions. ATP hydrolysis supplies the metabolic free-energy budget for the neural machinery and can in principle support local electron-transfer / redox cycling through mitochondrial and protein-pocket cofactors, but the explicit chain "ATP hydrolysis $\to$ electron donor/acceptor reset $\to$ beta-tubulin Trp radical-pair regeneration" is a closure target, not a demonstrated mechanism. The present chapter therefore treats ATP-coupled radical-pair regeneration as a **Tier 3 candidate mechanism** registered under App ORQ Open Problem O.34; the historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario was associated with the spin-selective recombination / hyperfine-mixing timescale ($\Gamma_{rec}\sim10^8$ s$^{-1}$), not with a derived ATP-hydrolysis clock. Even if measured in tubulin, a $10^8$ s$^{-1}$ recombination rate would be ordinary spin chemistry, not a Zeno Drive, phason rate or Selection-Operator clock.

A "WGM Cavity Bootstrap" reading of the historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario — in which an acoustic cavity resonance at 100 MHz is imagined to *project* the spin state — does not hold. A deterministic coherent coupling (cavity or otherwise) at 100 MHz produces reversible Rabi oscillations; its frequency is not a measurement rate. Strong unitary coupling can confine dynamics to Zeno subspaces (Facchi & Pascazio 2002, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 89:080401), but that protection scales with the coupling strength (e.g. the Rabi amplitude in spin locking), not with the drive frequency. The spin-selective recombination, by contrast, is a genuinely non-unitary Lindblad channel that depletes the singlet population irreversibly; the question is whether this Lindblad channel produces an *effective measurement* with strong-Zeno scaling in the parameter regime realized for Trp at 310 K.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Status of the historical coherence-extension scenario.** For parity with `protocol_decoherence_audit.py`, the bare radical-pair audit uses $\sigma_H/h\approx30$ MHz, $\Gamma_{rec}\approx10^8$ s$^{-1}$, $\omega_{hf}=\sigma_H/\hbar=2\pi(30\,\text{MHz})$, $\gamma_{\text{leak}}\sim\omega_{hf}^2/\Gamma_{rec}$, and $\tau_{\text{eff}}^{\text{bare}}\sim\Gamma_{rec}/\omega_{hf}^2\approx2.8\times10^{-9}$ s. The recombination rate is already in s$^{-1}$ and is not multiplied by $2\pi$. This bare channel is more than four orders below the auxiliary $\sim 100\,\mu$s–$1$ ms benchmark band and more than six orders below the declared $10$ ms stress target (App BEB); neither target is a Selection or Level-II requirement, and consistent angular/cyclic conventions do not move the bare result near them. Reaching them in a material system would require a *protected-subspace* model that suppresses the off-diagonal coupling $\Omega$ in the dissipative-Zeno scaling well below the bare hyperfine angular frequency. The chiral phonon-polariton Decoherence-Free Subspace of V1 §17.1.3c, in which an orbital-angular-momentum mismatch between a chiral phonon-polariton mode (carrying OAM) and the symmetric thermal phonon bath (lacking OAM) would suppress $\Omega_{\text{DFS}}$, is only a Tier 3 material model: its modes, bath symmetry, preparation and suppression rate are unmeasured, and OAM mismatch does not by itself derive a protected subspace. **App ORQ Open Problem O.23** therefore asks for an ordinary material Hamiltonian, full dissipator set and measured response; it is not a missing physical mechanism that must close for Selection or Level II.

**Two-layer candidate architecture.** The proposed CISS channel of §13.2.3 is modeled separately from long-lived radical-pair coherence. Chirality and an available charge-transfer/transport handle are candidate controls, not established necessary or sufficient conditions for a phason-winding channel or substrate status; Naaman, Paltiel & Waldeck (2019) establish the CISS empirical class, not GCT's tubulin-to-phason map. The Zeno layer is a candidate multiplier conditional on O.23. Positive or negative results constrain this architecture but do not establish an Identity Polaron or Level II; the typed coupling and independent phenomenal bridge remain open.

**Proxy-branch rejection condition.** If pulsed EPR measurements on intact β-tubulin yield $T_2 < 1\ \mu$s under physiological conditions, the registered long-coherence radical-pair branch is unsupported even before any coherence-extension scenario is invoked, and the spin/coherence layer of §13.2.3 carries no Zeno enhancement. Ordinary CISS response would then constrain the material system only; it is not a fallback that preserves the branch. A preregistered null on Protocol A-Prime *and*, once a powered gate exists, Protocol D, combined with $T_2 < 1\ \mu$s on Trp radical pairs in vitro, jointly rejects the registered biophysical substrate branch of this chapter as registered. Neither outcome is a verdict on GCT as a whole: the measurement tests an ordinary material proxy, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3); in particular it would not prove Level II absent, because the Level-II bridge is independently open and the Level II status is already open (Tier 3). V1 Ch17 carries the corresponding substrate-scope statement.

**Historical thermal-margin scenario [Tier 3; not an adopted interaction].** At physiological temperature, the biological thermal scale is $k_B T(310\,{\rm K}) = 8.617333262145\times10^{-5}\,{\rm eV/K}\times310 = 0.0267$ eV. $E_{\text{bio\_phason}}$ is this thermal-noise scale, not a separate eV-scale binding energy. The historical scenario required a candidate Rashba-phason coupling $E_{RP}\approx0.3$ eV to exceed it by at least a factor of ten. Protocol `protocol_rashba_phason.py` reports $E_{RP}/k_BT \approx 11$ only as arithmetic on declared Tier 3 inputs, and computes from the $A_5$ character table that the Eq. (17.3) cross-product coupling is not an icosahedral scalar for the vector phason (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3). The comparison is therefore retained only as a historical external-energy scenario; it is not a testable GCT phason prediction. As a thermal margin it is also withdrawn: without a type-correct, action-normalized coupling, $E_{RP}$ cannot be compared with $k_BT$ (Firewall §3 rule 6). Thermal perturbations (fever, anaesthetics) remain ordinary material controls for the coherence measurements of Chapter 16.

**13.4.5 Lindblad Treatment of the Tubulin Trp Open Quantum System [Tier 3]**

To formalize the open-system dynamics of the Trp radical pair at 310 K we deploy the Lindblad master equation:

$$ \frac{d\rho}{dt} = -\frac{i}{\hbar}[\hat{H}_{radical}, \rho] + \sum_i \gamma_i \mathcal{D}(\hat{\sigma}_-^i)\rho + \Gamma_{rec}\,\mathcal{D}(\hat{S}_{recomb})\rho, $$

where $\hat{H}_{radical}$ contains the hyperfine mixing $\omega_{hf}$, $\gamma_i = 1/T_2 \approx 10^5$ s$^{-1}$ [Tier 3 — model-derived import/extrapolation from cryptochrome/FAD-Trp radical-pair systems and microtubule radical-pair models; direct β-tubulin EPR/ODMR remains O.24] is the bare thermal spin decay, and $\Gamma_{rec} \sim 10^8$ s$^{-1}$ is the spin-selective recombination rate [Tier 3 — Trp radical-pair chemistry]. Here $\mathcal{D}(\hat{L})\rho = \hat{L}\rho\hat{L}^\dagger - \tfrac{1}{2}\{\hat{L}^\dagger\hat{L},\rho\}$, and $\hat{S}_{recomb}$ is defined as a jump from the radical-pair spin manifold into an explicit product/sink state (e.g. $|P\rangle\langle S|$, with channel sums when singlet/triplet products are both retained). On the enlarged radical-plus-product Hilbert space this is a CPTP Lindblad evolution; if the product/sink sector is traced out and only unrecombined radical pairs are retained, the reduced radical-pair equation is a trace-nonincreasing conditional master equation.

In the strong-coupling continuous-measurement limit (Facchi & Pascazio 2008 *J. Phys. A* 41:493001 §13.3), a dissipator of rate $\Gamma$ pinning a system into one of its eigenspaces suppresses leakage from the protected subspace at a rate $\gamma_{\text{leak}} \sim |\Omega|^2/\Gamma$, where $\Omega$ is the off-diagonal coupling to the leakage channel. **Unit guard:** $\Delta E/h$ and $\nu$ are cyclic frequencies in Hz; $\Omega$ and Lindblad rates are angular rates in rad/s. The dissipative-Zeno comparison converts with $\Omega=2\pi\nu$ before comparing or squaring rates. Applied to the Trp recombination dissipator with $\Omega = \omega_{hf} = 2\pi\times30\ \text{MHz} \approx 1.9\times10^8$ rad/s (the $\Delta_{ST}/h \approx 30$ MHz hyperfine band) and $\Gamma = \Gamma_{rec} \sim 10^8$ s$^{-1}$, this gives

$$ \tau_{\text{eff}}^{\text{dissipative}} = 1/\gamma_{\text{leak}} \sim \Gamma_{rec}/\omega_{hf}^2 \approx 2.8\times10^{-9}\ \text{s} = 2.8\ \text{ns}, $$

i.e., the dissipative-Zeno scaling recovers the same order-of-magnitude estimate as the pulsed Misra-Sudarshan formula of §13.4.3. The radical-pair recombination channel acting alone — whether interpreted as a continuous Lindblad dissipator or as a stroboscopic projective measurement — does *not* extend the Trp coherence time toward the historical 10 ms material-coherence target used for Protocol A-Prime / Protocol D. That target is not a Selection or Level-II requirement.

**Historical shielding-factor scenario.** The Trp radical pair lives inside the hydrophobic pocket and is not in bulk water; its decoherence channel is the singlet-triplet hyperfine interaction, with a model-derived imported baseline $T_2 \approx 1$–$10\ \mu$s extrapolated from cryptochrome/FAD-Trp systems and radical-pair models rather than direct β-tubulin measurement (Ritz et al. 2000; Hore & Mouritsen 2016; O.24). Taking $\tau_{\text{target}} \sim 10$ ms as a declared stress-test target defines

$$S_{\text{required}} = \frac{\tau_{\text{target}}}{\tau_{\text{base}}} \;\sim\; \frac{10^{-2}\ \text{s}}{10^{-5}\ \text{s}} = 10^3,$$
where $\tau_{\text{base}}\approx10\,\mu$s is the imported radical-pair baseline (distinct from the bulk-water $\tau_{raw}\approx10^{-13}$ s of §13.4.1).

The resulting $10^3$ ratio is arithmetic for that chosen material scenario. The $\sim 10^9$ shielding figure occasionally quoted in the warm-decoherence literature instead compares with an unrelated bulk-water scale ($\tau_{bulk} \sim 10^{-13}$ s). Neither is a GCT or Polaron requirement. **Open Problem O.23** asks whether any specified ordinary protected-subspace model can produce a measured enhancement and with what mechanism (§13.4.6, V1 §17.1.3c).

**13.4.6 Partial Floquet-Lindblad Master Equation for the Open Zeno System [Tier 3]**

The Misra-Sudarshan formula isolates the quantum system from its environment. To model the Tubulin Trp radical pair at 310 K coupled to a protein spin bath, the current manuscript uses a **partial Floquet-Lindblad scaffold** for the open quantum system (OQS) density matrix $\rho$:

$$ \frac{d\rho}{dt} = -\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_{\rm eff}, \rho] + \sum_k \left( L_k \rho L_k^\dagger - \frac{1}{2}\{L_k^\dagger L_k, \rho\} \right) $$

where the Floquet driving Hamiltonian $H_F(t)$ is defined in energy units:
$$ H_F(t) = \frac{\Delta_{ST}}{2}\sigma_z + \hbar\Omega \cos(2\pi \nu_d t)\sigma_x, $$
with $\Delta_{ST}=h(30\,\mathrm{MHz})$ (so $\Delta_{ST}/h \approx 30 \text{ MHz}$) as the engine's bare singlet-triplet placeholder (an FAD-derived external material-scenario input, §13.1.2b) and $\nu_d$ as an applied laboratory drive frequency. Equivalently, in angular-frequency units one may write $K_F(t)=H_F(t)/\hbar=(\Delta_{ST}/2\hbar)\sigma_z+\Omega\cos(2\pi\nu_d t)\sigma_x$ and $d\rho/dt=-i[K_{\rm eff},\rho]+\cdots$. The Protocol A-Prime branch frequencies ($112 \pm 10$ MHz if O.12 closes positive; $42 \pm 10$ MHz if O.12 closes negative) are historical proxy scan windows, not replacements for the bare $\Delta_{ST}$ value; O.12 does not establish them as operating frequencies, and they are not GCT rates.

The environmental spin-bath coupling retained in this scaffold is defined by three Lindblad jump operators $L_k$:
* $L_1 = \sqrt{\gamma_\uparrow}\sigma_+$ (Thermal excitation)
* $L_2 = \sqrt{\gamma_\downarrow}\sigma_-$ (Thermal relaxation)
* $L_3 = \sqrt{\gamma_\phi/2}\sigma_z$ (Pure dephasing)

where detailed balance enforces $\gamma_\uparrow / \gamma_\downarrow = \exp(-\Delta_{ST} / k_B T)$ — $\Delta_{ST}$ is an energy, so no factor of $\hbar$ enters; written with the angular splitting $\omega_{ST} = \Delta_{ST}/\hbar$ the same relation reads $\exp(-\hbar\omega_{ST}/k_B T)$ — and the dephasing rate is $\gamma_\phi = 1/T_2^*$. 

This is not the full dissipator set for hydrated tubulin at 310 K. Omitted channels include spin-selective singlet/triplet recombination into explicit product/sink states, hyperfine anisotropy, dipolar nuclear-spin bath fluctuations, vibrational relaxation of the Trp pocket, solvent/electrostatic noise, and any O.23 chiral-phonon-polariton dark-state jump structure. Those channels are closure targets for O.23/O.24 and for the in-vitro arm of Protocol A, not solved inputs here.

Within this declared open-system scaffold, transforming into the Floquet rotating frame defines a **scenario factor** $\eta_F \in (0, 1]$ for the effective coherence time of the open driven system:
$$ \tau_{eff}^F = \tau_{eff}^{\text{bare}} \cdot \eta_F \quad \text{where} \quad \eta_F = \frac{1}{1 + (\gamma_\phi \cdot T_2)^2 \cdot f(\Delta_{drive} / \Delta_{ST})}, $$

where the baseline $\tau_{eff}^{\text{bare}}$ must be supplied by a measured or separately justified material model (the bare Misra-Sudarshan estimate of §13.4.3 alone gives $\tau_{eff}^{\text{bare MS}} \approx 2.8$ ns from radical-pair recombination, well below the $\sim 10$ ms declared stress target; a hypothetical chiral phonon-polariton Decoherence-Free Subspace lifetime $\tau_{eff}^{\text{DFS}}$ of V1 §17.1.3c could be inserted only as an O.23 scenario). Inserting either baseline produces scenario curves only; no baseline is currently a GCT coherence-extension mechanism.

At ordinary driven two-level resonance, $\nu_d = \Delta_{ST}/h$, the declared detuning function gives $f \to 0$ and $\eta_F \to 1$; off resonance the Floquet factor multiplicatively suppresses the supplied baseline. This conditional algebra does not identify a geometric or phason resonance.

> **Conditional material-model resonance:**
> The declared two-level Floquet factor is maximized algebraically at $\nu_d = \Delta_{ST}/h \approx 30 \text{ MHz}$ once that material Hamiltonian is supplied. Protocol A-Prime tests both historical proxy windows under the single F1 rule: Branch A at $112 \pm 10$ MHz and Branch B at $42 \pm 10$ MHz. A single-branch null routes to O.12/O.23 branch interpretation; the surrogate-level F1 gate requires the three-conjunct proxy-branch null after S0-S7 acceptance checks: no Branch A peak, no Branch B peak, and no chirality contrast. That null rejects only the registered proxy branch; it is not a framework gate or a GCT frequency prediction. The 150 MHz sign remains a Tier 3 mechanism diagnostic rather than an F1 conjunct.

*For the bare inverse-Zeno diagnostic of the radical-pair recombination channel see **App BEB §BEB.7** and **App BEB §BEB.12**; the former reading of the A-Prime drive frequency as a Zeno sampling rate is a declared open programme (§13.4.7).*

**13.4.7 The Zeno/Anti-Zeno Crossover and the Drive-Window Logic [Tier 3; declared open programme]**

**Conditional open-system comparison:**

Within the short-time quadratic model used above, equating the effective rate $\gamma_{\rm eff}(\tau_{Zeno}) = \tau_{Zeno}/\tau_Z^2$ to the bare exponential rate $1/T_2$ locates a crossover at $\tau^* = \tau_Z^2/T_2$, equivalently the crossover frequency

$$\nu^* = 1/\tau^* = T_2/\tau_Z^2.$$

This identity is a diagnostic of that model rather than a general result. Misra & Sudarshan (1977) establish the limiting Zeno dynamics, and Facchi & Pascazio (2008 §2.2.5) define a Zeno/anti-Zeno crossover implicitly by $\gamma_{\rm eff}(\tau^*) = \gamma$ where a finite intersection exists; neither identifies $\tau^*$ with $\tau_Z^2/T_2$ nor guarantees anti-Zeno behaviour beyond it, and the same review cautions that $\tau_Z$ can misestimate the quadratic interval. The sign assignments below therefore hold only within the quadratic model and its assumed spectral density. Here $\nu_{\text{sample}}$ is the rate of a physical measurement channel (for example recombination); an applied drive frequency is not such a rate.

- For $\nu_{\text{sample}} > \nu^*$ (Zeno regime): measurement *suppresses* decoherence — coherence time increases.
- For $\nu_{\text{sample}} < \nu^*$ (Anti-Zeno regime): measurement *accelerates* decoherence — coherence time decreases.

The crossover depends on both the Zeno time $\tau_Z$ (variance of the interaction Hamiltonian) and the exponential dephasing time $T_2$. For Tubulin Trp radical pairs with the engine's $\sigma_H/h \approx 30$ MHz placeholder [Tier 3 — FAD-derived rms placeholder, within ~10% of the TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ effective coupling, §13.1.2b] and $T_2 \approx 10\ \mu$s [Tier 3 — model-derived extrapolation from cryptochrome FAD-Trp radical-pair magnetoreception studies (Ritz 2000, Hore-Mouritsen 2016) plus microtubule radical-pair theoretical models (Zadeh-Haghighi-Simon 2022); direct β-tubulin Trp EPR/ODMR measurement is the closure target of O.24], $\tau_Z\approx5.305$ ns and the quadratic-model bare crossover is $\nu^*\approx3.6\times10^{11}$ Hz, far above the recombination rate $\Gamma_{rec}\approx10^8$ s$^{-1}$. This places the bare single-pair recombination channel in the inverse-Zeno regime relative to the bare hyperfine Hamiltonian, consistent with the §13.4.3 conclusion that the radical-pair channel alone does not extend coherence.

**Declared open programme [Tier 3] — drive-frequency Zeno windows.** (a) *Claimed:* that the applied RF/coil drive frequency $\nu_d$ acts as the Zeno sampling rate, so that the registered A-Prime branch windows sit on the inverse-Zeno side of the bare $\nu^*$ and would move to the Zeno-protected side if an O.23 protected subspace lowered $\nu^*_{\rm DFS}$ into the kHz–MHz band; an in-vitro comparison of $T_2$ in the branch windows against a 50 kHz drive was registered as a decision on the O.23 layer. (b) *Defect:* a coherent drive has no measurement rate (§13.4.4); where strong driving gives Zeno-like protection (spin locking, Zeno subspaces), it scales with the Rabi amplitude, not with $\nu_d$. The mapping $\nu_d\to\nu_{\text{sample}}$ is a category error, so no Zeno/anti-Zeno side can be assigned to any drive window, and the 50 kHz comparison decides nothing. (c) *Closing would need:* a physical measurement channel whose rate is tuned (e.g. an optical or recombination readout rate), or a restatement of the windows as dynamical-decoupling filter frequencies probing a noise spectral density. (d) Nothing downstream uses this window logic as support: the A-Prime F1 rule (§13.3.5) does not depend on it, and the former 50 kHz decision rule is withdrawn.

**13.5 The $\eta_{Zeno}$ Scenario Calculator (Formal Definition; Non-Diagnostic)**

The preceding sections specified the Zeno Drive piece by piece — the Tavis-Cummings cooperative pumping condition (§13.1.2), the candidate magnon-polaron origin of the registered $\nu_c \approx 112 \pm 10$ MHz window (§13.1.2b; Tier 3 specific value), the open-system Floquet-Lindblad correction (§13.4.6), and the substrate-discriminant logic of Protocol A-Prime (§13.3.5). The present section assembles these into a single closed-form procedure that returns a scalar $\eta_{Zeno}$ given a substrate description, so that past engine outputs remain reproducible. It computes a dimensionless rate ratio **only after all rates and model gates are supplied externally**; it does not derive a GCT material coupling, classify a substrate or measure consciousness.

**The DMC legs are candidate missing-leg controls, not an Apperception gate.** Non-zero nuclear spin and molecular chirality motivate controlled comparisons for the proposed phason channel, but neither is established as necessary or sufficient for Level II. The former $g_{single}^{eff}$, $\eta_{Zeno}$, and $N_{coh}$ numbers are retained below only as conditional external-rate scenarios. O.21, O.23, O.34, a typed and normalized coupling, and an independent phenomenal bridge remain open; therefore no material descriptor executes a zero-coupling inference or categorical substrate verdict.

The procedure is computationally **tractable** on a small set of declared substrate variables — nuclear-spin lattice, molecular chirality, Tavis-Cummings cavity parameters, vibrational thermal-bath coupling — and is implemented as a chain of five documented functions in the GCT Physics Engine (`GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_eta_zeno.py`), a conditional scenario calculator whose outputs audit supplied arithmetic rather than physical verdicts. Engine-generated values for the three scenario test cases (biological tubulin, $^{28}$Si silicon, NV-centre Protocol-A-Prime surrogate) are quoted in §13.5.7 below.

**13.5.1 The Chain (Formal Statement)**

$$
\boxed{\;\eta_{Zeno} \;\equiv\; \underbrace{\frac{g_{single}^{\,eff}\,\sqrt{N_{bio}}}{\kappa}}_{\eta_{TC}\ \text{(bare Tavis-Cummings ratio)}} \;\cdot\; \underbrace{\eta_F}_{\text{Floquet correction}}\;}
$$

with the chain of dependencies

$$
\underbrace{(\hat{I},\,\chi,\,\mu_{dip},\,m_{eff},\,\omega_d,\,a_{lat},\,\phi^{n})}_{\text{substrate}} \;\xrightarrow{\;\text{Step 1}\;}\; g_{single}^{\,eff} \;\xrightarrow{\;\text{Step 4}\;}\; \eta_{TC}
$$
$$
N_{coop}\;\xrightarrow{\;\text{Step 2}\;}\;\sqrt{N_{bio}} \qquad (\omega_d,\,\phi^{-18},\,N) \xrightarrow{\;\text{Step 3}\;} \kappa
$$
$$
(\gamma_\phi,\,T_2,\,\Delta_{drive},\,\Delta_{ST}) \;\xrightarrow{\;\text{Step 5}\;}\; \eta_F.
$$

Each step is a closed-form expression conditional on declared Tier-3 inputs. DMC descriptors annotate candidate-control comparisons at Step 1; they do not derive $g_{single}^{eff}$, set it to zero, or execute a Level-II decision. Zero and non-zero rates below are explicit legacy external-rate scenarios retained for sensitivity bookkeeping.

**13.5.2 Step 1 — Single-Dipole Coupling $g_{single}$ [Tier 3 scenario form and inputs]**

The historical scenario form wrote the single-dipole coupling to the phason mode as the substrate's chiral dipole transition acting on a phason zero-point electric field, attenuated by the RT-shell geometric gradient and the phason zero-point displacement. This expression has no valid action-level provenance and does not by itself define a rate (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3); it is retained only to identify the engine path, and 38.3 MHz and all overlap-propagated descendants are external scenario values:

$$
g_{single}^{\,eff} \;=\; \chi \cdot f_{\text{overlap}}\cdot \frac{\mu_{dip}\,E_{\text{phason}}^{\,zpf}}{\hbar} \cdot \frac{\phi^{\,n}}{a_{lat}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2\,m_{eff}\,\omega_d}},
$$

with $E_{\text{phason}}^{\,zpf} = \sqrt{\hbar\,\omega_d / (2\,m_{eff})}$ (as written this has units of velocity, not electric field, so the displayed form is dimensionally incomplete and does not define a rate) and $\chi \in \{+1,-1,0\}$ the chirality sign ($\chi = 0$ for achiral in this scenario form; a missing-leg control, not a derived zero coupling). The exponent $n = -9$ is imported from the lattice-speed relation $\hat c=\phi^{-9}$ (V2 §6.2.2): only the integer (half of the Tier 2 $D=18$) is Tier 2, while its reading as the lattice speed of light is the Tier 3 P3b / O.15(b) stiffness-map hypothesis (V2 Ch06 §6.2.2), and its appearance in this coupling belongs to the Tier 3 scenario form (V1 §17.1.3); the dipole moment $\mu_{dip}$, overlap fraction $f_{\text{overlap}}$, and effective mass $m_{eff}$ are Tier 3 substrate inputs. For the canonical tubulin substrate, Appendix GPE retains the external pre-overlap scenario anchor $g_{single}\approx38.3$ MHz. The operative $\eta_{\rm Zeno}$ branch applies $f_{\rm overlap}$ to that anchor: at the engine-current $f_{\rm overlap}=0.01$, $g_{single}^{eff}=3.83\times10^5$ Hz, with the overlap-propagated plausible range $3.8\times10^3$-$3.8\times10^5$ Hz. Unless explicitly labelled "pre-overlap anchor," downstream $\eta_{\rm Zeno}$ and $N_{\rm coh}$ quotes use the overlap-propagated coupling.

**13.5.3 Step 2 — Collective Enhancement $\sqrt{N_{\rm coop}}$ [Tier 3 input]**

The Tavis-Cummings cooperative pumping enhances the coupling by $\sqrt{N_{\rm coop}}$, where $N_{\rm coop}$ counts primary oscillators phase-locked to the cavity mode within the Polaron volume. The primary oscillator basis is the beta-tubulin Trp radical-pair inventory,
$$N_{\rm coop}=N_{\beta{\rm Trp}}\times n_{\rm rp}\times f_{\rm active},$$
where $N_{\beta{\rm Trp}}$ is the beta-Trp candidate count, $n_{\rm rp}$ is the number of assembled-MT radical-pair hosts per dimer, and $f_{\rm active}$ is the phase-locked active fraction. Hydration-shell spins, including OH and proton dipoles, are bath/environment degrees of freedom: they can dress the protected subspace and enter O.23/O.33 decoherence and isotope-systematics budgets, but they are not counted in the cooperative-oscillator basis. The operative central branch remains $n_{\rm rp}=0$ pending O.21 assembled-MT lumen-axis closure; the $n_{\rm rp}=1$ sensitivity branch uses the conservative beta-Trp inventory (the $1.625\times10^9$ spin-count tracked in `protocol_zeno_energy_budget.py`) and reports any hydration contribution separately as environmental dressing, not as additional Tavis-Cummings oscillators. For a single-NV Protocol A-Prime surrogate: $N_{\rm coop} = 1$. The $\sqrt N$ factor describes collective coupling, not thermodynamic erasure cost. Any implementation that irreversibly erases one bit per oscillator per cycle of the historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario exceeds the 1 nW Landauer budget by $4.8\times10^5$ on the sensitivity branch; a QND/reversible sampling and reset model is required under O.34 [Tier 3 thermodynamic closure condition].

**13.5.4 Step 3 — Cavity Decay Rate $\kappa$ [Tier 3 P3b insertion or Tier 3 measured]**

Two parallel modes are exposed because biological and engineered substrates declare $\kappa$ differently:

*Historical biological scenario ("geometric" mode).* The engine inserts the Tier 3 stiffness-map hypothesis P3b, $K_\perp / K_\parallel = \phi^{-18}$ (only the integer $D = 18$ is Tier 2; V2 Ch04 §4.2, V3 §13.1.2), acting on the Tier 3 cage posit of $N_{cage} = 144$ nodes:
$$
\kappa^{\text{geom}} \;=\; \phi^{-18}\,\frac{\omega_d}{N_{cage}}.
$$
For a $100$ MHz cyclic reference, $\kappa_{\rm cav}\approx120.19$ Hz; at the operative $112$ MHz branch used by the engine, $\kappa_{\rm cav}=134.610$ Hz. Here $\kappa_{\rm cav}$ is reported as a cyclic linewidth, consistently with cyclic $g_{single}^{eff}$. These numbers are external scenario outputs, not derived tubulin linewidths.

*Direct mode (engineered cavity).* For NV-centre / cavity-QED surrogates, $\kappa$ is the directly measured linewidth ($\sim 1$ MHz for current NV cavities).

**13.5.5 Step 4 — Bare Tavis-Cummings Ratio $\eta_{TC}$ [conditional algebra; Tier 3 inputs]**

$$
\eta_{TC} \;=\; \frac{g_{single}^{\,eff}\sqrt{N_{bio}}}{\kappa}.
$$

This is dimensionless algebra when $g$ and $\kappa$ are supplied in the same rate convention. It carries no substrate or phenomenal verdict.

**13.5.6 Step 5 — Floquet Open-System Correction $\eta_F$ [Tier 3, V3 §13.4.6]**

The declared Floquet-Lindblad scaffold for the open quantum system at 310 K defines a scenario factor $\eta_F \in (0,1]$:

$$
\eta_F \;=\; \frac{1}{1 + (\gamma_\phi\,T_2)^2\,f(\Delta_{drive}/\Delta_{ST})},
$$

with $f(x) = x^2/(1+x^2)$ a Lorentzian detuning function that vanishes on resonance. At ordinary driven resonance $\nu_d = \Delta_{ST}/h$, $\eta_F \to 1$. Off resonance, $\eta_F < 1$ multiplicatively suppresses the bare Tavis-Cummings ratio. It is a model factor for an ordinary driven open system, not a geometric resonance or a Selection-Operator efficiency; it is the same $\eta_F$ that appears in the Protocol A-Prime $T_2(\nu_d)$ scenario profile of §13.3.5 (for the bare $\Delta_{ST}$ it peaks at 30 MHz, below the scan, and does not shape the branch-window peak, §13.3.5; the table's $\eta_F = 1$ assumes the O.12-positive renormalisation).
