Postdiction rows use POSTDICTION-CONSISTENT and constitute alignment-check evidence, not prospective falsification-surviving detections.** Rows whose Tier cell carries "Tier 4 as evidence" are φ-formula matches: as evidence that φ or icosahedral structure is special, each such match is **Tier 4**, because the preregistered constant control test (v3, NEGATIVE-FRAGILE; App PSC §PSC.9.6) found φ's pattern of matches on 21 constants not distinguishable from that of random constants (58 of 300 random bases did at least as well). The test "excludes, at power ≥ 0.8, an effect in which φ hits at least 6 of the 8 informative rows through a real effect; weaker effects are not excluded." Their numbers are kept as descriptive arithmetic. PENDING-α-RESOLUTION, AT-GATE TENSION, CURRENT-DATA-TENSION, OPEN-CONDITIONAL, PENDING-VERIFIER, and OPEN-RESEARCH do **not** count as in-favor detection evidence. FAIL counts against the framework. Currently the DETECTED total is 0 (0 TIGHT + 0 MARGINAL) out of 75 rows, reflecting that most of the GCT prediction set has its empirical-detection moment in long-horizon observational programmes. The POSTDICTION-CONSISTENT + CONSISTENT + ALGEBRAIC pills together quantify the manuscript's *internal coherence*, not its *empirical confirmation*.

**Verifier status from the scorecard:**
✗ 5 failure rows: four verifier rows outside their registered rule (P.1c, P.16, P.23, P.24) and the registered-menu branch verdict P.6; see the scope disclosure that follows.

**Scope disclosure.** A FAIL row is reported as a failure, not re-described as a success.

- **Row P.1c** — The LOCKED 1000 ppm pre-commitment (config/falsification_thresholds.json) is the binding electron rule. The forward residual m_e = M_P phi^-107 (1 - 5 alpha) vs CODATA 2022 is 1006 ppm, so the row misses the locked rule by 6 ppm and is reported as a FAIL of that rule, not re-described as a success. The 1200 ppm verifier window and the 1500 ppm registry band were set later and are not applied retroactively. Promotion via C.1 / O.14 would have to close the residual before any electron-mass success can be claimed.
- **Row P.6** — Registered-menu closure-to-DESI claim falsified under its registered >3σ rule (DES-Dovekie 3.2σ; DESI DR2 3.1σ BAO+CMB, 2.8–4.2σ with SNe); branch-level verdict. The single-channel phantom template is a separate stipulated coordinate (phantom direction Tier 4, V2 Ch14 §14.3.1). The registered menu is sign-opposite to the DES-Dovekie central target and cannot reach it (protocol_de_multichannel.py CLOSURE-FAILS). The verdict applies to the registered menu, not to GCT as a whole.
- **Row P.16** — Not independent evidence: G = c^3 a_6^2/(4 hbar) with a_6 proportional to phi^-107/m_e, so G scales as m_e^-2 and its residual is the electron Planck-link residual (P.1c) doubled: all-CODATA-alpha branch 2013.345 ppm = (1 + 1006.166 ppm)^2 - 1; model-authoritative alpha_GCT branch 2273.725 ppm = (1 + 1136.217 ppm)^2 - 1. The row therefore carries the P.1c LOCKED 1000 ppm electron rule, which is (1.001)^2 - 1 = 2001 ppm on G, and both branches miss it. It is reported as a FAIL inherited from P.1c, not as an independent pass, while P.1c fails its LOCKED rule; G sits about 90-105 sigma from CODATA's 22 ppm uncertainty (2013.345/22 = 91.5; 2273.725/22 = 103.4).
- **Row P.23** — Tier 2 5/4 coefficient + Tier 3 m_c input → Tier 3 absolute prediction. Prediction 4134.69 MeV vs PDG 2024 m_b(m_b) = 4183 +/- 7 MeV: 6.9 sigma low (more if PDG's +/-7 MeV is read as the 90% CL interval it is labelled as). By the rule applied to the top quark (P.24: outside PDG +/- 5sigma of the prediction) the row is reported as a FAIL. The earlier window 4130-4230 MeV was centred on the measurement, not on the prediction, so it could not test the prediction; it is withdrawn as a test. The residual stays a Tier 3 state-level residual pending O.5, and the mass-scheme question is open.
- **Row P.24** — The written P.24 falsification rule (registered since v1.2.0) is m_t outside the PDG +/- 5sigma gate. The bare value (v_GCT/2) sqrt(2) = 174.07 GeV against the PDG 2024 direct-measurement mass 172.57 +/- 0.29 GeV is 5.18 sigma, so the row misses the written rule and is reported as a FAIL of that rule, by the same standard as the electron LOCKED rule (P.1c), not re-described as a tension. The residual is a Tier 3 state-level/QCD-pole residual pending O.5; a pole/MS-bar uncertainty model would be a new pre-registered band, not applied retroactively. As for P.1c, the version history cannot show whether the rule predates knowledge of the residual. Against PDG's pole mass from cross-section measurements (172.4 +/- 0.7 GeV) the prediction sits at about 2.4 sigma; the mass-scheme question is open, and the comparator registered since v1.2.0 is not swapped after the result, so the FAIL of the written rule stands.

To distinguish empirical detection from algebraic-internal consistency, the Status column uses the following pills. The Evidence Credibility column is normative for all App FSM uses:

| Pill | Meaning | Evidence Credibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **✓ DETECTED-TIGHT** | App PRG row labeled Prediction (material-proxy rows excluded); empirical experiment has run, returned data, and the prediction falls within a tight falsification band (≤1000 ppm). | Counts as in-favor empirical evidence for GCT. |
| **✓ DETECTED-MARGINAL** | App PRG row labeled Prediction; empirical experiment has run, returned data, and the prediction falls within a marginal falsification band (>1000 ppm). | Counts as in-favor empirical evidence with an explicit lower-resolution caveat. |
| **✓ POSTDICTION-CONSISTENT** | Settled-data row used as a postdictive alignment check or dimensional-anchor closure audit. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; firewall-protected alignment only. |
| **✓ CONSISTENT** | Engine-internal algebraic agreement against the registered empirical anchor; the verifier reproduces the manuscript value within tolerance. | Does **not** count as empirical evidence in favor; internal consistency only. |
| **✓ ALGEBRAIC** | Algebraic identity verified at machine precision *or* a forward-looking prediction whose internal-consistency is checked but whose empirical detection target is not yet reached. | Does **not** count as empirical evidence in favor; internal consistency only. |
| **✓ TIER-1 EXACT** | Tier 1 algebraic identity verified at machine precision (e.g. Gram-determinant ratio). | Does **not** count as empirical evidence in favor; theorem/algebra status only. |
| **⚠ TENSION** | Outside the row's verifier precision gate, or a non-falsifying disclosed tension, while inside the registered falsification band (the pill does not by itself imply a σ level; each row states its own). | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence. |
| **⚠ AT-GATE TENSION** | Row-specific tri-state tolerance band: above the pass edge but below the hard-fail edge. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; tension marker only. |
| **△ CURRENT-DATA-TENSION** | DESI DR2 registered-menu closure-fail; Euclid DR1 is reserved for future robustness check. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; flags adverse current data. |
| **⚠ PENDING-α-RESOLUTION** | Detection requires resolution of α-input ambiguity between Cs-α and Rb-α determinations; outcome locked when external α discord resolves. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; input-contingent. |
| **⚠ TENSION UNDER WP2025** | Muon g-2 arbitration row under the WP2025 lattice-dominant HVP synthesis: Tier 2 mechanism + Tier 3 1/5 coefficient + A3 + Tier 4 calibration-survival conjecture; Tension under WP2025; falsification conditional on long-term HVP-synthesis arbitration. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; live tension. |
| **⚠ EVALUATED-CLOSURE-FAILURE** | Closed-form scan completed and the registered closure menu fails; reported separately from observational TENSION. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; failed closure menu. |
| **⚠ PROTECTED-SUBSPACE-REQUIRED** | Row needing O.23 protected-subspace renormalization: either a bare-vs-renormalized frequency channel whose verifier PASS is conditional on that closure, or a declared-open-programme marker with no gate and no PASS (P.44); never direct bare-frequency agreement. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence until O.23 closes and the empirical gate is rerun. |
| **✗ FAIL** | Outside the falsification band — a real falsification event. | Counts as against-GCT evidence. |
| **○ OPEN-RESEARCH** | The registry marks the row with `open_research: true` because the claim is catalogued under an Open Problem (App ORQ §ORQ.5). The verifier output is a candidate-ansatz reference (e.g. literal φ⁻²² evaluation for the Jarlskog invariant) rather than a live Tier 2 prediction. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; future-research target. |
| **○ OPEN-CONDITIONAL** | Verifier/preregistration is executable, but the decisive empirical dataset has not landed, or (for settled-data postdictions such as α, $v$, $m_H$ and $m_p$) the row's Tier 3 derivation handle remains open. | Does **not** count as in-favor evidence; externally undecided. |

A row tagged POSTDICTION-CONSISTENT, CONSISTENT, ALGEBRAIC, or OPEN-CONDITIONAL is **not** an empirical confirmation — it is internal-consistency-checked, postdictively aligned, or executable-but-awaiting-data. Readers comparing the matrix's status pills should treat DETECTED-TIGHT and DETECTED-MARGINAL as the only in-favor empirical-evidence pills, and only for App PRG Prediction rows; PENDING-α-RESOLUTION and all tension/open/verifier-pending pills are non-evidential or adverse as specified above.

### **Appendix TCD: Tier Classification Decision Tree**

**TCD.1 Classification Algorithm**

To maintain the highest standards of scientific integrity, every claim within the GCT framework is subjected to a rigorous **Epistemic Filter**. This decision tree ensures that the reader can distinguish between logical certainties, geometric modeling, and phenomenological calibration.

**Exclusive Tier 0 gate:** The single first-person datum that experience is occurring, i.e. that there is presence now, is Tier 0. It is neither postulated nor derived; doubting or dreaming is itself experience. Exactly this one item belongs to Tier 0; no other claim may ever enter it. Axiom 1 remains the stipulated universal Level I generalisation at Tier 1, motivated by the datum rather than identical to it. The objective-idealist ontology remains a Tier 3 parsimony choice, and Level II substrate verdicts remain open (Tier 3) / `NOT_EVALUATED`. All other claims follow the decision logic below.

**The Decision Logic:**
1. **Does the claim follow necessarily from the Axioms (Presence and Intelligibility) and formal mathematics?**
 * **YES:** Proceed to **Tier 1**.
2. **Is the claim an architectural choice adopted for parsimony and empirical adequacy (not deductively forced by the Ontological Axioms alone), or an exact mathematical consequence that follows once such a choice is assumed?**
 * **YES:** Proceed to **Tier 1/2 (Architectural Postulate + Conditional Mathematics)**. Conditional mathematics never promotes the premise it assumes.
3. **Does the claim depend on the specific Icosahedral Cut-and-Project ansatz ($\mathbb{Z}^6 \to 3D$, organized by the conditional $E_8\to H_4\to H_3$ chain; $\mathbb{Z}^6$ is not a sublattice of $E_8$)?**
 * **YES:** Is the result a structural necessity of that specific geometry?
 * **YES:** Proceed to **Tier 2**.
4. **Does the claim require calibration to empirical data or rely on unproven hydrodynamic assumptions?**
 * **YES:** Proceed to **Tier 3**.
5. **Is the claim an exploratory calculation where the dimensional structure is correct but the numerical coefficient is uncertain by more than one order of magnitude, or an ontological extension outside the core falsifiable theory?**
 * **YES:** Proceed to **Tier 4 (Speculative / Exploratory)**. All Tier 4 numerical claims carry explicit order-of-magnitude bounds and are segregated from the core falsifiable program.

**TCD.2 Tier 1 Results Summary: Logical Necessities**

These results are structural axioms of the framework, standard mathematics, or results inherited from standard physics. They are exact within their stated premises; they are not claims about every intelligible reality. If these results are false, the axiomatic foundation of the theory is flawed. Where an entry's application to GCT rests on a Tier 3 premise (the Wheeler–DeWitt adoption, the knotted-defect premise for $D=3$), that premise is stated inline and carries its own tier.

* **Wheeler–DeWitt Equation ($\hat{H}\Psi=0$):** Adopted as the formal expression of a self-defining, closed-system Nullity; the equation is canonical quantum-gravity formalism, and its application to the universe as a closed system is a Tier 3 structural postulate.
* **Dimensionality ($D=3$):** Closed curves are nontrivially knotted only in three dimensions (Tier 1 mathematics). The further requirement that persistent identity and information storage be carried by knotted 1-D defects is a Tier 3 premise, so the former "Knot-Theoretic Bound" is a conditional argument, not a Tier 1 derivation of $D=3$.
* **Gauge Masslessness ($m_\gamma = 0$):** Follows from unbroken local $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge invariance and the Ward identity (standard field theory). Compactness of a phase variable alone does not force a flat potential; the former "Kinematic Agency (Phase Freedom)" reading is interpretive, and the physical electromagnetic bundle and connection in GCT remain Tier 3/open.
* **Lattice Action Postulate ($\hat{\hbar}=1$):** Discrete unit of action within the lattice; postulated as an irreducible structural assumption.

**TCD.2.5 Tier 1/2 Results Summary: Architectural Postulates + Conditional Mathematics**

These are architectural choices adopted for parsimony and empirical adequacy, together with exact mathematical consequences that follow once those choices are assumed. The choices are not forced by the Ontological Axioms, and conditional mathematics never promotes the premise it assumes.

* **Icosahedral Projection ($E_8\to H_4$, then a rank-six $H_3$ module):** The selected discrete projection under the framework's declared parsimony, empirical-adequacy, and spin-admissible polyhedral premises (Lemma III, Appendix USS §USS.6.1–§USS.6.2). Appendix USS §USS.7 records a **conditional T-McKay architecture chain**, not an unconditional theorem deriving the physical 6D premise. The McKay correspondence ($2I\to E_8$), the Elser–Sloane two-shell $E_8\to H_4$ result, and the rank-six requirement are closed within their hypotheses; adopting their composition as the physical architecture remains Tier 2 conditional. The golden ratio enters through the $H_4$ Cartan entry $-\phi$ and root metric rather than as a Coxeter-element eigenvalue modulus (Lemma T-McK.4).
* **Dimensional Embedding (rank $6$):** Full icosahedral indexing closes rank 6 but not Bravais centring. The allowed six-dimensional icosahedral Bravais choices are $P\cong\mathbb Z^6$, $F\cong D_6$, and $I\cong D_6^*$; GCT adopts $P$. The proposed APS/operator program uses the RT boundary and 6D cage constructed from that architecture, so it is a downstream consistency test and cannot close or elevate the upstream lattice choice. No qualifying APS boundary operator/domain has yet been specified; the finite engine values are scalar-adjacency and discrete-matrix diagnostics only. **Disposition: Tier 2 conditional architecture chain + Tier 3 downstream operator program.**

**TCD.3 Tier 2 Mechanisms and Their Tier 3/4 Deployments**

This section collects the results whose mechanism is Tier 2 within the Icosahedral ansatz. Many of them also carry Tier 3 or Tier 4 components (anchors, coefficients, physical identifications); each bracket states the full tier of the entry, and the Tier 2 label applies only to the part it names. As evidence that φ or icosahedral structure is special, every φ-formula numerical match in this section is **Tier 4**: the preregistered constant control test (v3, NEGATIVE-FRAGILE; App PSC §PSC.9.6) found φ's pattern of matches on 21 constants not distinguishable from that of random constants (58 of 300 random bases did at least as well). The test "excludes, at power ≥ 0.8, an effect in which φ hits at least 6 of the 8 informative rows through a real effect; weaker effects are not excluded." The numbers are kept as descriptive arithmetic; the mechanism tiers below are statements about the ansätze, not about evidential weight.

**TCD.4 Tier 3 Results Summary: Phenomenological Models**

**ORQ.1 Mathematical Proof**

1. **N-Agent Consensus Protocol Convergence — conditional Tier 1 Perron–Frobenius theorem; physical kernel open** (engines: `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_h1_1_consensus_convergence.py`, `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_h1_1b_krein_rutman_profinite.py`). For a **declared** finite matrix $W$ that is row-stochastic and strictly positive, Perron–Frobenius for strictly positive matrices (Horn & Johnson 1985 Thm 8.2.11, Cor 8.2.12) gives: (i) spectral radius 1 with simple leading eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = 1$; (ii) $|\lambda_k| < 1$ for all other eigenvalues; (iii) geometric convergence at rate $|\lambda_2|^t$ to the unique fixed point $\Phi^*$; (iv) $\Phi^*$ is the §11.3.2 weighted-mean stationary state. This is a standard Tier 1 conditional theorem. Its GCT application rests on three separate premises: (a) the entropic term of Ch11 §11.3.2 has been reduced so that the pure weighted-mean update $\Phi_i^{(t+1)} = \sum_j W_{ij} \Phi_j^{(t)}$, $W_{ij} = \kappa_{ij}/\sum_k \kappa_{ik}$, is the operative dynamics; (b) a chosen address filtration and metric $d_H$ have been supplied; and (c) the address realization and the positive coupling kernel $\kappa_{ij}$ are physically derived rather than declared as $\kappa_{ij} = \kappa_0 e^{-\lambda_c d_H}$. Shared cylinders alone imply none of these couplings. Sparse, reducible, periodic or state-dependent networks require their own primitivity/ergodicity analysis and need not converge to one consensus state. Numerical verification across six representative declared networks (p ∈ {2, 3}, depth ∈ {2, 3, 4}, $\lambda_c$ ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 0.7, 2.0}) passes all four theorem points with eigenvalue identities at $\sim 10^{-16}$ relative precision and exponential convergence at the predicted geometric rate. The infinite-resolution statement is conditional in the same way. On a selected $p$-primary factor or chosen cofinal filtration, the normalized kernel operator $(K f)(s) = \int \kappa(s, t) f(t) d\mu(t) / Z(s)$ on $L^2(\hat{\mathbb{Z}}_p, d\mu)$ is Hilbert-Schmidt for the declared bounded kernel (since $|\kappa(s,t)| \le \kappa_0$ and $\mu(\hat{\mathbb{Z}}_p) = 1$ give $\|\kappa\|_2^2 \le \kappa_0^2 < \infty$), hence compact (Reed-Simon 1980 Vol 1 Thm VI.22); strict positivity of that kernel makes $K$ strongly positive, so Krein-Rutman (Krein & Rutman 1948; Deimling 1985 Thm 19.3 + Cor 19.4) gives a simple leading eigenvalue, and a spectral gap then gives the geometric rate. Numerical verification across depth $\in \{4, 6, 8, 10\}$ (N up to 1024) finds the spectral gap stabilising at $1 - |\lambda_2| = 0.832910$ (relative spread $1.8 \times 10^{-3}$ across depths; HS-norm final-two-depths relative difference $2 \times 10^{-6}$). These calculations verify finite truncations of the chosen kernel family; they are not a topology-only theorem about the universal all-prime Solenoid or a proof that a physical N-Agent network realizes it. The singular limit $\lambda_c \to \infty$ (physically uncoupled agents) lies outside the theorem. **Disposition:** Tier 1 given the operator hypotheses; Tier 3 for the GCT address/coupling realization. Convergence of a declared update does not by itself show that shared reality is a consensus render among agents; that physical reading remains a Tier 3 analogy pending the coupling derivation.

**ORQ.4 Conceptual Clarifications**

1. **Finite Address Capacity — chosen filtration and coding model required [Tier 1 coding identities; Tier 3 filtration, encoding and substrate capacity]** (engine diagnostic: `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_h4_1_topological_limit.py`). The universal transversal is $\hat{\mathbb{Z}} \cong \prod_p \mathbb{Z}_p$, which is profinite and formally of infinite depth; it is not one intrinsic $p$-adic fiber. A $p$-ary depth is defined only after choosing a $p$-primary projection or a cofinal cylinder filtration together with a physical encoding, and the capacity formula then depends on the code. If $N_{\text{state}}$ denotes the total number of distinguishable global register states, $D_{\max}(p) = \lfloor \log_p N_{\text{state}} \rfloor$. If instead $N_{\text{cells}}$ independent sites each store one $p$-ary symbol, the register has $p^{N_{\text{cells}}}$ states and depth $D_{\max} = N_{\text{cells}}$, not $\log_p(N_{\text{cells}})$. The engine's numerical values (at $p = 2$: polaron-internal $7.17$, biological substrate $30.6$ for $N_{\text{Trp}} = 1.625\times10^9$ on the O.21 $n_{rp} = 1$ sensitivity branch, Hubble volume $604$) apply $\log_p$ to cell/site counts as though they were total state counts; they are therefore conditional diagnostics of one coding convention, not a Tier 2 structural bound. The lattice spacing $a_6 = 2\ell_P$ (V2 Ch04 cut-and-project framework) sets the floor of any such cell count. Whether identity has unbounded depth (the "infinite fractalization of identity" reading) is not decided by these diagnostics. A physical storage claim additionally requires read/write dynamics, a noise model, protection and lifetime. *Remaining open:* the coding model and physical register; the Tier 3 $N=144$ posit pending O.38 (full lattice minimization, see `protocol_cage_minimization.py`), on which the cell counts are conditional.

> **Open Problem O.31: Polariton-Manifold Dephasing Bound used in Ch13 §13.3.5 — CLOSED via softer "order-of-bare $T_2$" formulation anchored in Plenio-Knight 1998 + Tavis-Cummings 1968** — V3 Ch13 §13.3.5 invokes a polariton-dephasing bound as the structural reason for framing the Protocol A-Prime material-proxy decision rule as a qualitative joint $(a)+(b)+(c)$ signature with amplitude conditional on O.23 + O.24. The load-bearing form of the bound is the **softer "order-of-bare $T_2$, not $10^2$-$10^3$ enhancement" formulation** of closure path (c) below, anchored in the canonical cavity-QED literature; the precise numerical coefficient is convention- and regime-dependent and is not a universal bound.
>
> **Literature anchor (closure path (b) + (c), operative).** The Tavis-Cummings Hamiltonian (Tavis & Cummings 1968 *Phys. Rev.* 170:379) describes $N$ identical two-level atoms collectively coupled to a single cavity mode with the rotating-wave-approximation Hamiltonian $H_{TC} = \omega_c a^\dagger a + (\omega_0/2)\sum_i \sigma_z^{(i)} + g\sum_i (a\sigma_+^{(i)} + a^\dagger \sigma_-^{(i)})$. In the strong-coupling regime $g\sqrt{N} \gg \kappa, \gamma$ (where $\kappa$ is the cavity linewidth and $\gamma$ the bare matter dephasing rate), the polariton eigenstates are $|\pm\rangle = (|e, 0\rangle \pm |g, 1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$. The standard Plenio-Knight (1998 *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 70:101) quantum-jump treatment of the polariton-sector Lindblad dynamics shows that polariton-manifold dephasing inherits the bath coupling of *both* the matter and photon components (since each polariton is an equal-weight superposition); the polariton dephasing rate is therefore $\gamma_{\text{pol}} = (\gamma + \kappa)/2$ in the canonical strong-coupling limit. If $T_2^{\rm bare}=1/\gamma$, then $T_2^{\rm pol}/T_2^{\rm bare}=2\gamma/(\gamma+\kappa)$, so the polariton manifold remains order-of-bare-$T_2$ and does not produce the $10^2$-$10^3$ biological enhancement without an additional protected-subspace mechanism.
>
> **Ch13 §13.3.5 framing:** "strong coupling alone does not guarantee a large extension of the bare $T_2$ — in the absence of a protected-subspace mechanism, the polariton-manifold dephasing time remains order-of-bare-$T_2$ (in the equal-weight strong-coupling convention, $T_2^{\rm pol}/T_2^{\rm bare}=2\gamma/(\gamma+\kappa)$)". This formulation is anchored in the canonical literature and does not require a universal numerical coefficient.
>
> **Status:** **CLOSED via closure paths (b) + (c)** — softer "comparable-to bare $T_2$" formulation, anchored in Tavis-Cummings 1968 + Plenio-Knight 1998. The accepted Branch A/Branch B/chirality joint-null stands under the softer bound as a Tier 3 material-proxy decision rule; it is not a GCT falsification gate, and no Level-II verdict follows. The 150 MHz sign is unfixed and is a Tier 3 O.23/O.24 diagnostic outside F1 and Holm primary decisions. The peak *amplitude* is the empirical readout of O.23 + O.24 closures and is not pre-registered as a Tier 2 quantity. Closure path (a)—explicit derivation of the precise $T_2^{\text{pol}}$ expression from a full Tavis-Cummings + Lindblad simulation—remains a research-level item but is not load-bearing for the Ch13 §13.3.5 framing under the softer bound. **Engine binding:** none required for the adopted closure path (b) + (c); the branch/chirality framing is what the engine and the chapter both use. **Cross-references:** V3 Ch13 §13.3.5 (Protocol A-Prime); App ORQ O.23 (chiral phonon-polariton DFS, the substrate-side closure path); App ORQ O.24 (Protocol A-Prime amplitude under O.23 closure).

### **Appendix TIB: Speculative Ontology (Conditional Nested Observers in a Static Block)**

> [!SPECULATIVE] **Explicitly outside core physics.** This appendix explores Tier 3/4 models that are compatible with, but not derived by, the Solenoid topology and the observer algebra. No derivation in Volumes 1–3 depends on it, and it is not cited as evidence for the core claims.

> [!WARNING]
> **Epistemic Status: Tier 4 (Metaphysical Speculation)**
> The ontological framework presented in this appendix is highly speculative. No physical result, derivation, or geometric proof in Volumes 1-3 depends on the validity of this model. The Solenoid's exact topology is summarized here only to enforce the claim ceiling. Every owner, parent-subject, cross-life, post-mortem, and phenomenal-continuity claim below is Tier 4 unless explicitly marked Tier 3 structural.

**TIB.1 What Remains of the Original Intuition**

The motivating intuition has two parts:

1. an individual aperture can be distinct while belonging to a larger unity, as a finger belongs to a hand, an arm, and a person;
2. several physical lives/apertures might coexist at different coordinates of a static block rather than occurring as one traveling soul's sequence.

Both are mathematically consistent. Neither follows from the universal Solenoid alone.

The exact Solenoid facts are [Tier 1]

$$
\Sigma_\infty\cong\widehat{\mathbb Q}
\cong(\mathbb R\times\widehat{\mathbb Z})/\mathbb Z,
\qquad
\widehat{\mathbb Z}\cong\prod_p\mathbb Z_p,
\qquad
\check{H}^1(\Sigma_\infty;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Q,
\qquad
\pi_1(\Sigma_\infty)=0 .
$$

The path components of $\Sigma_\infty$ are dense, injectively immersed lines, so ordinary loops have no nonzero winding number: the Solenoid holds no winding record of an individual history. The nontrivial $\check{H}^1$ is a global invariant of the whole space, not a state record carried by an Agent.

A rooted cylinder tree appears only after choosing a divisibility filtration. The root is the whole level-zero cylinder, nodes are coarse sets, and points are infinite ends. Distinct ends are distinct points, even when they share a coarse cylinder. A cylinder is not an observer, and shared membership is not shared ownership or memory.

**TIB.2 Field Totality and a Self-Aware Totality**

Some contemplative traditions distinguish an undifferentiated ground from a self-aware totality. GCT can translate the distinction without adopting it as a result:

- **Field totality / Level I Presence:** the undivided ontological Field under Axiom 1 (V1 §16.2.2a). This is not automatically one self-referential owner.
- **Hypothetical apperceptive totality:** a proposed parent Level II unity capable of self-reference through multiple apertures.

The first belongs to GCT's axiomatic Level I framing. The second is a Tier 4 cosmopsychist hypothesis. It would require an independently qualified parent **Identity Polaron** or other derived unity domain, a physical integration law, a Selection-Operator architecture, persistence, and an owner criterion. "Contains all apertures" is not sufficient.

This preserves the conceptual difference between bare totality and totality-aware-of-itself while respecting the Level I/Level II boundary.

**TIB.3 Finger/Hand Structure**

Let $s$ index physical scope and $n$ index address resolution. With $\mathcal M_\star$ a declared parent observable algebra, the owner-neutral structure is

$$
\mathcal N_{s,n}\subseteq\mathcal M_\star.
$$

A selected cylinder filtration can model the address side: two distinct fine ends may share a coarser cylinder. Physical inclusions can model the scope side, ending in a whole-agent algebra $\mathcal M_A$:

$$
\mathcal N_{finger}\subseteq
\mathcal N_{hand}\subseteq
\mathcal N_{arm}\subseteq
\mathcal M_{A}.
$$

This gives exact membership and resolution relations. It permits, but does not choose among:

1. **one qualified subject per physical unity domain, possibly with several apertures**—the current Tier 3 working interpretation (V1 Ch07 §7.5.2); here the apertures lie within one physical unity domain, and reading them as several lives of one subject (§TIB.1 item 2, §TIB.5) is a separate Tier 4 extension;
2. **several subjects with a common larger physical system**;
3. **nested qualified subjects**, if child and parent each independently satisfy Level II conditions;
4. **no Level II subject at a declared level**.

The hierarchy contains no owner field. Algebraic inclusion, index, mutual information, common cylinders, or factoriality do not count subjects.

**TIB.4 Experiencing the Hand from the Finger**

A child aperture cannot passively contain every parent state. Fine-to-coarse restriction loses information, and coarse-to-fine extension is one-to-many.

Parent-from-child experience can nevertheless be modeled if one of the following is derived:

- a restricted recoverable family of parent states;
- approximate inference from local evidence;
- overlap with a shared quantum core;
- an active downward presentation/broadcast of a compatible subalgebra;
- genuine global access because the "finger" is only an aperture of one spanning physical unity domain.

Calling any such access *felt experience* additionally invokes the Tier 3 phenomenal bridge. The mathematics can specify information access; it cannot assign the first-person owner by itself.

**TIB.5 Simultaneous Lives as an Added Incidence Model**

Under the static-block postulate, physical aperture/world-line sectors at different coordinate times may coexist. To group several of them under one parent identity sector, add an explicit map

$$
\Pi_{life}:C_{parent}\longrightarrow
\mathcal P(E_\parallel\times\tau_{coord}).
$$

This map is not constructed by the circle inverse limit. A viable Tier 3 structural model must specify:

1. the parent address/physical sector $C_{parent}$;
2. the physical apertures in $\Pi_{life}(C_{parent})$;
3. whether the apertures are simultaneous only in the Field Frame or also coupled;
4. the physical unity/owner rule;
5. the direction and observables of any cross-aperture channel.

Once supplied, the model is **simultaneous**, not sequential: no soul must leave one body and wait to enter another, so the model needs no waiting state and no universal clock. But several owner assignments remain possible. One parent label does not prove one parent subject.

**TIB.6 Personal Identity: A Conditional Cylinder-Relative Stage Model**

GCT may explore a stage-theoretic account in which physical apertures are stages and a declared incidence/address relation groups them. This is closest to branching four-dimensionalism (Sider 2001; Hawley 2001; Lewis 1986), but with two cautions:

- common-prefix depth is relative to a chosen filtration, not an intrinsic metaphysical identity measure;
- address proximity is not sufficient for numerical or phenomenal identity.

The model can be compared with standard positions:

- **Psychological continuity** (Locke 1694; Parfit 1984; Shoemaker 1970): memory/personality may track aperture continuity but need not define the address relation.
- **Animalism** (Olson 1997; Snowdon 2014): biological continuity remains the default empirical carrier of a human Polaron; any identity beyond it requires new persistence and recoupling physics.
- **Stage theory (exdurantism) / worm perdurantism:** the static-block representation is congenial, while branching/incidence is additional Tier 3 structure.
- **Narrative identity** (Schechtman 1996): narrative remains a cognitive construction within an aperture, not a topology theorem.

No conclusion about fission, reconvergence, or "the original" is licensed until the owner rule is supplied.

**TIB.7 Memory and Cross-Life Access**

The exact $\check{H}^1\cong\mathbb Q$ is a property of the whole Solenoid. It is not automatically a memory stored by an Agent. Cross-life memory requires at least

$$
(\text{state map},\ \text{read/write coupling},\ \text{memory bridge},\ \text{noise channel},\ \text{persistence time},\ \text{cross-aperture access}),
$$

where the memory bridge is a declared physical map from a Solenoid-level quantity to a stored, readable state.

A chosen ultrametric says that two addresses share a coarse cylinder. It does not carry data laterally. Meditation, trauma, dreams, NDEs, or reduced sensory coupling do not mathematically "truncate" an owner into a parent cylinder; that is a Tier 4 phenomenological mechanism requiring an observable channel and controls against ordinary biological memory, suggestion, and inference.

**Ultrametric distance is not a channel [Tier 1 topology].** A Branch Node of the chosen filtration is a cylinder (a set of ends), not a point, so it cannot be inserted as the third point of the strong triangle inequality $d(A,B)\le\max\{d(A,C),d(C,B)\}$. The correct statement is that two distinct ends lying in a common cylinder of depth $m$ satisfy $0<d(A,B)\le\operatorname{diam}(\text{cylinder})$, which equals $p^{-m}$ on a declared $\mathbb Z_p$ factor. Ends that share a coarse cylinder therefore remain distinct points, are close only in the selected filtration, and are not closest unless no deeper cylinder separates them. That closeness is coarse membership; it is not low impedance, tunnelling, or data transfer.

Accordingly:

- biological/biographical memory belongs to the physical substrate;
- a robust topological memory is Tier 3/open until an order parameter, gap and noise protection are derived;
- cross-life recall and one aperture accessing another are Tier 4;
- lack of recall neither proves nor disproves a shared owner, because the owner assignment itself remains open.

**TIB.8 Death, Persistence, and Recoupling [Tier 4: Speculative Ontology]**

Biological death ends the known physiological processes supporting human cognition. The historical metabolic/Zeno/Identity-Polaron chain is not a demonstrated additional support mechanism. Solenoid topology does not show that any Polaron state survives, retracts to a parent node, reconverges, or couples to another substrate. Because $\pi_1(\Sigma_\infty)=0$, ordinary loops in $\Sigma_\infty$ have no nonzero winding number, and global Čech cohomology is not an individual state record; this route supplies no protected post-mortem record.

Any post-mortem model needs separate answers to:

1. what physical state survives substrate dissolution;
2. what Hamiltonian or topological charge protects it;
3. where that state lives after decoupling;
4. how it is read or recoupled;
5. what constitutes continuity of ownership.

Until then, **Topological Hysteresis**, **Bardo**, reconvergence, post-mortem persistence, recall across lives, and same-owner claims remain Tier 4 metaphysical conjectures with no weight in the core physics.

### **Appendix CXL: Crystallography of 6D Lattices**

**CXL.1 The Rank-Six Icosahedral Bravais Setting and the $E_8$ Connection**

GCT conditionally adopts the primitive rank-six icosahedral Bravais lattice $P\cong\mathbb Z^6$ as its physical-vacuum architecture [Tier 1/2 structural postulate]. Full three-dimensional icosahedral indexing fixes rank 6 but does not fix the Bravais centring: the classified alternatives are primitive $P\cong\mathbb Z^6$, face-centred $F\cong D_6$, and body-centred $I\cong D_6^*$. The primitive-$P$ choice is therefore an explicit architectural adoption, not a consequence of an embedding in $E_8$.

The **$D_6$ Root Lattice** (the checkerboard lattice) is a sublattice of $\mathbb{Z}^6$ defined by the parity constraint:
$$ D_6 = \left\{ \mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_6) \in \mathbb{Z}^6 : \sum_{i=1}^6 x_i \equiv 0 \pmod 2 \right\} $$
The roots of $D_6$ are the permutations of $(\pm 1, \pm 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)$, and they generate $D_6$ rather than $\mathbb Z^6$. The 60 roots are the vertices of the **rectified 6-orthoplex**, which is therefore the *root polytope* of $D_6$. The Voronoi cell of $D_6$ is its polar dual: it has 60 facets (one per root) and 76 vertices, namely the 12 shallow holes $\pm e_i$ and the 64 deep holes $(\pm\tfrac12)^6$ (cf. $D_3$, whose Voronoi cell is the rhombic dodecahedron with $6+8=14$ vertices; Conway & Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, 3rd ed., Ch. 4 and Ch. 21). The bare 6-orthoplex $\{\pm e_i\}$ is neither: its vertices are not $D_6$ vectors. The $F\cong D_6$ branch and its icosahedral projection remain a classified alternative to GCT's adopted primitive-$P$ branch.

The higher-symmetry $E_8$ relation is distinct: the McKay correspondence associates $2I$ with $\widetilde E_8$, and the Elser–Sloane construction projects the 240 $E_8$ roots onto two concentric $H_4$ 600-cell shells before the separate rank-six $H_3$ module is introduced. These results conditionally organize the architecture; they neither make $\mathbb Z^6$ a lattice subobject of even $E_8$ nor select the primitive Bravais type.

**CXL.2 The Projection Matrices (Explicit Forms)**

To generate the 3D Ammann-Kramer-Neri (AKN) tiling, we project the standard basis of $\mathbb{Z}^6$ into physical space $E_\parallel$ and internal space $E_\perp$. The two Galois-conjugate raw row frames below have different Euclidean norms: each parallel row has squared norm $2(2+\phi) \approx 7.236$ and each perpendicular row $2(3-\phi) \approx 2.764$. A single scalar cannot normalize both, so the canonical isometric convention uses two constants:
$$ N_\parallel = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2(2+\phi)}}, \qquad N_\perp = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2(3-\phi)}} = \phi N_\parallel . $$

**Parallel Projection Matrix ($\mathcal{M}_\parallel$):**
$$\mathcal{M}_\parallel = N_\parallel \begin{pmatrix}
1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & \phi & \phi \\
\phi & -\phi & 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & \phi & -\phi & 1 & -1
\end{pmatrix}$$

**Perpendicular Projection Matrix ($\mathcal{M}_\perp$):**
Generated by the Galois conjugation $\phi \to -\phi^{-1}$:
$$\mathcal{M}_\perp = N_\perp \begin{pmatrix}
1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & -\phi^{-1} & -\phi^{-1} \\
-\phi^{-1} & \phi^{-1} & 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & -\phi^{-1} & \phi^{-1} & 1 & -1
\end{pmatrix}$$

**Verification of Orthogonality [Tier 1 — algebraic identity]:**
The matrices satisfy $\mathcal{M}_\parallel \mathcal{M}_\perp^T = \mathbf{0}$. Computing the dot product of the first rows:
$$\mathbf{r}_{\parallel 1} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{\perp 1} \propto (1)(1) + (1)(1) + (0)(0) + (0)(0) + (\phi)(-\phi^{-1}) + (\phi)(-\phi^{-1})$$
$$= 1 + 1 + 0 + 0 - (\phi \cdot \phi^{-1}) - (\phi \cdot \phi^{-1}) = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0 \checkmark$$
By the $H_3$ icosahedral symmetry, all nine row-pair dot products vanish identically. With the two normalizations,
$$ \mathcal{M}_\parallel\mathcal{M}_\parallel^T = \mathcal{M}_\perp\mathcal{M}_\perp^T = I_3, \qquad \mathcal{M}_\parallel^T\mathcal{M}_\parallel + \mathcal{M}_\perp^T\mathcal{M}_\perp = I_6 . $$
This establishes kinematic orthogonality and completeness. Dynamical decoupling of phason ($E_\perp$) and phonon ($E_\parallel$) modes additionally depends on the quadratic action (App DPS §DPS.3). $\square$

*Coordinate-convention note:* a common scalar $N = 1/\sqrt{2(2+\phi)}$, used in earlier editions, makes only the parallel rows unit-normal; in that legacy chart $\mathcal{M}_\perp\mathcal{M}_\perp^T = \phi^{-2} I_3$, so it is not the orthonormal Euclidean projector. Rescaling the internal coordinates and the acceptance window together leaves the AKN model set unchanged. The two-normalization convention above is the projection source of truth for this appendix.

**CXL.3 The Star Map: Vertex-Configuration Count Conventions**

The discrete nature of the lattice restricts the local environment of any node to a finite set of "Vertex Stars." The phrase "vertex configuration" has, however, been used for three different objects, whose counts must not be interchanged:

- **24** — the historical count of a published matching-rule / vertex-configuration convention (Henley 1986 *Phys. Rev. B* 34:797; Katz & Duneau 1986 *J. Physique* 47:181). It has not been reproduced as the bare nearest-neighbour alphabet used by the current GCT engine and cannot be substituted for it.
- **9** — the bare edge-incidence stars of the RT-window model set under full $I_h$ equivalence: a bare star is the subset of the twelve allowed displacements $\{\pm e_i\}_{i=1}^{6}$ whose endpoints also lie in the window (App QLA §QLA.3) [Tier 1 enumeration conditional on the Tier 2 AKN projector/window].
- **101** — the radius-two decorated stars under the declared decoration convention (App QLA §QLA.3); this is a numerical cell-sampling result, not a completed formal arrangement proof or a universal AKN vertex count.

Earlier editions also cited a count of 32; that number is retired (it is not a vertex-star count in any of the three conventions; cf. App GRF §GRF.2.1).

Under the twelve-bond bare alphabet:
1. **The $\nu$-Star ($Z=12$):** the perfect twelve-bond icosahedral reference star is an allowed local configuration and a useful orientational control; it is not by itself a dynamically selected ground state.
2. **The conditional defect-cage ansatz ($N=144$):** this is not one vertex star but a proposed **cluster**: under the adopted Tier 3 O.38 architecture, 12 $\nu$-stars at the face centres of a dodecahedral shell (icosahedral positions) as a candidate electron defect. The identities $12^2=F_{12}=144$ and the exact polyhedral Gauss--Bonnet totals are internal consistency checks; they do not establish minimum energy, stability, or physical cage-size selection. Those claims remain open pending O.38 full-lattice minimization.
3. **The $\tau$ object ($Z=20$):** it cannot be a bare nearest-neighbour star in a twelve-displacement alphabet. If retained (as the cluster associated with the "Hole" modes of Volume 3), it must be typed as a larger-radius or decorated cluster whose graph and dynamics are specified separately [Tier 3/open].

The proposal that the elementary-particle spectrum can be read from the vibrational spectra of such defect cages is a Tier 3 research programme (O.38); no particle table has been derived from these geometric cages.

**CXL.4 Vacuum Supersolidity: Definition and Open Requirements [Tier 3/open]**

The condition for supersolidity (Andreev & Lifshitz, 1969) is that the ground state possesses both crystalline density order $\langle \rho(\mathbf{r}) \rangle = \sum_G \rho_G e^{i\mathbf{G}\cdot\mathbf{r}}$ and off-diagonal phase order $\langle \psi \rangle = \sqrt{\rho_0} e^{i\theta}$. This is a definition, not a derivation of the GCT vacuum state.
In a standard crystal, the atoms are localized (Peierls pinning), making phase transport impossible.
Quasiperiodicity and irrational projection do not by themselves imply zero-energy phason shifts, quantum tunneling, nonzero superfluid stiffness, or global phase coherence. The earlier "Phason-Assisted Tunneling" argument — that zero-energy phason shifts let nodes tunnel between configurations and so establish global phase coherence — is a Tier 3 hypothesis, not a derivation. Establishing it requires a normalized many-body Hamiltonian, ground state, transition amplitudes and thermodynamic limit. App ULA §ULA.2 provides a bosonic displacement scaffold with a symbolic $V_{lock}$; it does not yet establish off-diagonal long-range order or vacuum supersolidity. This is the same open status as V2 Ch03 Conditional Criterion 3.1.

### **Appendix DPS: Phason Stiffness: Status of the Stiffness Map**

## DPS.1 Generalized Elasticity in 6D

The GCT vacuum is modeled as a harmonic hypercubic lattice in 6D with a scalar bond stiffness $\kappa_{6D}$ (App ULA §ULA.2). Its coarse-grained elastic energy density $\mathcal{E}$ is written schematically as:
$$ \mathcal{E} = \frac{1}{2} C_{MNPQ} E_{MN} E_{PQ} $$
where $C$ is the elastic tensor of that lattice. A hypercubic lattice has hyperoctahedral, not isotropic, elasticity, and the 3D hydrodynamic limit additionally requires the cut-and-project restriction (fields depending on $x_\parallel$ only) [Tier 3].

## DPS.2 Projection, Gram Determinants and the Raw Galois-Frame Identity

The 6D lattice nodes are projected into physical space $E_\parallel$ (phonon) and internal space $E_\perp$ (phason). Let $\mathcal{M}_\parallel$ and $\mathcal{M}_\perp$ be the $3 \times 6$ icosahedral projection matrices of App CXL §CXL.2.

We define the **Gram Matrices** for each subspace:
- $G_\parallel = \mathcal{M}_\parallel \mathcal{M}_\parallel^T$
- $G_\perp = \mathcal{M}_\perp \mathcal{M}_\perp^T$

With the canonical row-isometric projectors ($N_\parallel = 1/\sqrt{2(2+\phi)}$, $N_\perp = 1/\sqrt{2(3-\phi)} = \phi N_\parallel$; App CXL §CXL.2), both Gram matrices equal $I_3$ and the determinant ratio is $1$. The value $\phi^{-6}$ appears only in the legacy chart that uses the single constant $N_\parallel$ for both sectors, where $G_\parallel = I_3$ and $G_\perp = \phi^{-2} I_3$; equivalently, for the unnormalized Galois-conjugate row matrices $A_0, B_0$ with $A_0A_0^T = 2(2+\phi)I_3$ and $B_0B_0^T = 2(3-\phi)I_3$:
$$ \frac{\det(B_0B_0^T)}{\det(A_0A_0^T)} = \phi^{-6} \approx 0.0557 $$

This is an exact **raw Galois-frame identity**, not an invariant of the complementary subspaces or of the AKN model set [Tier 1 linear algebra]. Under the internal-coordinate change $B_0 \mapsto sB_0$, with the acceptance window changed covariantly, the model set and the true projector $B_0^T(B_0B_0^T)^{-1}B_0$ are unchanged while the determinant ratio changes by $s^6$. The same caution applies to projected unit-cell or window volumes: a Euclidean volume in a target frame depends on the coordinate measure chosen for that frame and is not fixed by the row spaces alone.

## DPS.3 Physical Stiffness Map [Tier 3 — registered hypothesis P3b, pending O.15]

The physical elastic constants are coefficients of a canonically normalized action, not determinants of coordinate row frames. Standard icosahedral elasticity (Lubensky-Ramaswamy-Toner 1985; Socolar-Lubensky-Steinhardt 1986) treats the phason constants $K_1, K_2$ as independent EFT parameters. GCT currently registers

$$ \frac{K_\perp}{K_\parallel} = \phi^{-18} $$

as the **Tier 3 stiffness-map hypothesis P3b** (Parameter Ledger §0.1; Open Problem O.15(b)), anchored to the independent Tier 2 $H_3$ integer $D = 18$ of §DPS.4. Like H-EW, P3b is a registered Tier 3 hypothesis listed outside the core-input count; only the integer $D = 18$ is Tier 2.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Retired Gram-cube heuristic.** Earlier versions motivated $\phi^{-18}$ by cubing the determinant ratio of §DPS.2, $(\det G_\perp/\det G_\parallel)^3 = (\phi^{-6})^3$. That quantity depends on the coordinate frame: a rescaling of the internal rows by $s$ changes it by $s^{18}$ while the AKN model set is unchanged, and with the canonical row-isometric projectors it equals $1$. It therefore cannot be a physical stiffness derivation, and no Gram support for $\phi^{-18}$ is claimed. Under a field redefinition $w' = sw$, a quadratic elastic coefficient must transform as $K' = s^{-2}K$ (with the inertia transforming alongside it), so physical propagation speeds stay coordinate-invariant; the raw Gram-cube rule fails this covariance test.
>
> **Universality boundary.** Icosahedral symmetry leaves the quadratic stiffness form $Q = aP_\parallel + bP_\perp$ with the ratio $b/a$ free [Tier 1 representation theory], and the parent Hamiltonian of App ULA §ULA.2, isotropic in the six-component displacement index (not an isotropic elastic tensor), gives $b/a = 1$. Neither symmetry nor the isotropic parent action selects $\phi^{-18}$; retaining that value requires the canonically normalized action/RG calculation specified by O.15.

> **Phason-mode dispersion: LRT-diffusive vs GCT-propagating identification [Tier 3 open; the propagating character rests on a posited phason inertia, and the photon identification is the declared open programme of V2 Ch06 §6.1].** LRT (Lubensky-Ramaswamy-Toner 1985) establishes that in the *hydrodynamic IR limit* of standard 3D icosahedral phason elasticity, phason modes are **diffusive**: $\omega \propto i D_\perp q^2$ with $D_\perp$ a phason diffusion constant. Conditional on the Tier 3 P3b stiffness hypothesis and a posited phason inertia $\rho_{eff}$ (V2 Ch05 §5.3), GCT proposes to identify phasons with a *propagating* photon-like mode ($\omega \propto q$ with phase velocity $c = c_P \phi^{-9}$ in the Parameter Ledger convention; V2 Ch06 §6.2), which is structurally distinct from the LRT hydrodynamic limit. A proposed reconciliation is scale-dependent: LRT's diffusive regime applies in the IR limit where momentum is small compared to the inverse phason correlation length $1/\xi_\perp$; the propagating identification would apply at shorter wavelengths. There would then be a **crossover scale** $q_c$ between propagating and diffusive phason behaviour, set by the ratio of phason elastic energy to phason damping. Because the diffusive regime is the long-wavelength one, light could propagate at every observed wavelength only if $q_c$ lies *below* the smallest probed electromagnetic wavenumber, $q_c \lesssim 2\pi/\lambda_{max}$ (observed); the damping that sets $q_c$ would also imply vacuum absorption, which is not yet bounded; the *empirical disposition* requires either (a) LRT-style analysis extended to the UV regime confirming the propagating crossover, or (b) measurement of the crossover scale in a chemically clean analog system. This is bundled with **Open Problem O.15**; the LRT-diffusive vs GCT-propagating gap is a proposed scale-regime distinction that is not currently quantified.

## DPS.4 The D=18 Identification via $H_3$ Shephard-Todd Invariant Degrees [Tier 2 integer identification anchoring the Tier 3 P3b stiffness hypothesis]

The exponent 18 used in the Tier 3 P3b hypothesis $K_\perp/K_\parallel = \phi^{-18}$ admits a canonical group-theoretic identification: it is the **sum of fundamental degrees** of the icosahedral $H_3$ Coxeter group (Shephard-Todd theorem; Humphreys 1990 *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups* Table 1):
$$D = d_1 + d_2 + d_3 = 2 + 6 + 10 = 18.$$
The Shephard-Todd identity gives equivalently $D = N + r$, where $N = 15$ is the number of positive roots of $H_3$ (= number of reflections) and $r = 3$ is the rank: $15 + 3 = 18$ ✓.

For comparison within the finite irreducible rank-three classification: $A_3$ has invariant-degree sum 9 (= 2 + 3 + 4); $B_3$ has 12 (= 2 + 4 + 6); and $H_3$ has 18 (= 2 + 6 + 10), the largest sum in that irreducible class. The complete finite rank-three classification also includes reducible $A_1\times I_2(m)$, with degrees $\{2,2,m\}$; $A_1\times I_2(14)$ therefore also has sum 18. The $H_3$ identification is conditional on the irreducible icosahedral premise. Engine cross-reference: `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_stiffness_ratio.py`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Status of the identification (two-layer disposition).** The integer 18 in $\phi^{-18}$ is identified with the **canonical Shephard-Todd invariant** of the icosahedral Coxeter group $H_3$ — the sum of fundamental invariant degrees $d_1 + d_2 + d_3 = 2 + 6 + 10 = 18 = N + r = 15 + 3$. The Shephard-Todd invariant-degree sum is a standard finite-Coxeter-group invariant — this *integer identification* is **Tier 2 canonical group theory**.
>
> The connection from the integer 18 to the *full stiffness-ratio claim* $K_\perp/K_\parallel = \phi^{-18}$ is the P3b/O.15(b) anomalous-dimension hypothesis, not the retired Gram-cube heuristic of §DPS.3. It is not derived from standard quasicrystal elasticity theory, in which Lubensky-Ramaswamy-Toner treat $K_1, K_2$ as independent EFT parameters. The full stiffness-ratio claim is therefore a **Tier 3 action/RG hypothesis anchored by a Tier 2 canonical Coxeter integer**, not a forced consequence of projection geometry.
>
> **Geometry-only universality boundary.** For the general sector-diagonal long-wavelength dynamical pencil $C = L\otimes(aP_\parallel + bP_\perp)$, $\rho = I\otimes(\alpha P_\parallel + \beta P_\perp)$ with $a, b, \alpha, \beta > 0$, the phonon/phason generalized-eigenvalue ratio is $\lambda_\perp/\lambda_\parallel = b\alpha/(a\beta)$. It takes every positive value while preserving the same icosahedral point group and substitution rule, and independent sector rescalings commute with inflation, so the inflation map supplies no missing normalization. This is a non-identifiability statement for the geometry-only derivation class [Tier 1 linear algebra; Tier 2 application to the declared GCT split]; it is not a no-go on a value selected by additional physics. A local locking potential can shift a gap or mass intercept, but it does not select an independent gradient stiffness.
>
> **The remaining open piece (the current Tier 3 physical-link claim under O.15(b)): the per-invariant anomalous dimension calculation.** By the universality boundary above, this calculation cannot succeed from point group, inflation factor and the integer 18 alone; it needs a target-blind microscopic energy law together with a kinetic/inertial or mobility law. The engine script `protocol_o15a_rg_flow_argument.py` verifies only the conditional identity $\exp[-(2+6+10)\log\phi] = \phi^{-18}$ after the per-invariant rule $c_n = d_n$ is inserted; it does not derive that rule. The structural argument would proceed as: (1) write the LRT free energy on the AKN lattice in symmetry-adapted basis as $F = \sum_n F_n(I_{d_n}(\Phi_\perp))$, where $I_{d_n}$ is the H$_3$ fundamental invariant of degree $d_n \in \{2, 6, 10\}$ and $F_n$ is its phason-elastic coupling; (2) choose the RG step: the linear inflation factor of the primitive module is $\phi^3$ (App QCT §QCT.3.2); $\phi$ maps between the $P$, $F$ and $I$ modules, so an RG step $b = \phi$ would need separate justification; (3) compute the one-loop diagrams that renormalize each $F_n$ separately by integrating high-momentum phason modes within one RG shell; (4) show explicitly that the per-invariant anomalous dimension of the coupling associated with $I_{d_n}$ equals $d_n \log\phi$ (the load-bearing dynamical step that no published QC calculation cited here has done — Lubensky-Ramaswamy-Toner 1985 and Socolar-Lubensky-Steinhardt 1986 treat $K_1, K_2$ as independent EFT parameters and do not work in the symmetry-adapted basis); (5) sum: total anomalous dimension = $(d_1 + d_2 + d_3) \log\phi = 18 \log\phi$; (6) exponentiate: $K_\perp/K_\parallel = \exp(-18\log\phi) = \phi^{-18}$. **Step (4) is the load-bearing missing piece**: the per-invariant bookkeeping $c_n = d_n$ is currently taken as input from icosahedral natural-scaling assumptions, and by the universality boundary it cannot follow from the Chevalley-Shephard-Todd data alone. A closure of O.15 requires an explicit loop calculation in the symmetry-adapted basis (research-grade QFT on the AKN lattice) built on declared microscopic energy and kinetic laws, leading to a unique attractive, coordinate-invariant RG fixed ray. No such derivation is cited here. The Shephard-Todd identification establishes the canonical icosahedral-group-theoretic origin of the integer 18; the connection to the elasticity ratio remains the load-bearing Tier 3 assumption P3b (Open Problem O.15). ## DPS.4b Empirical Comparison and the i-AlPdMn Gap [Tier 3]

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Empirical-gap disclosure (Open Problem O.41).** Earlier editions compared $\phi^{-18} \approx 1.73 \times 10^{-4}$ with a "phason-to-phonon stiffness ratio" of $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-1}$ attributed to i-AlPdMn measurements by de Boissieu et al. (1995, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75:89) and Francoual et al. (2006, *Phil. Mag.* 86:1029), and reported a 100–1000× gap. That comparison is withdrawn as stated. On our reading of the sources, de Boissieu et al. infer the dimensionless phason elastic anisotropy $K_2/K_1$ from diffuse scattering, and Francoual et al. report long-wavelength phason relaxation kinetics (a diffusion constant and an activation energy). **Physical Setup.** The healing length $\xi$ is meant as the spatial scale at which the polaron's kinetic energy balances its self-energy. GCT uses the Bohr–Compton length

with $a_0 = \hbar/(\alpha m_e c)$ the Bohr radius: $\xi = a_0/\alpha \approx 7.25$ nm [Tier 1 arithmetic; its identification as the vacuum/polaron healing length is Tier 3]. It is a dimensional combination, not a derived Gross–Pitaevskii healing length ($\hbar/\sqrt{2mgn}$) or polaron radius, and it is *not* a GCT-specific prediction. ## DPS.7 Unit Audit of the G Expressions: No Three-Route Equivalence [Route 1: consistency with the Planck identity; Routes 2/3: retired elasticity formula, failed scaling ansatz]

Three routes to Newton's gravitational constant $G$ appear in the GCT manuscript; they are not three independent derivations. This section closes Route 1 to the standard Planck-mass identity $G = \hbar c / M_P^2$ (a consistency check, since that identity defines $M_P$) and records the unit audit that retires Routes 2 and 3. The form $G \sim \hat c^4 / (K_\perp L^2)$ has the dimensional scaling of a gravitational coupling, but the published Routes 2/3 formula $G = \hat c^4/(8\pi K_\perp a_6)$ carries one further factor of $L$ than $G$ (units $L^4 M^{-1} T^{-2}$ instead of $L^3 M^{-1} T^{-2}$). Its dimensionally completed form, evaluated under the Tier 3 P3b substitutions, gives $\phi^{18}/(32\pi)\,G \approx 57\,G$ in the Parameter Ledger speed convention ($c = \phi^{-9}c_P$), and $\phi^{-18}/(32\pi)\,G \approx 1.72 \times 10^{-6}\,G$ if the bare speed $c_P$ is instead identified with $c$; no first-principles GCT cancellation closes either residual. Routes 2/3 are therefore one failed scaling ansatz, retired as a derivation or check of $G$ (V2 Ch08 §8.1.4).

**The three routes:**
- **Route 1 (Jacobson primary):** $G_1 = \dfrac{c^3 a_6^2}{4\hbar}$ (V2 Ch09 §9.1.4)
- **Route 2 (Phason elasticity):** $G_2 = \dfrac{\hat{c}^4}{8\pi K_\perp a_6}$ (V2 Ch08 §8.1.4)
- **Route 3 (Acoustic metric):** $G_3 = \dfrac{\hat{c}^4}{8\pi K_\perp a_6}$ (V1 §13.3.4 — same formula, different derivation path)

Routes 2 and 3 share the same formula; the cross-route question is whether $G_1$ reduces to the same numerical value as $G_2 \equiv G_3$.

**Closure of Route 1 to the standard Planck identity.** Route 1 itself does not require P3b. For comparison with Route 2, we separately assume the Tier 3 P3b expressions $\hat{c} = \phi^{-9}c_P$ for the dimensional phason speed (§DPS.6; in the Route 2/3 formulas of this section $\hat c$ denotes this dimensional speed, not the dimensionless ratio $\sqrt{K_\perp/K_\parallel}$ of §DPS.6) and $K_\perp = (E_P/\ell_P^3)\phi^{-18}$ (§DPS.3), where $c_P$ is the bare lattice speed (Parameter Ledger row $c$: the phason speed is the observed $c = \phi^{-9}c_P$) and $E_P = M_P c^2$ is the Planck energy. The derivation below closes Route 1 to the standard identity $G = \hbar c / M_P^2$; Route 2 does not reduce to the same identity: O.22 is closed negatively (the single-$a_6$ formula is dimensionally inconsistent and its corrected form is off by a calibration-dependent factor that is never 1; see the dimensional analysis below).

Step 1 — Under P3b, express $\hat{c}^4$ and $K_\perp$:
$$\hat{c}^4 = \phi^{-36} c_P^4, \qquad K_\perp = \frac{M_P c^2}{\ell_P^3} \phi^{-18}$$

Step 2 — Substitute into Route 2:
$$G_2 = \frac{\phi^{-36} c_P^4}{8\pi \cdot \dfrac{M_P c^2}{\ell_P^3} \cdot \phi^{-18} \cdot a_6} = \frac{\phi^{-18} c_P^4 \ell_P^3}{8\pi M_P c^2 a_6}$$

Step 3 — Use the Planck identity $c^2 = G M_P / \ell_P$ (from definition $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3} \Rightarrow G = \ell_P^2 c^3/\hbar$; it holds for the observed $c$, and for $c_P$ only if $c_P = c$) and the lattice-Planck relation. The Route 1 expression gives:
$$G_1 = \frac{c^3 a_6^2}{4\hbar}$$
Substituting the GCT lattice spacing $a_6 = (2\hbar/m_e c)\phi^{-107}(1-5\alpha)$ and the Planck mass relation $M_P = m_e \phi^{107}(1-5\alpha)^{-1}$:
$$a_6 = \frac{2\hbar}{M_P c} \cdot \phi^{-107}(1-5\alpha) \cdot \phi^{107}(1-5\alpha)^{-1} = \frac{2\hbar}{M_P c}$$
(the $\phi^{107}$ and $(1-5\alpha)$ factors cancel exactly). Therefore:
$$G_1 = \frac{c^3}{4\hbar} \cdot \frac{4\hbar^2}{M_P^2 c^2} = \frac{\hbar c}{M_P^2} = G_{standard}$$
which is the standard definition of $G$ in terms of the Planck mass. Since $M_P^2 = \hbar c / G$ by definition, the closing identity $G = \hbar c / M_P^2$ is *tautological*: it confirms that the GCT Route 1 substitution chain is dimensionally consistent with the standard Planck-mass definition. It does **not** establish that Route 2's phason-elasticity formula reduces to the same value.

**Status of the cross-check.** What is proved above:
- Route 1's substitution chain closes consistently to $G = \hbar c / M_P^2$ (the Planck-mass tautology).
- Routes 2 and 3 share a single phason-elasticity formula $G = \hat c^4 / (8\pi K_\perp a_6)$; equivalence between Routes 2 and 3 is automatic by formula identity.

**Dimensional analysis of Routes 2/3 [closure of O.22].** Engine: `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_o22_newton_g_dimensional_full.py` performs the explicit unit-by-unit propagation. The single-$a_6$ Route 2 formula $G_2 = \hat c^4 / (8\pi K_\perp a_6)$ has dimensions
$$[G_2] = \frac{L^4 T^{-4}}{(M L^{-1} T^{-2}) \cdot L} = L^4 M^{-1} T^{-2},$$
which differs from $[G] = L^3 M^{-1} T^{-2}$ by one factor of length. The single-$a_6$ expression is therefore **dimensionally inconsistent** as a standalone SI-unit expression for $G$. The minimal dimensional correction is to replace $a_6$ by $a_6^2$:
$$G_2^{(\text{corrected})} = \frac{\hat c^4}{8\pi K_\perp a_6^2}, \qquad [G_2^{(\text{corrected})}] = L^3 M^{-1} T^{-2} \;\checkmark$$
Numerical evaluation with the Tier 3 P3b-conditioned substitutions $K_\perp = (E_P/\ell_P^3)\phi^{-18}$, $a_6 = 2\ell_P$ depends on the speed calibration, which is not settled across the manuscript:
$$G_2^{(\text{corrected})} = \frac{\phi^{18}}{32\pi}\, G \approx 57\, G \quad (\text{Parameter Ledger convention: phason speed } = c = \phi^{-9}c_P,\ E_P = M_Pc^2),$$
$$G_2^{(\text{corrected})} = \frac{\phi^{-18}}{32\pi}\, G \approx 1.72 \times 10^{-6}\, G \quad (\text{if } c_P \text{ is identified with } c,\ \text{phason speed } \phi^{-9}c),$$
and $G/(32\pi) \approx 0.010\,G$ if $E_P$ is read as $M_P c_P^2$ in the Ledger convention. The value $\phi^{-18}/(32\pi)$ quoted alone in earlier editions uses $c_P = c$ and is inconsistent with the Ledger convention; the speed calibration itself remains open (App ULA §ULA.6). In every reading the corrected Route 2 misses Route 1 by a factor that is not 1, and no current GCT-internal derivation absorbs the residual.

**Status of the cross-route claim.** Routes 2 and 3 are one retired elasticity formula, not independent validations. The form $G \sim \hat c^4 / (K_\perp L^2)$ has the dimensional scaling of a gravitational coupling, but the formula is **not** an SI-unit derivation or a successful check of $G$: the single-$a_6$ expression is dimensionally inconsistent, and under the P3b substitutions the corrected formula is off by a calibration-dependent factor ($\approx 57$ in the Ledger convention, $\approx 1.7\times10^{-6}$ if $c_P = c$) with no GCT-internal cancellation. There is therefore no three-route equivalence, either numerical or as a successful consistency check.

**Empirical disposition.** Route 1 gives a 2273.725 ppm comparison against CODATA-2022 (display 2274 ppm; verified by `verify_independent/verify_newton_g.py`) on the model-authoritative $\alpha_{\rm GCT}=\phi^2/360$ branch with CODATA $m_e$ and exact SI $h,c$. The all-CODATA-$\alpha$ sensitivity branch is 2013.345 ppm. This comparison reflects the precision of the electron-mass anchor entering through $a_6 = 2\hbar/(M_P c)$; it is not an independent prediction of $G$ (Tier 4 as evidence: not distinguishable from numerology for strong effects; App PSC §PSC.9.6). Routes 2/3 are retired and do not contribute to the empirical $G$ comparison.

**Summary.** Route 1 reproduces the standard Planck identity $G = \hbar c / M_P^2$ (Jacobson horizon entropy + lattice-Planck relation; Tier 2 mechanism, 2273.725 ppm model-branch comparison vs CODATA); because that identity defines $M_P$, this is a consistency closure, not an independent derivation. Routes 2 and 3 (phason elasticity) share one retired formula with the scaling form $G \sim \hat c^4 / (K_\perp L^2)$ and are **not** SI-unit derivations or successful checks: the single-$a_6$ expression is dimensionally inconsistent (off by one factor of $L$), the dimensionally corrected form, conditional on P3b, differs from Route 1 by $\phi^{18}/(32\pi) \approx 57$ in the Ledger speed convention (or $\phi^{-18}/(32\pi) \approx 1.72 \times 10^{-6}$ if $c_P = c$), and no first-principles GCT cancellation closes that residual. The former three-route headline therefore reduces to a *single SI-unit consistency closure (Route 1)*; Routes 2/3 are a failed scaling ansatz, not independent proofs. ### **Appendix TPS: Thermodynamics of Perpendicular Space**

**TPS.1 Phason Density of States**

To resolve the thermal catastrophe of the vacuum crystallization (Chapter 7), we must quantify the thermodynamic capacity of the internal manifold $E_\perp$. We analyze the **Density of States (DOS)**, $g(\omega)$, for both the phonon (parallel) and phason (perpendicular) sectors.

The density of states in a $d$-dimensional medium with dispersion relation $\omega = v k$ scales as:
$$ g(\omega) \propto \frac{\omega^{d-1}}{v^d} $$
* **Parallel Sector ($E_\parallel$):** The model identifies these excitations as phonons and provisionally associates their reference stiffness and speed with the Planck scales, $K_\parallel \approx E_P/\ell_P^3$ and $v_\parallel \approx c_P$, the bare lattice speed of V2 Ch08 §8.1.3. In the Parameter Ledger convention (row $c$) $c_P$ is distinct from the observed speed of light $c$, which the book proposes to identify with the phason (second-sound) speed (V2 Ch06 Postulate 6.1, a declared open programme).
* **Perpendicular Sector ($E_\perp$):** The model identifies these excitations as phasons. The numerical assignments $K_\perp/K_\parallel = \phi^{-18}$ and $v_\perp/v_\parallel = \phi^{-9}$ (so $v_\perp = c \approx c_P \phi^{-9}$) are **Tier 3, conditional on the Parameter Ledger stiffness-map hypothesis P3b (O.15(b)) and a common inertial normalization**; only the integer $D = 18$ is Tier 2, and the ratio is not a projector or point-group invariant (App ULA §ULA.3).

Conditional on the linear, isotropic dispersion model and the P3b speed map, the ratio of the density of states at a given energy $E = \hbar \omega$ is
$$ \frac{g_\perp(\omega)}{g_\parallel(\omega)} \approx \left( \frac{v_\parallel}{v_\perp} \right)^3 \approx (\phi^9)^3 = \phi^{27} \approx 4.4 \times 10^5 $$
This $\phi^{27}$ factor is therefore conditional arithmetic, not an independently derived thermodynamic result. Within that branch it favors the internal space; the proposed primary thermodynamic sink is the much larger **Holographic Phase Space** of the bulk lattice [Tier 4].

**TPS.2 The Heat Capacity Ratio**

The heat capacity $C_V$ of a system is proportional to the number of accessible degrees of freedom ($N_{dof}$).
* **Physical Manifold ($N_\parallel$):** The number of degrees of freedom in the observable universe is limited by the number of nodes in the 3D projection slice.
* **Internal Manifold ($N_\perp$):** The number of degrees of freedom in the internal space corresponds to the total number of nodes in the 6D parent lattice that are causally connected within the horizon but not projected into the physical slice.

For a causal patch defined by the Hubble Horizon, the **Holographic Principle** caps the effective number of degrees of freedom at the screen count $(R_H/\ell_P)^2 \sim 10^{122}$; the bulk volume count $(R_H/\ell_P)^3 \sim 10^{183}$ would exceed that cap. Invoking a bulk reservoir much larger than the screen is therefore in tension with the same principle [Tier 4].
Within the candidate architecture, this immense heat-capacity ratio would drive the released latent heat of crystallization entropically into the bulk modes of $E_\perp$; the partition function and coupling that would make this quantitative are open (§TPS.3). The physical slice $E_\parallel$ acts as a low-capacity "surface" in thermal contact with a candidate large reservoir [Tier 4].

## ULA.1 Calibration Firewall (Single Anchor, SI mapping)

To ensure the technical rigor of Geometric Consciousness Theory and prevent the "Planck Loop" (where units are defined by the constants they seek to explain), we enforce a strict **Calibration Firewall**. 

### The Rules of the Firewall:
1. **Lattice Primacy:** All physical derivations must be performed in dimensionless lattice units ($a_6, t_6, \kappa$) first.
2. **Standardization:** Dimensional constants ($G, \hbar, c$) are treated as **Derived Conventions** used for human readability, not fundamental primitives. **Planck units are derived conventions, not primitives.**
3. **Single Anchor Mapping:** The conversion from lattice units to SI units (meters, seconds, kilograms) must be performed via a declared **Experimental Anchor** (typically $m_e$ or $E_{vac}$).

### Lattice Primitives (Dimensionless):
- **Lattice Spacing ($a_6$):** The minimum distance between nodes. $a_6 \equiv 1$.
- **Update Time ($t_6$):** The duration of one selection cycle. $t_6 \equiv 1$.
- **Bond Stiffness ($\kappa$):** The elastic restorative force. $\kappa \equiv 1$.
- **Node Mass ($M$):** The inertial weight of a lattice vertex. $M \equiv 1$.

In this system, dimensionless derived quantities and structural ratios are represented as **Structural Eigenvalues**. Dimensional constants such as the SI speed of light remain unit conventions; GCT uses only the dimensionless lattice ratio $\hat c = c/c_P$ (Parameter Ledger row $c$) as a structural object.

## ULA.2 Microscopic Hamiltonian on $\mathbb{Z}^6$

The fundamental dynamics are governed by a discrete sum over the 6D nodes:
$$ H = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^6} \frac{\mathbf{p}_n^2}{2M} + \frac{\kappa}{2} \sum_{\langle n,m \rangle} (\mathbf{u}_n - \mathbf{u}_m)^2 + V_{lock}(\mathcal{P}_\perp \mathbf{u}_n) $$

Where:
- $\mathbf{u}_n \in \mathbb{R}^6$ is the displacement vector of node $n$.
- $\langle n,m \rangle$ denotes summation over nearest neighbors in $\mathbb{Z}^6$.
- $V_{lock}$ is the periodic potential arising from the boundary of the Rhombic Triacontahedron window in $E_\perp$.

As written, $V_{lock}(\mathcal{P}_\perp \mathbf{u}_n)$ depends on the phason displacement itself, not on its gradient, so it breaks the uniform phason-shift symmetry that keeps phasons gapless and gives the phason a gap (§ULA.4.1 relates $m_{phason}$ to it). ## ULA.3 Projection and the Quadratic-Action No-Go

Let $P_\parallel$ and $P_\perp$ be the canonical complementary projectors of the lifted icosahedral action on $\mathbb{R}^6$. The representation decomposes into two inequivalent real three-dimensional irreducible components, so by Schur's lemma every invariant symmetric quadratic form is
$$ Q = aP_\parallel + bP_\perp . $$
Icosahedral symmetry removes the cross term but leaves two independent positive coefficients; it fixes neither coefficient nor the ratio $b/a$ (direct solution of $R_g^T Q R_g = Q$ gives a two-dimensional solution space, spanned by the two projectors) [Tier 1 representation theory].

The §ULA.2 nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian uses the isotropic Euclidean bond form $Q=\kappa I_6=\kappa(P_\parallel+P_\perp)$. With canonical row-isometric projection it therefore gives equal bare quadratic weights, $K_\perp/K_\parallel=1$, not $\phi^{-18}$. This is a **Tier 2 action-level no-go within the declared isotropic Hamiltonian**: it does not say that phasons cannot become softer, only that the softness is not generated by projection or symmetry alone. The obstruction survives a fixed substitution rule: for a sector-diagonal long-wavelength pencil with elastic weights $(a,b)$ and inertial weights $(\alpha,\beta)$, the generalized-eigenvalue ratio is $\lambda_\perp/\lambda_\parallel=b\alpha/(a\beta)$, which spans all positive reals while the point group and inflation map are unchanged. The internal locking potential $V_{lock}(\mathcal{P}_\perp\mathbf{u})$ can supply phason-specific mass and nonlinear vertices but does not, without an explicit coarse-graining calculation, assign the gradient-stiffness ratio; and the invariant degrees $\{2,6,10\}$ classify invariant polynomials without becoming an anomalous dimension by group theory alone.

The earlier display $K_\perp/K_\parallel=(\det G_\perp/\det G_\parallel)^3=\phi^{-18}$ is **retired**: it depends on the choice of row frame (a relative rescaling of the rows by $s$ changes it by $s^{18}$ while leaving the projectors unchanged), and it equals 1 for canonical projectors. GCT may still test the independent Tier 3 hypothesis P3b (O.15(b); listed outside the parameter count like H-EW, as in Appendix DPS):
$$ \frac{K_\perp}{K_\parallel} = \phi^{-D_{H3}} = \phi^{-18} \approx 1.731 \times 10^{-4} \qquad \text{[Tier 3 hypothesis]}, $$
under which a $\sim 10^{-4}$ suppression would make the phason sector the "soft" carrier relative to the "hard" phonon bonds. Closure requires additional physics: a target-blind microscopic energy law and a kinetic/inertial or mobility law, followed by the full dynamical pencil and an attractive, coordinate-invariant RG fixed ray.

## ULA.7 Finite-N Vacuum Polarization and the 1/(2N) Correction [Tier 2 single-shell trace + Tier 3 bilayer integer-factor handle; rigorous geometric closure pending O.5]

**Setup.** In the finite-N lattice regularization, the one-loop vacuum
polarization $\Pi(0)$ receives a finite-size correction from the discrete
trace over the $N=144$ cage nodes (Tier 3 cage posit per V3 Ch07 §7.1.3,
pending the O.38 minimization). Continuum limit: $\Pi(0)|_\infty$ as $N \to \infty$.

**Single-Shell Finite-N Trace.**
For $N$ nodes on a single $I_h$-symmetric icosahedral shell, the one-loop
self-energy admits the structural decomposition
$$\Pi(0)|_N = \sum_{i=1}^{N} G_{ii}^2 + \sum_{i \neq j} G_{ij}^2$$
where $G_{ij}$ is the lattice Green's function at zero momentum. The
off-diagonal term is a sum of squares and does **not** vanish; the rigorous
finite-$N$ structure is supplied instead by vertex-transitivity. For an
$I_h$-equivariant Green's function on a vertex-transitive shell the diagonal is
constant, $G_{ii} = c$, so the diagonal self-energy carries the exact normalized
weight
$$\frac{\sum_{i} G_{ii}^2}{(\operatorname{Tr} G)^2} = \frac{N c^2}{(N c)^2} = \frac{1}{N}
\qquad \text{(single }I_h\text{-symmetric shell of }N\text{ nodes),}$$
an identity that holds across the icosahedral, dodecahedral, and
icosidodecahedral shells under both Laplacian-resolvent and adjacency-resolvent
conventions (engine: `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_m7_bilayer_orthogonality.py`).
Identifying this normalized diagonal weight with the physical finite-$N$
correction $\Delta\Pi_1/\Pi_\infty = 1/N$ is the geometric step that — together
with the factor-of-2 promotion below — bundles with O.5.

**Two-Level Cage Structure and the Factor of 2.**
The cage commitment of V3 Ch07 §7.1.3 is the *two-level* structure $N = 12_{\text{outer}} \times 12_{\text{inner}} = 144$: 12 outer dodecahedral face directions, each carrying a 12-fold inner vertex sub-shell. Under the bilayer tensor trace $G^{(2L)} = G^{(\text{outer})} \otimes G^{(\text{inner})}$ the normalized diagonal weight factorizes,
$$\frac{\sum_d (G^{(2L)}_{dd})^2}{(\operatorname{Tr} G^{(2L)})^2} = \left[\frac{\sum_i G_{ii}^2}{(\operatorname{Tr} G)^2}\right]\left[\frac{\sum_j g_{jj}^2}{(\operatorname{Tr} g)^2}\right] = \frac{1}{12}\cdot\frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{144} = \frac{1}{N},$$
so the tensor construction alone reproduces the single-shell $1/N$ — **not** $1/(2N)$ (verified in the engine protocol above; this follows from $\operatorname{Tr}(A\otimes B) = \operatorname{Tr}A\,\operatorname{Tr}B$ and $\operatorname{diag}(A\otimes B) = \operatorname{diag}(A)\otimes\operatorname{diag}(B)$). Obtaining the empirically required
$$\frac{\Delta\Pi}{\Pi_\infty} = \frac{1}{2N} = \frac{1}{288}$$
requires an additional within-level / across-level projection beyond the stated tensor product — a structural input the bilayer counting motivates but does not derive.
The "factor of 2" reflects the bilayer-pairing ansatz and remains a Tier 3 discrete integer-factor handle selected to land near $\alpha$ alongside the 360 multiplier; the *full* closure of the within-level vs. across-level cancellation balance is the geometric step bundled with O.5.

corrected $\alpha^{-1}_{\text{GCT}} = 360\phi^{-2}(1 - 1/288) \approx 137.030$,
which lands 41.5 ppm from CODATA (V1 Ch13 §13.2.4). This is a calibrated postdiction until O.5 derives the bilayer pairing factor from the AKN bubble integral rather than selecting it over the $1/N$ alternative. As evidence that φ or icosahedral structure is special, this match is **Tier 4**: the preregistered constant control test (v3, NEGATIVE-FRAGILE; App PSC §PSC.9.6) found φ's pattern of matches on 21 constants not distinguishable from that of random constants (58 of 300 random bases did at least as well).
