### **Appendix SNE: Selection, No-Signalling, and Energy**

## SNE.1 The Closed System Identity

Geometric Consciousness Theory (GCT) maintains that the universe is a closed system at the fundamental level of the Bulk. Under the Tier 3 Wheeler-DeWitt structural postulate (V1 Ch05), the universal wavefunction $|\Psi\rangle$ satisfies the constraint:
$$ \hat{H} |\Psi\rangle = 0 $$

For the following formal consistency check, $\mathcal{F}_{sel}$ is stipulated as an Agent-frame conditionalization map rather than a modification of the global Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$. This is a model definition, not a derivation or physical realization of a Selection Operator.

### Conditional No-Added-Energy Identity
If an observer conditions a description on branch $|\phi_k\rangle$ while the stipulated global state remains the unitary superposition
$$ |\Psi\rangle = \sum_i c_i |\phi_i\rangle $$
then the unchanged global Wheeler-DeWitt expectation remains
$$ \langle \Psi | \hat{H} | \Psi \rangle = 0 $$
This identity says only that descriptive conditioning does not alter the stipulated global state. It does not prove that a physical Agent collapses, redistributes, or steers amplitudes, nor that a non-unitary $\mathcal F_{sel}$ can be implemented without an explicit open-system energy ledger.

## SNE.2 The Metabolic Trade

This section records a **hypothetical energy ledger** for a future intent-to-metabolism bridge. No realized physical $\mathcal F_{sel}$, mental force, or material-to-vacuum transducer is presently derived; the bookkeeping is conditional on supplying such a bridge independently.

### The Cost of Thought
Within that conditional surrogate, define **Selection Work** ($W_{sel}$) as a placeholder for energy transferred through a specified material action channel toward a declared target configuration. The First-Law ledger would read:
$$ \Delta E_{bio} = W_{sel} + \Delta Q_{heat} $$
This identity enforces energy accounting only after the terms are physically defined. It does not establish a "Mental Force," an exact topological torque, or an ATP-powered Zeno interface (the microtubule-lumen interface remains Tier 3 candidate biochemistry, App ORQ O.34). ATP hydrolysis is a measured metabolic energy source and therefore a possible budget ceiling, not evidence for phason bias or vacuum winding.

**Conditional surrogate ledger:**
1. **Input candidate:** Measured chemical potential ($\Delta \mu_{ATP}$).
2. **Transduction placeholder:** A hypothetical Zeno/THz material channel whose coupling, efficiency, and directionality remain unmeasured and underived.
3. **Target variable:** A declared GCT configuration change; neither topological winding of the vacuum lattice nor its identification with $\mathcal{F}_{sel}$ has been physically realized.

If such a bridge were established, conservation would require it to redirect supplied metabolic free energy rather than create energy. This is a constraint on a future mechanism, not evidence that an Agent presently gates metabolic entropy.

## SNE.4 Conditional Subluminal Readout for a Declared Phason Source [Tier 1 selection rule; Tier 3 subluminality premise]

**Scope of the result.** The calculation below is a conditional field-propagation statement: if a declared source enters the phason equation and couples into the physical phonon sector through the allowed strain bilinear, the physical disturbance is carried by the phonon propagator at no more than the phonon speed; it is subluminal only on the additional premise $v_{\rm phonon}\leq c$ (Step 2), which GCT's own speed hierarchy does not supply. This is distinct from the standard quantum-information no-signalling theorem, which concerns completely-positive trace-preserving (CPTP) maps, local instruments and outcome averaging on a joint state. No established GCT result presently derives a nonlocal topological correlation, entangled state, common source, or cross-aperture channel from Solenoid topology. The theorem therefore constrains a source model **after** such physical data are supplied; it does not validate those data.

**Theorem SNE.1 (Phonon-speed-bounded physical readout of a declared address coupling).** Choose an address filtration and suppose a separately derived physical source/coupling associates two apertures with a common cylinder at depth $m$. Any observable disturbance transmitted from the phason source into $E_\parallel$ through the strain-level $K_3$ phason–phonon channel propagates no faster than the physical phonon characteristic speed $v_{\rm phonon}$; it propagates no faster than $c$ only under the additional premise $v_{\rm phonon}\leq c$ [Tier 3 premise; it fails under the P3b speed map, Step 2]. Shared cylinder membership alone does not establish a correlation, common state, or access channel.

**Proof.** The proof has three steps.

**Step 1 — Selection-rule structure of the phason–phonon coupling [Tier 1 character calculation given the representations; Tier 2 GCT field assignment].** The phonon displacement $u_\parallel$ transforms as the vector representation $T_1$ of the icosahedral group $I$ (order 60), and the phason displacement $u_\perp$ transforms as the Galois-conjugate representation $T_2$ (related to $T_1$ by the $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ automorphism $\phi \mapsto 1 - \phi$) — this is the standard quasicrystal-theory identification (Senechal 1995 *Quasicrystals and Geometry* §2.5; Janssen et al. 2018 *Aperiodic Crystals* §6.3). $T_1$ and $T_2$ are inequivalent 3-dimensional irreducible representations of $I$.

Two distinct bilinears must be examined to see which mode-couplings are allowed by $H_3$:

(i) *Displacement-level bilinear* $u_\parallel^i u_\perp^j$ (a candidate mass-like mixing term, transforming in $T_1 \otimes T_2$). With the conjugacy classes ordered $(e, 5A, 5B, 3A, 2A)$ (sizes $1, 12, 12, 20, 15$), the character of $T_1 \otimes T_2$ is the pointwise product $(9, -1, -1, 0, 1)$, and the multiplicity of the trivial irrep is

$$n_A(T_1 \otimes T_2) = \frac{1}{60}(9 - 12 - 12 + 0 + 15) = 0.$$

A direct $H_3$-invariant displacement–displacement coupling is therefore *forbidden*: no mass-like phonon–phason mixing exists at the algebraic level.

(ii) *Strain-level bilinear* $C^{mix}_{ijkl}\,\varepsilon_{ij}\,w_{kl}$. The physical phonon strain is symmetric in its two indices, $\varepsilon_{ij} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_i u_\parallel^j + \partial_j u_\parallel^i)$, and therefore lives in $\mathrm{Sym}^2(T_1) = A \oplus H$ (the antisymmetric part $\Lambda^2(T_1) = T_1$ is the rotation of the displacement field, which couples through gauge-rotation invariance separately). The phason gradient $w_{kl} = \partial_k u_\perp^l$ lives in $T_1 \otimes T_2 = G \oplus H$. The strain-level mixing coupling therefore lives in
$$\mathrm{Sym}^2(T_1) \otimes (T_1 \otimes T_2) = (A \oplus H) \otimes (G \oplus H).$$
By the canonical multiplicity formula $n_A(R \otimes S) = \sum_X m_R(X)\,m_S(X)$, the multiplicity of the trivial irrep in this product equals the number of irreps appearing in both $\mathrm{Sym}^2(T_1)$ and $T_1 \otimes T_2$:
$$n_A\bigl(\mathrm{Sym}^2(T_1) \otimes (T_1 \otimes T_2)\bigr) = \sum_{X \in \{A, T_1, T_2, G, H\}} m_{\mathrm{Sym}^2(T_1)}(X)\,m_{T_1 \otimes T_2}(X).$$
Both decompositions contain $H$ exactly once; no other irrep is shared between $\mathrm{Sym}^2(T_1) = A \oplus H$ and $T_1 \otimes T_2 = G \oplus H$. Therefore $n_A = 1 \cdot 1 + 0 = 1$, and exactly one $H_3$-invariant strain–strain coupling exists, arising from the shared $H$ representation. This is the standard Socolar–Lubensky–Steinhardt / Lubensky–Ramaswamy–Toner $K_3 \varepsilon_{ij} w_{kl}$ term of icosahedral quasicrystal elasticity (Socolar et al. 1986; Lubensky et al. 1985); it is the same coupling that appears as the $C^{mix}_{ijkl}$ term of the hydrodynamic free energy in V2 Ch05 §5.2.2.

The first selection rule forbids displacement-level mixing in the declared representation assignment; a future $\mathcal F_{sel}$ source model would have to respect it, but no physical Selection Operator is derived. The second permits one ordinary strain-level quasicrystal-elasticity coupling. A separately supplied phason source could drive the phonon equation through that channel; GCT has not derived such a source or linked it to selection. Engine verification computing both multiplicities: `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_w4_h3_bilinear_coupling_ban.py`.

**Field-typing consistency note [Tier 1 representation theory].** The same selection rule underlies the field-typing analysis of V1 Ch17 §17.1.3. Vector phason strain lies in $T_1 \otimes T_2 = G \oplus H$, while the Levi-Civita cross product $\mathbf{k} \times \boldsymbol{\sigma}$ lies in $T_1$; they share no irrep, so the cross-product coupling of V1 Eq. (17.3) gives no icosahedral scalar for the vector phason. The full tensor $\mathbf{k} \otimes \boldsymbol{\sigma} = A \oplus T_1 \oplus H$ shares exactly one $H$ with the phason strain; under full $I_h$ parity the bare contraction is a pseudoscalar, and multiplication by a time-even molecular-handedness pseudoscalar $\chi \in A_u$ permits one candidate term. This establishes only that such a channel is allowed and unique up to its coefficient and normalization. It does not insert the term into the action, fix its coefficient, or turn the conditional source of Theorem SNE.1 into a physical Dual-Material or Selection source.

The linearised equations of motion in the presence of the $K_3$ coupling read schematically
$$\rho \ddot{u}_\parallel = K_\parallel \nabla^2 u_\parallel + K_3\, \nabla\!\cdot w, \qquad \rho_{eff} \ddot{u}_\perp = K_\perp \nabla^2 u_\perp + K_3\, \nabla\!\cdot \varepsilon,$$
i.e. a $w$-source in the phason equation feeds the phonon equation through the $K_3 \nabla\!\cdot w$ term. The phonon propagator then carries that disturbance into $E_\parallel$. Step 2 controls the propagation speed.

**Step 2 — The induced signal in $E_\parallel$ is bounded by the phonon speed; bounding it by $c$ is an extra premise [Tier 2 propagation bound within the declared linear model; Tier 3 subluminality premise].** The $K_3$-induced phonon disturbance propagates as a solution of the phonon wave operator $\rho \partial_t^2 - K_\parallel \nabla^2$, whose characteristic speed is the phonon sound speed $v_{\rm phonon}$; within the declared linear model the disturbance therefore travels no faster than $v_{\rm phonon}$, regardless of the algebraic structure of the source term. The further bound $v_{\rm phonon}\leq c$ is **not derived here**. It is an additional premise: that the long-wavelength effective theory of the phonon sector is Lorentz invariant with limiting speed $c$ (cf. Volovik, G. E. (2003), *The Universe in a Helium Droplet*, Oxford University Press). That premise is in tension with GCT's own speed hierarchy: the book identifies $c$ with the phason ("second sound") speed (V2 Ch06 Postulate 6.1; V2 Ch08; Parameter Ledger row $c$), and under the Tier 3 stiffness-map hypothesis P3b the reference phonon speed is $v_\parallel\approx c_P=\phi^{9}c>c$ (App TPS §TPS.1), with the phason sector the "soft" carrier relative to the "hard" phonon bonds (App ULA §ULA.3). **Under P3b the premise fails**, and Step 2 then bounds the readout only by $v_{\rm phonon}$, which is not a subluminality result. The subluminality of the readout is therefore conditional on the extra premise $v_{\rm phonon}\leq c$ [Tier 3], not a load-bearing physical fact of the GCT model.

**Step 3 — Address proximity is not physical proximity or a correlation law.** Two distinct Solenoid ends may share a cylinder in a chosen filtration while remaining different points. The Realization/Incidence map to physical locations $\mathbf{r}_{\parallel}^{(i)}$ and $\mathbf{r}_{\parallel}^{(j)}$ is additional Tier 3 data, as is any common-source or cross-aperture correlation kernel. The topology does not put the apertures at one Solenoid point and does not remove the need to specify how a measurable correlation is produced.

**Conclusion.** The field-theoretic calculation establishes a conditional propagation bound: if a declared phason source drives an $E_\parallel$ observable through the $K_3$ channel, the readout propagates no faster than the phonon speed, and subluminally only on the extra premise $v_{\rm phonon}\leq c$ (which fails under P3b). It does **not** derive simultaneous access, static co-location, Bell correlations, or a cross-aperture channel from shared cylinders. Those premises require an independent physical law and must also satisfy the standard CPTP no-signalling constraints. $\square$

**Scope corollary.** Bell-inequality violations cannot presently be recast as Solenoid-cylinder correlations by this theorem. Such a model would need an explicit entangled state, local instruments, outcome statistics reproducing the quantum correlations, and a proof of no signalling after outcome averaging. The present $K_3$ calculation constrains only the physical field-readout channel [Tier 1 selection rule; Tier 3 subluminality premise; Solenoid/Bell identification Tier 3/open].

**Consequence under P3b [Tier 3; open problem App ORQ O.48(b)].** If the Tier 3 stiffness-map hypothesis P3b holds, the phonon speed is $v_{\rm phonon}\approx c_P=\phi^{9}c>c$ (Step 2), so a declared phason source driving an $E_\parallel$ observable through the $K_3$ channel would be a superluminal channel inside the model. This tension with relativistic causality is not resolved here; it is registered as App ORQ O.48(b).

## SNE.5 Born-Marginal Constraint on Biased Selection [Tier 1 — standard QI consequence; its application to GCT selection is the open problem App ORQ O.48(a)]

The standard no-signalling identity used in V1 Ch09 §9.4.3 sums unnormalised projections, $\sum_k \mathrm{Tr}_A[(\hat P_k\otimes\hat I_B)\rho(\hat P_k\otimes\hat I_B)]=\rho_B$, so it holds when the outcomes at A occur with the Born weights $p_k=\mathrm{Tr}[(\hat P_k\otimes\hat I_B)\rho]$. If a will-, resonance- or impedance-biased Selection Operator reweighted A's outcomes to $q_k\neq p_k$, B's outcome-averaged state would be $\sum_k q_k\,\rho_{B|k}\neq\rho_B$ in general, and the bias would signal superluminally (Gisin 1990; Polchinski 1991). Any selection bias that GCT entertains (V1 Ch09 §9.5.3; V1 Ch10 §10.3.2) must therefore leave the outcome-averaged marginals at their Born values on every subsystem. Local unitary or CPTP steering before an outcome is registered meets this constraint, because it changes the state to which the Born rule applies rather than the rule itself. No mechanism that biases individual outcomes while meeting the constraint is stated in the manuscript; this gap is App ORQ O.48(a).

### **Appendix BEB: The Bio-Physical Energy Budget [Tier 3]**

## BEB.1 The Gap: Vacuum vs. Thermal

This appendix records a multi-scale **energy-comparison scenario** for candidate material degrees of freedom [Tier 3]. $$ E_{vac} \approx 3.55 \text{ keV} $$

At physiological temperatures (310 K), the thermal noise floor is:

The ratio between these two scales is:
$$ \frac{E_{vac}}{k_B T} \approx 1.36 \times 10^5 $$

identification as the vacuum/polaron healing length is Tier 3]. Its biological
identification with microtubule geometry is also Tier 3. See the Parameter Ledger and the Ch13 Tier Boundary callout.

## BEB.2 The Shielding Requirement

The shielding scenario compares a candidate radical-pair coherence time with contextual bulk-water dipole estimates near $\tau_{raw} \approx 10^{-13}$ seconds. That bulk-water scale is not a measured bound for a qualified β-tubulin Trp radical pair, and no phase used for biological Zeno-gating has been identified.

The material scenario imports a **Singlet-Triplet ($S \leftrightarrow T_0$) gap** for Tubulin Tryptophan (Trp) aromatic radical pairs and $T_2 \sim 1-10 \ \mu\text{s}$ from radical-pair references; neither is a direct measurement of a qualified intact β-tubulin Trp pair or evidence for a stable quantum reservoir. The 10 ns interval used below ($\tau_{\rm meas}=1/\Gamma_{rec}$, $\Gamma_{rec}\sim10^8$ s$^{-1}$) is the radical-pair recombination channel treated as a measurement; the historical 100 MHz figure is a material-scan scenario only, not an operative Continuous Zeno Drive, a derived measurement rate, or a GCT frequency, and an applied drive frequency is not a measurement rate (V3 Ch13 §13.4.7). Sampling faster than the exponential $T_2$ scale is not sufficient for a Zeno regime: the bare Misra-Sudarshan crossover depends on $\tau_Z^2/T_2$, and the bare radical-pair Hamiltonian places the $10^8$ s$^{-1}$ recombination channel on the inverse-Zeno side. O.23 therefore explores a hypothetical ordinary protected-subspace material model that would lower the effective Hamiltonian variance; such a model is not established, is not required by Selection, and would not by itself be evidence of a phason interaction or of Level II.

### BEB.2b — Coherence-Extension Material Scenario [Tier 1 Misra–Sudarshan arithmetic; Tier 3 material scenario; O.23 open]

The Misra-Sudarshan quantum Zeno theorem (Misra & Sudarshan 1977 *J. Math. Phys.* 18:756; reviewed in Facchi & Pascazio 2008 *J. Phys. A* 41:493001 §2.1) gives, for projective measurements at interval $\tau_{\rm meas}$, a diagnostic effective-coherence-time extrapolation from the short-time survival law:

$$\tau_{eff} = \frac{\tau_Z^2}{\tau_{\rm meas}}, \qquad \tau_Z^{-2}\equiv\frac{\sigma_H^2}{\hbar^2},\qquad \sigma_H^2\equiv\langle H^2\rangle-\langle H\rangle^2.$$

The Zeno time is uniquely fixed by the survival-probability curvature: $P(t)=1-(\sigma_Ht/\hbar)^2+O(t^4)$, hence $\tau_Z=\hbar/\sigma_H$. Writing the variance as a cyclic frequency $\Delta\nu_H\equiv\sigma_H/h$ gives $\tau_Z=1/(2\pi\Delta\nu_H)$, not $1/\Delta\nu_H$. For a finite projective-measurement interval, $\Gamma_{\rm eff}=\tau_{\rm meas}/\tau_Z^2$ is the standard short-time consequence of the Misra-Sudarshan limit (see Facchi & Pascazio 2008 §2.1). Within the manuscript's quadratic-to-exponential matching diagnostic, the nominal boundary $\tau^*=\tau_Z^2/T_2$ is $2.81$ ps for $T_2=10\,\mu$s and $\tau_Z=5.305$ ns, so the 10 ns recombination interval is an out-of-regime diagnostic extrapolation. Facchi, Nakazato & Pascazio (2001, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 86:2699, eq. 16) instead write $\tau^*\simeq\gamma_0\tau_Z^2$ for a golden-rule population-decay rate $\gamma_0$; identifying $\gamma_0=1/T_2$ is an additional Tier 3 channel-matching assumption.

where the **Zeno time** $\tau_Z$ is set by the variance of the interaction Hamiltonian in the initial state — *not* the exponential decoherence time $T_2$. Facchi & Pascazio (2008 §2.2.5, eq. 19) define a finite Zeno/inverse-Zeno crossover implicitly by $\gamma_{\rm eff}(\tau^*)=\gamma$ when an intersection exists; they do not identify it generally with $\tau_Z^2/T_2$ or guarantee the sign beyond it.

Applied to the bare Trp radical-pair singlet with the engine's placeholder variance $\sigma_H/h \approx 30$ MHz (the FAD-derived rms of §BEB.12, within ~10% of the TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ effective coupling), the Zeno time is $\tau_Z=1/[2\pi(30\,\text{MHz})]\approx5.305$ ns [Tier 3 hyperfine import]. At $\tau_{Zeno} = 10$ ns (the recombination interval $1/\Gamma_{rec}$, not a drive period) the bare Misra-Sudarshan formula gives

$$\tau_{eff}^{\text{bare MS}} = \frac{\tau_Z^2}{\tau_{\rm meas}} \approx 2.8\,\text{ns}.$$

This is an out-of-quadratic-regime diagnostic extrapolation of the bare Misra-Sudarshan formula, not an in-regime lifetime or an established extension. It is more than four orders below the $\sim 100\,\mu$s–$1$ ms registered material-scenario band and more than six orders below the 10 ms conservative comparison target; both are declared material-scenario stress targets, not Selection or Level-II requirements. ## BEB.6 Conditional Spin-Phason Sector Model [Tier 1 conditional algebra; Tier 3 physical realization open]

This section states the exact algebraic conditions under which a spin-only Zeno-type measurement channel would preserve a physically instantiated topological sector. It does **not** show that the Identity Polaron supplies such a sector, that the biological Hamiltonian is block diagonal in it, or that a macroscopic protection gap has been derived.

**BEB.6a Non-interchangeable integer candidates.** Three integer-valued quantities have different domains and must not be identified merely because each takes values in $\mathbb{Z}$:

1. **Compact phase-vortex winding** $W_{\rm vor}(\gamma)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\oint_\gamma d\theta_{\rm phason}\in\pi_1(S^1)\cong\mathbb{Z}$. It is defined only after an $S^1$-valued field $e^{i\theta_{\rm phason}}$, a domain on which its amplitude is non-zero, an oriented loop $\gamma$ and the excluded core or boundary data are supplied [Tier 1 topology conditional on the stated field and domain; GCT phason realization Tier 3/open].
2. **Three-dimensional texture degree** $w_{\rm tex}\in\pi_3(M)$, conditionally $\pi_3(S^3)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ if a normalized map $S^3_{\rm space}\to S^3_{\rm order}$ and a compactifying boundary condition are supplied.
3. **Framed-core self-linking** $h_F(K,v)=\operatorname{lk}(K,K_v)\in\mathbb{Z}$ for a physical normal field $v$ with push-off $K_v$; removing the frame collapses all $h_F$ values to the same unframed core.

No identity $W_{\rm vor}=w_{\rm tex}=h_F$ holds by default; any equality between them is a separate physical bridge to be derived.

**BEB.6b Dimensionally typed conditional Hamiltonian.** Retain the Tavis-Cummings spin/cavity sector of §BEB.4,
$$\hat H_{\rm spin}=\frac{\hbar\omega_a}{2}\sum_i\hat\sigma_z^i+\hbar\omega_c\hat a^\dagger\hat a+\hbar g\sum_i\left(\hat a^\dagger\hat\sigma_-^i+\hat a\hat\sigma_+^i\right).$$
Suppose, as an additional physical premise, that one of the integer candidates is instantiated as a dimensionless observable $\hat W=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}n\,\hat\Pi_n$ on a phason-sector Hilbert space with spectral projectors $\hat\Pi_n$. A minimal model is then
$$\hat H_{\rm total}=\hat H_{\rm spin}\otimes\mathbb I+\mathbb I\otimes\hat H_{\rm phason}+\hbar g_W\,\hat S_z\otimes f(\hat W)+\hat V_{\rm mix},$$
where $\hat S_z=\frac12\sum_i\hat\sigma_z^i$ and $f(\hat W)$ are dimensionless, $g_W$ is an angular frequency, and $\hat H_{\rm phason}$ (for example the phason elastic energy $K_\perp\int|\nabla\mathbf u_\perp|^2d^3x$ of Volume 2 Ch.2) and $\hat V_{\rm mix}$ have units of energy. The diagonal term commutes with $\hat W$ by construction: it can produce a sector-dependent spin phase but cannot write or change the sector. Any CISS/Rashba-phason transducer able to change the sector belongs in $\hat V_{\rm mix}$ until its matrix elements between sectors are derived. The local gradient coupling of V1 §17.1.3 does not by itself establish the diagonal form.

**Theorem BEB.6.1 (Conditional sector-preservation criterion) [Tier 1 algebra conditional on the declared model]:**
Let the open-system evolution be
$$\dot\rho=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[\hat H_{\rm total},\rho]+\sum_\alpha\mathcal D[\hat L_\alpha]\rho,\qquad \mathcal D[\hat L]\rho=\hat L\rho\hat L^\dagger-\tfrac12\{\hat L^\dagger\hat L,\rho\}.$$
If $[\hat H_{\rm total},\hat\Pi_n]=0$ and $[\hat L_\alpha,\hat\Pi_n]=0$ for every $n$ and every active collapse/measurement channel, then the sector probabilities $p_n=\operatorname{Tr}(\hat\Pi_n\rho)$ are constant, $\dot p_n=0$.

Spin-only measurement operators $\hat L_\alpha^{\rm spin}\otimes\mathbb I$ satisfy the second condition automatically. Full sector preservation additionally requires $[\hat H_{\rm phason},\hat W]=[\hat V_{\rm mix},\hat W]=[\hat L_\alpha^{\rm phason},\hat W]=0$ for the actual phason Hamiltonian, transducer, recombination channel and environmental collapse operators, or a quantitative bound on their off-diagonal matrix elements. These commutators are physical premises or dynamical calculations; they do not follow "by definition" from calling $\hat W$ topological. The theorem is therefore conditional: a strictly spin-only measurement preserves an already-instantiated sector when the complete dynamics is sector preserving. The present corpus has not derived these block-diagonality conditions for the Identity Polaron, the CISS coupling, radical-pair recombination or substrate turnover. Even when they hold, only the sector probabilities are conserved; relative phase coherence between sectors, a writable memory and an observable readout are not thereby supplied.

**BEB.6c Barrier and transition-rate requirement.** The quantum of the historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario is $h\nu\approx4.14\times10^{-7}$ eV. This is a useful diagnostic scale, but it does not establish decoupling without an independently derived sector-transition barrier
$$\Delta E_{n\to n\pm1}=\inf_{\Gamma:n\to n\pm1}\ \max_{s\in[0,1]}\left(F[\Gamma(s)]-F_n\right)$$
for the actual identity-sector free-energy functional, followed by thermal, driven and quantum transition-rate estimates $\Gamma_{n\to n\pm1}=\Gamma_{\rm thermal}+\Gamma_{\rm driven}+\Gamma_{\rm quantum}$. Changing $W_{\rm vor}$ normally requires a phase slip through a zero of the order-parameter amplitude, vortex passage across the loop or boundary escape; changing $h_F$ requires frame degeneration, core crossing, reconnection or boundary escape; changing $w_{\rm tex}$ requires a singularity, target-space escape or boundary leakage. A topological label alone does not provide finite-size energetic stability.

**BEB.6d Physical status and closure gates.** The topology and Theorem BEB.6.1 are Tier 1 under their declared hypotheses; their realization by the Identity Polaron, the phason field, the CISS channel, a Zeno-type drive or the tubulin network is Tier 3/open. Closure requires: (1) declaring which of $W_{\rm vor}$, $w_{\rm tex}$ or $h_F$ is the physical state; (2) supplying its configuration space, domain, boundary condition, orientation and reference; (3) deriving the operator and projectors $\hat\Pi_n$; (4) evaluating all Hamiltonian and Lindblad off-diagonal sector matrix elements; (5) deriving a transition barrier and lifetime under the biological bath and drive; (6) preparing and blindly reading at least two signed sectors; and (7) showing how the proposed CISS/Zeno operation writes or reads the sector without erasing it during recombination.

for an isolated quantum system under projective measurement. In a biological

$J(\omega)$.
For a **super-Ohmic** bath ($J(\omega) \propto \omega^s$, $s > 1$), rapid
measurements at rate $\nu_{Zeno}$ can increase coupling to high-frequency
modes, *reducing* coherence — the Anti-Zeno Effect.

 the scan range. A discrete hyperfine spectrum has no power-law exponent;
 the earlier Ohmic ($s\approx1$) and sub-Ohmic ($s\approx0.5$) labels were
 unsourced and are withdrawn. A measured $J(\omega)$ is required.

## BEB.11 Ordinary CISS Material-Response Channel; GCT Coupling Open [Tier 3]

This section records ordinary spin-orbit/CISS transport observables in the α-helical tubulin backbone (both α- and β-tubulin monomers contribute α-helical secondary structure to the microtubule lattice; the Dual Material Constraint candidate controls operate at the heterodimer scale). These observables need not require long-lived radical-pair coherence. They do not define a phason-winding coupling: the CISS-to-phason map, its coefficient, normalization and rate are not derived here (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3) and remain a Tier 3/Tier 4 physical-link target, pending the typed, normalized, measured coupling (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3) and O.23. The symbol $g_{CISS}$ below denotes an ordinary current-generated Zeeman-frequency scenario, not a derived phason coupling.

### BEB.11.1 Spin-Orbit Coupling in Helical Peptide Bonds

The spin-orbit Hamiltonian for an electron in the electrostatic potential $V(\mathbf{r})$ of the peptide chain is:
$$\hat{H}_{SO} = \frac{\hbar}{4 m_e^2 c^2} \nabla V \times \hat{\mathbf{p}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\sigma}}$$

For the α-helix geometry, the net electrostatic gradient $\nabla V$ along the helical axis is non-zero due to the net dipole moment of each amide bond (~3.7 D per residue). This asymmetry creates a momentum-dependent effective magnetic field:
$$\mathbf{B}_{SO} = \frac{\hbar}{2 m_e c^2 e} (\nabla V \times \mathbf{k})$$

The CISS effect amplifies this spin-orbit field through the collective helical geometry. For a peptide helix with $n_{res}$ residues and pitch $p$, the spin-split conductance is (Naaman et al.):
$$\Delta G_{CISS} = G_\uparrow - G_\downarrow \approx P_{CISS} \times G_0$$

where the operative protein-band value is $P_{CISS} \in [0.05, 0.20]$ for α-helical protein/peptide systems, while $P_{CISS} \approx 0.6$ is retained only as a DNA-equivalent ordered-helix stress-test upper edge. This protein-band value is a literature-calibrated Tier 3 input; no engine protocol currently verifies it, and the CISS-to-phason map remains open pending the typed, normalized, measured coupling (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3) and O.23. The DNA-equivalent stress edge is barred from tubulin defaults unless direct tubulin current, redox handle, and phason-coupling calibration are measured on the same substrate. Source anchors by band: Naaman-Paltiel-Waldeck 2019 *Nat. Rev. Chem.* 3:250 is the review anchor; Göhler et al. 2011 *Science* 331:894 reports $\sim 55$–$61\%$ on ordered-helical dsDNA SAMs and sets only the DNA-equivalent stress edge; Mishra et al. 2013 *PNAS* 110:14872 reports bacteriorhodopsin near the mid-teen-percent scale; Kettner et al. 2018 *J. Phys. Chem. Lett.* 9:2025 gives helicene monolayer values in the single-digit to mid-teen-percent band; Aragonès et al. 2017 *Small* 13:1602519 supports the single-chiral-oligopeptide $\sim 5$–$20\%$ operative protein/peptide band. $G_0 = 2e^2/h$ is the conductance quantum.

### BEB.11.2 Ordinary Current/Field Estimate (scenario $g_{CISS}$; not a phason coupling)

Given a measured current and geometry, one may estimate an ordinary magnetic flux and Zeeman frequency; mapping that to a phason coupling would additionally require the missing interaction and normalization. For tubulin's helical geometry the effective magnetic flux is $\Phi_B \sim J_{CISS}\cdot L_{\rm dimer}\cdot \mu_0/(4\pi)$, and the field over the coupling area $A_{\rm dimer}$ is $B_{\rm eff} = \Phi_B/A_{\rm dimer}$. The Zeeman-like coupling is
$$g_{CISS} = \left(\frac{\mu_B B_{\rm eff}}{\hbar}\right)\eta_{\rm geom} = \left(\frac{\mu_B \Phi_B}{\hbar\,A_{\rm dimer}}\right)\eta_{\rm geom},$$

an angular frequency, with cyclic frequency $g_{CISS}/2\pi$. The area is required rather than incidental: $\mu_B\Phi_B/\hbar$ alone carries units of m$^2$/s.
where $\eta_{\rm geom}$ is the geometric overlap of the radical-pair spin operator with the induced B-field. With $L_{\rm dimer}=8$ nm, $A_{\rm dimer}=16$ nm², $J_{CISS}=P_{CISS}\times2e^2/h\times V_{\rm bias}$ (a per-dimer current; $V_{\rm bias}=50$ mV bench-transport calibration), the spin-polarized current vanishes at $P_{CISS}=0$ and reaches the full conductance channel only at perfect polarization. Evaluated at $\eta_{\rm geom}=1$, this expression gives cyclic frequencies of $1.4\times10^5$, $5.4\times10^5$ and $1.6\times10^6$ Hz for $P_{CISS}=0.05$, $0.20$ and $0.60$. Reaching the full $10^1$–$10^3$ Hz scale across this input band would require $\eta_{\rm geom}$ spanning approximately $6.1\times10^{-6}$–$7.4\times10^{-3}$, and no derived or measured value for $\eta_{\rm geom}$ is supplied here. The scale of $g_{CISS}$ is therefore not closed: this is a Tier 3 dimensional construction of an ordinary current/field response whose overlap factor, and with it the in-vivo magnitude, awaits a derived or measured $\eta_{\rm geom}$ (tracked with O.23 in the §BEB.11.4 table). It is not a phason coupling.

### BEB.11.3 No Derived Classical Phason Floor

As defined, $g_{CISS}$ depends only on $J_{CISS}$, $\mu_B$ and geometric constants, not on $T_2$, so $\lim_{T_2 \to 0} g_{CISS} = g_{CISS}^{(0)}$, which is non-zero provided $\eta_{\rm geom} > 0$ (expected on symmetry grounds, not established here). If a driven chiral device carries a non-zero current as $T_2\to0$, an ordinary current-generated magnetic response can therefore persist. That limit does not establish a non-zero phason coupling or phason-winding efficiency; no GCT floor follows without the missing interaction and normalization (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3; O.23).

The Tavis-Cummings cooperativity ratio $g_{coll}/\kappa$ evaluated in `GCT_Physics_Engine/src/protocol_eta_zeno.py` (with $g_{coll} = g_{single}\sqrt{N_{bio}}$ the collective Rabi coupling and $\kappa$ the cavity decay rate) is a conditional external-rate scenario: it reproduces supplied inputs and is not a physical coupling margin. The bare Misra-Sudarshan extension $\tau_Z^2/\tau_{\rm meas}$ of §BEB.2b is a separate diagnostic. Neither quantity is what a Protocol A-Prime outcome measures; the protocol measures ordinary chirality-correlated current, spin and $T_2$ response.

## BEB.12 Hyperfine Characteristic Frequency and Operational Crossover [Tier 3]

The Trp radical-pair singlet-triplet dynamics define a *hyperfine characteristic frequency* $\nu_{hf}$ that sets the natural scale of the bare interaction Hamiltonian. We compute $\nu_{hf}$ here as the Tier 3 material input to the bare inverse-Zeno diagnostic of V3 Ch13 §13.4.3/§13.4.7 (the former drive-window anti-Zeno test is a declared open programme there). A shifted *operational* Zeno-to-anti-Zeno crossover is defined only inside the hypothetical protected-subspace model of V1 §17.1.3c, conditional on App ORQ Open Problem O.23; no physical Zeno clock, protected channel or GCT rate is thereby supplied.

**1. Hyperfine Characteristic Frequency**
For a spin system with $H_{int} = H_{hf} = \sum_k A_k\,\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf I_k$, the cyclic characteristic frequency is defined by the singlet-state Hamiltonian standard deviation,
$$ f_{hf} \equiv \sigma_H/h = \tfrac12\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_k A_k^2\, I_k(I_k+1)}, $$
which sets $\tau_Z=\hbar/\sigma_H=1/(2\pi f_{hf})$ in §13.4.3. A mean or rms over the coupling list (the $\bar A$ of item 2) is not this quantity.

**2. FAD/Trp Radical-Pair Literature Reference Band**
The N5/N10 hyperfine constants are FAD semiquinone literature values, used here only as an order-of-magnitude reference band for singlet-triplet mixing. Trp indole radicals have different atom labels and require the assembled-MT partner geometry of O.21 before a residue-specific table is claimed. Reference scale:
- $A_N(\text{N5}) \approx 42$ MHz (FAD semiquinone nitrogen-5 reference)
- $A_N(\text{N10}) \approx 28$ MHz (FAD semiquinone nitrogen-10 reference)
- $A_H(\text{H5}) \approx 12$ MHz (aromatic proton reference)
- Additional proton couplings ($\approx 6$–$8$ MHz each, 3–4 nuclei)

$$ \bar A = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum A_{couplings}^2} \approx 20.3 \text{ MHz}\ (N=7), \qquad \sigma_H/h = \tfrac12\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_k A_k^2\, I_k(I_k+1)} \approx 36 \text{ MHz}.$$

The first expression is a mean coupling, not the Hamiltonian variance: dividing by $N$ makes added nuclei lower it, which is backwards. The singlet-state variance of $H=\sum_k A_k\,\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf I_k$ is the second expression, $\approx36.3$–$36.7$ MHz for this list (two $I=1$ nitrogens, $I=\tfrac12$ protons; Tier 1 arithmetic on imported couplings, which are not checked here as isotropic values). For the Trp side, the DFT-based isotropic effective couplings of Wong, Benjamin & Hore (2023, *Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.* 25:975–982) are $0.97$ mT ($\approx27$ MHz) for TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ and $0.70$ mT ($\approx20$ MHz) for FAD$^{\bullet-}$: the Trp radical couples *more* strongly than FAD, not less.

The bare Zeno time is therefore $\tau_Z^{\text{bare}}=1/(2\pi f_{hf})$. The engine uses a declared placeholder $\Delta_{ST}/h\approx30$ MHz, which is the plain rms of the three FAD couplings above ($\sqrt{(42^2+28^2+12^2)/3}\approx30.0$ MHz), not a Trp measurement; it lies within about 10% of the TrpH$^{\bullet+}$ effective coupling ($\approx27$ MHz, which would give $\tau_Z\approx5.85$ ns and $\nu^*\approx2.9\times10^{11}$ Hz). With the 20.3 MHz mean value instead, $\tau_Z^{\text{bare}}\approx7.84$ ns and $\nu^*_{\text{bare}}\approx1.6\times10^{11}$ Hz; with the 36 MHz variance, $\tau_Z\approx4.4$ ns. None of these changes the inverse-Zeno conclusion. Using the engine placeholder gives $\tau_Z^{\text{bare}}\approx1/[2\pi(30\,\text{MHz})]\approx5.305$ ns and the quadratic-model diagnostic $\nu^*_{\text{bare}}=T_2/\tau_Z^2\approx3.6\times10^{11}$ Hz — far above the recombination rate $\Gamma_{rec}\approx10^8$ s$^{-1}$. Facchi & Pascazio (2008 §2.2.5, eq. 19) define the physical crossover only implicitly by $\gamma_{\rm eff}(\tau^*)=\gamma$; the displayed $T_2/\tau_Z^2$ value additionally identifies the relevant golden-rule population-decay rate with $1/T_2$ [Tier 3 channel-matching assumption]. The recombination channel acting on the *bare* radical-pair Hamiltonian therefore sits in the inverse-Zeno regime within this diagnostic, as confirmed by the bare Misra-Sudarshan estimate of §13.4.3 ($\tau_{eff}^{\text{bare MS}}\approx2.8$ ns).

**3. Operational Crossover under Candidate Protected-Subspace Mechanism**
The biologically relevant crossover would be shifted into the kHz–MHz band only if the protected-subspace effective coupling $\Omega_{\text{DFS}} \ll \omega_{hf}$ is supplied by the candidate chiral phonon-polariton DFS mechanism of V1 §17.1.3c. This DFS comparison uses angular rates explicitly: $\tau_Z^{\rm DFS}=1/\Omega_{\rm DFS}$ and the quadratic-model operational crossover frequency is $\nu^*_{\text{DFS}}=T_2\Omega_{\rm DFS}^2$; it is therefore *conditional on closure of App ORQ Open Problem O.23*. The explicit Lindblad small-$N$ solve has not demonstrated DFS suppression, and the collective-dressing operative band is reached only in the long 50-$\mu$m-MT regime; under the operational target $\Omega_{\text{DFS}} \sim 10^5$ rad/s, $\nu^*_{\text{DFS}}$ would lie in the kHz band, but this remains a Tier 3/Open condition rather than an established protected-subspace Zeno regime.

**Former Prediction P.8 crossover comparison (declared open programme).** The comparison of $T_2$ in the A-Prime branch windows ($112 \pm 10$ MHz or $42 \pm 10$ MHz) against a 50 kHz drive read the drive frequency as a Zeno sampling rate, which it is not; it is a declared open programme in V3 Ch13 §13.4.7 and supports no decision. The $\nu^*_{\rm DFS}$ arithmetic above applies only to a physical measurement channel. Rejection of the registered biophysical branch (F1) still requires the three-conjunct joint null specified in Protocol A-Prime (no peak in Branch A, no peak in Branch B, and no chirality contrast; 150 MHz is diagnostic only). Neither outcome is a verdict on GCT as a whole: the measurement tests an ordinary material proxy, and no phason, Selection-Operator or Level-II inference follows from it (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3). A preregistered null rejects only the registered biophysical branch, and only under that branch's registered decision rule (the three-conjunct joint null above).

## BEB.13 Geomagnetic Bias as an Ordinary Material-Control Hypothesis [Tier 3]

One material-control hypothesis asks whether an external symmetry-breaking field could bias a candidate radical-pair preparation at $310$ K. The ambient **geomagnetic field** ($\sim 50\ \mu\text{T}$) supplies an ordinary electron-Zeeman splitting of order $1.4$ MHz, not the 100 MHz scan cadence.

By analogy with radical-pair models of avian magnetoreception, this field may be included as a weak spin-axis control and tested against shielded or rotated-field conditions. No result currently shows that it is required, that it seeds a protected subspace, or that it hands off to internal phason/DFS dynamics. The registered A-Prime branch frequencies remain externally registered material-scan settings; no phason-driven loop, Selection mechanism or GCT validation follows.

#### PUP.1 Statement

Let $\Sigma_\infty = \varprojlim (S^1, z \mapsto z^n)$ denote the universal Adelic Solenoid (App TAS §TAS.1). By Pontryagin duality (App TAS §TAS.2),
$$\Sigma_\infty \;\cong\; (\mathbb{R} \times \hat{\mathbb{Z}})/\mathbb{Z}.$$
For each $n \geq 1$, let $X_n \cong S^1$ denote the $n$-th term in the inverse system, and let $p_n: \Sigma_\infty \to X_n$ be the canonical projection. For each $n$, the configuration space of an Identity Polaron at finite resolution $n$ is the product
$$M_n \;:=\; X_n \times E_\parallel \;\cong\; S^1 \times \mathbb{R}^3,$$
where $E_\parallel \cong \mathbb{R}^3$ is the physical projection slice of the adopted icosahedral cut-and-project ansatz (Parameter Ledger P1; App FTH §FTH.3; cf. Theorem FTH.1 for the conditional knot-dimension bound). Let $q_{nm}:M_m\to M_n$ be the ambient bonding maps and $\widetilde\Sigma_\infty:=\varprojlim_n(M_n,q_{nm})$. Projected knot cores and deleted supports are typed separately below.

Dimensional clarification: $M_n$ is a four-dimensional product. This appendix adopts one geometry consistently:
$$H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}:\quad \mathscr D_n:=X_n\times K_n\subset M_n,$$
where $K_n\subset E_\parallel$ is the projected framed-ribbon core and $\mathscr D_n$ is its full identity-fibre support. Consequently
$$M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n=X_n\times(E_\parallel\setminus K_n).$$
This **full-fibre complement hypothesis** is not the incompatible fixed-slice deletion $M_n\setminus(\{x_n^0\}\times K_n)$. The latter retains every point $(x,k)$ with $x\ne x_n^0$ and does not have the displayed product form. The formal proposition below is conditional on $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$; establishing that the physical Polaron carries full-fibre support, or replacing it with a genuine four-dimensional fixed-slice complement calculation, remains an O.18 modelling target.

Assume also $q_{nm}^{-1}(\mathscr D_n)=\mathscr D_m$. Then $q_{nm}$ restricts to the complements. Set
$$\mathscr D_\mathcal K:=\varprojlim_n\mathscr D_n,\qquad
\widetilde\Sigma_\infty\setminus\mathscr D_\mathcal K\cong\varprojlim_n(M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n).$$

> **Proposition PUP.1 (Polaron Unity Proposition, revised; conditional on O.18 and $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$) [Tier 3 conditional; part (ii) withdrawn].**
> *Let $\mathscr D_\mathcal K\subset\widetilde\Sigma_\infty$ be the inverse limit of complement-compatible full-fibre supports $\mathscr D_n=X_n\times K_n$. Then:*
>
> *(i) **Complement fundamental pro-group.** The inverse-limit topological group*
> $$\Pi_\mathcal K:=\varprojlim_n\pi_1(M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n),$$
> *is freely indecomposable: it admits no non-trivial free-product decomposition $G_1 * G_2$ with $G_1, G_2 \neq 1$.*
>
> *(ii) **Withdrawn.** The former claim that the canonical representation space $\mathcal H_\mathcal K$ of the represented quotient $\Gamma_\mathcal K$ admits no $\Gamma_\mathcal K$-equivariant tensor product decomposition is withdrawn. The bridge it relied on is false (§PUP.4.2, Counterexample PUP.4.2.B). No Hilbert-space non-factorizability statement is made in this appendix.*
>
> *(iii) **Uniqueness of the invariant normalized density (conditional lemma).** If $\mathcal M=\rho(\Gamma_\mathcal K)''$ is a finite factor with normalized trace $\tau$, a positive, unit-trace, Zeno-invariant density $R_{\rm inv}\in\mathcal M$ commuting with $\rho(\Gamma_\mathcal K)$ is uniquely $\mathbf1$. This is a density/state statement, not a uniqueness theorem for the canonical non-unitary Selection Operator $\mathcal F_{sel}=\mathcal P_{actualize}\circ\mathcal U_{steer}$. For the trefoil its hypothesis fails in the regular representation of $\Gamma_\mathcal K=B_3$, because $L(B_3)$ is not a factor (O.36, §PUP.6); (iii) therefore applies only to a factorial sector that has not been physically identified.*

The argument proceeds via four lemmata and one finite-level remark (§PUP.3). Lemmata PUP.3.2, PUP.3.4, and PUP.3.5 have the scopes stated below; Remark PUP.3.3 records finite-level evidence without pretending to prove an inverse-limit theorem. Lemma PUP.3.1 is conditional on the explicitly adopted full-fibre hypothesis $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$. Lemma PUP.3.4 — the identification of the abstract Gelfand–Naimark–Segal (GNS) representation associated with $\mathcal{K}$ with the *physical* phason Hilbert space — remains an open structural gap. Section PUP.4.2 records why the former direct-product/operator-factor step is false rather than open. O.35 (unique trace) and O.36 (factoriality of the regular algebra) fail as posed for the represented trefoil group $\Gamma_\mathcal K=B_3$ and hold for the further central quotient $B_3/Z(B_3)\cong C_2*C_3$ (§PUP.6). Together with the Anderson-Putnam extension to $S^3 \setminus K$ (Open Problem O.18) and the canonicity assignment $K \mapsto \mathcal{A}_K$, these items define the conditional structure on which parts (i) and (iii) rest.

> **Claim ceiling.** Even with every listed closure, the content of this appendix is at most an algebraic unity candidate. No theorem here identifies an Identity Polaron, an owner, one subject, any other subject count, or Level II Apperception; those require independent physical and phenomenal bridges (V1 Ch16 §16.2.7).

#### PUP.2 Preliminaries

##### PUP.2.1 The Adelic Solenoid revisited

The space $\Sigma_\infty$ is the inverse limit of the system $\{X_n, f_{nm}\}_{n \mid m}$ where $X_n \cong S^1$ and $f_{nm}(z) = z^{m/n}$. As a topological group,
$$\Sigma_\infty \;\cong\; (\mathbb{R} \times \hat{\mathbb{Z}})/\mathbb{Z},$$
with $\hat{\mathbb{Z}} = \varprojlim \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ the profinite completion of the integers. The space is compact, connected, but not locally path-connected; locally, $\Sigma_\infty \cong \mathbb{R} \times \mathcal{C}$ where $\mathcal{C}$ is a Cantor set (App TAS §TAS.1).

The three inverse-limit objects used here must be kept distinct. The profinite group
$$\hat{\mathbb Z}=\varprojlim_n\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$$
is the totally disconnected fibre (address group) in the quotient presentation above. The Čech/shape fundamental invariant of $\Sigma_\infty$ is instead the pro-group represented by
$$\bigl\{\pi_1(X_n)\cong\mathbb Z,\ (f_{nm})_*=\times(m/n)\bigr\}_{n\mid m}.$$
It is this inverse system, rather than a single group isomorphic to $\hat{\mathbb Z}$, that shape theory assigns to the solenoid. Finally, the ordinary group inverse limit of this integer system is trivial: compatibility would require an integer divisible by every positive degree. These statements concern the solenoid itself and do not classify the later knot-complement pro-group. [Tier 1 — Standard inverse-limit and shape theory.]

##### PUP.2.2 The augmented configuration space

A Polaron at finite resolution $n$ is a framed ribbon embedded in the augmented configuration space
$$M_n \;=\; X_n \times E_\parallel \;\cong\; S^1 \times \mathbb{R}^3.$$
The $S^1$ factor records the identity-fiber coordinate at depth $n$; the $\mathbb{R}^3$ factor is the physical slice. The augmented inverse-limit space
$$\widetilde{\Sigma}_\infty \;:=\; \varprojlim_n M_n \;=\; \Sigma_\infty \times E_\parallel$$
is the proposed home of the Polaron knot, replacing the heuristic phrase "$\mathcal{K} \subset \Sigma_\infty$" that appears in the Chapter 11 statement. The replacement is motivated, not forced: knotting of one-dimensional defects needs a three-dimensional ambient slice (cf. Theorem FTH.1), and the bare solenoid $\Sigma_\infty$ has local Lebesgue dimension one, so a knot cannot sit in $\Sigma_\infty$ itself. The physical slice $E_\parallel \cong \mathbb{R}^3$ supplies the three transverse dimensions, while the solenoid fiber records the identity address. That a physical Polaron is confined to such a slice, with the support required by $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, is a Tier 3 modelling hypothesis under O.18; the Chapter 11 Polaron ansatz does not establish it. A single fixed-slice copy of the knot does not give the product complement (§PUP.1). Within the model, this is the sense in which the Polaron is a knot "in the solenoid": it is a knot in the augmented total space whose ambient projection onto the identity factor recovers the address path of Chapter 7 §7.4.

##### PUP.2.3 Definition of the Polaron knot $\mathcal{K}$

> **Definition PUP.2.3 (Polaron knot and full-fibre support).** A Polaron knot is an inverse system $\mathcal{K}=(K_n,\iota_{nm})$ where:
> 1. For each $n$, $K_n\subset E_\parallel$ is the core $\kappa_n(S^1\times\{\tfrac12\})$ of a smoothly embedded framed ribbon $\kappa_n:S^1\times[0,1]\hookrightarrow E_\parallel$ and is a tame prime knot in the standard three-dimensional sense (Burde–Zieschang, *Knots*, §3).
> 2. The bonding maps $\iota_{nm}:K_m\to K_n$ form a coherent system induced by the declared finite-resolution construction.
> 3. Under $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, the corresponding deleted defect support in $M_n$ is $\mathscr D_n=X_n\times K_n$. This full-fibre support, rather than a single-slice copy $\{x_n^0\}\times K_n$, is the object whose complement is used below.
> 3a. Ambient bonding maps satisfy $q_{nm}^{-1}(\mathscr D_n)=\mathscr D_m$, hence restrict to maps of supports and complements.
> 4. The framing is non-trivial: the linking number of the two ribbon edges $\kappa_n(S^1 \times \{0\})$ and $\kappa_n(S^1 \times \{1\})$ (with $\kappa_n$ the ribbon embedding of item 1) equals $N$, the braid index of the underlying Polaron condensate.

The condition that the projected core be prime at each finite level is the rigorous translation of the Chapter 11 §11.12.2 phrase "the link reduces to an irreducible knot whose peripheral structure is trivial only for the full $N$-component system." Primeness is asserted for $K_n\subset E_\parallel$, while the complement calculation is asserted for its full-fibre support $\mathscr D_n\subset M_n$; the two object types are not conflated. Primeness of a knot is not the same as irreducibility of its exterior (§PUP.3, scope note after Lemma PUP.3.2); the free-indecomposability step uses only the latter, which holds for prime and composite knots alike.

##### PUP.2.4 The Wirtinger pro-system

For each $n$, $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$ gives the product complement exactly:
$$M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n=X_n\times(E_\parallel\setminus K_n).$$
Its knot-group factor admits a **Wirtinger presentation**
$$G(K_n)=\pi_1(E_\parallel\setminus K_n)=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_{k_n}\mid r_1^{(n)},\ldots,r_{k_n-1}^{(n)}\rangle,$$
where the $x_i$ are meridians of $K_n$ and the $r_j^{(n)}$ are the crossing relations (Burde–Zieschang §3.B). The bonding maps induce group homomorphisms
$$\varphi_{nm}:\pi_1(M_m\setminus\mathscr D_m)\to\pi_1(M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n).$$
Define the complement fundamental pro-group
$$\Pi_\mathcal K:=\varprojlim_n\pi_1(M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n).$$
The finite-level knot groups are generally infinite, so this inverse limit is not called profinite. A profinite group would require a separately constructed inverse system of finite quotients or completions. [Tier 3 conditional; inverse-limit free indecomposability remains open.]

##### PUP.2.5 The canonical phason representation $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}$

In the model, each meridian generator $x_i$ is posited to act on phason modes of the lattice as a holonomy of a phason gauge connection around the knot core, and the action is posited to be unitary for the phason inner product. Both are Tier 3 modelling hypotheses: no phason gauge connection around a knot core has been derived, and no engine calculation establishes this holonomy representation. Let
$$\rho:\Gamma_\mathcal K\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H_\mathcal K)$$
denote this posited unitary representation, where $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}$ is constructed as follows.

> **Definition PUP.2.5 (Canonical phason Hilbert space).** Let $\mathcal{A}_\mathcal{K} := C^*_r(\Gamma_\mathcal{K})$ denote the reduced group C\*-algebra of the represented discrete knot group after the central $\mathbb{Z}$ factor supplied by the full-fibre product complement has been quotiented out. For the trefoil this group is the knot group $\Gamma_\mathcal K=B_3$ itself, whose own centre $\langle\Delta^2\rangle\cong\mathbb Z$ is nontrivial. The Zeno boundary condition (§PUP.2.6) was intended to select a distinguished tracial state $\tau$ on $\mathcal{A}_\mathcal{K}$ through the unique-trace hypothesis registered as O.35; for $B_3$ that hypothesis fails (§PUP.2.6, §PUP.6), so $\tau$ below denotes the canonical regular trace, chosen rather than selected. The canonical phason Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}$ is the GNS Hilbert space of $(\mathcal{A}_\mathcal{K}, \tau)$.

This construction is standard in operator-algebraic representation theory (Brown–Ozawa, *C\*-algebras and Finite-Dimensional Approximations*, §1.5).

##### PUP.2.6 The Zeno boundary condition

The hypothesised Zeno Drive of Chapter 17 §17.1.2 (Tier 3) is modelled as imposing a continuous projective measurement of the singlet state of the Trp radical pair network. The picture uses the historical 100 MHz material-scan scenario (the imported $\sim10^8$ s${}^{-1}$ spin-selective recombination timescale of the radical-pair scenario) as a placeholder only; it is not an operating Zeno cadence, and no Zeno measurement rate is derived (V1 Ch17 §17.1.3; V3 Ch13 §13.4.7). Mathematically, the model treats the boundary as a conditional expectation onto the represented trace-bearing algebra:
$$\mathbb{E}_{Zeno}: \mathcal{A}_\mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_\mathcal{K}).$$
That the physical Zeno map equals such a trace-preserving conditional expectation is itself a Tier 3 hypothesis.

> **Definition PUP.2.6 (Zeno Boundary) [Tier 3 modelling hypothesis; its physical Zeno-Drive realization is Tier 3].** The Zeno boundary is proposed to select a distinguished faithful normalized trace on $\mathcal{A}_\mathcal{K}=C^*_r(\Gamma_\mathcal{K})$, the reduced group C\*-algebra of the represented discrete quotient introduced in Definition PUP.2.5 after quotienting the full-fibre product's central $\mathbb{Z}$ factor. That trace would be *the* unique one only if condition (a) below held; for the trefoil group $B_3$ condition (a) fails, so no unique trace exists and the selection is hypothetical. The pro-group $\Pi_\mathcal K$ supplies inverse-system control data; the BKKO theorem is invoked only for $\Gamma_\mathcal K$, and would require:
> (a) $\Gamma_\mathcal{K}$ has the unique-trace property, equivalently trivial amenable radical in the Breuillard-Kalantar-Kennedy-Ozawa theorem (2017, Theorem 1.3, arXiv:1410.2518). C\*-simplicity is a stronger separate condition and is not asserted here; and
> (b) the central $\mathbb{Z}$ factor introduced by the full-fibre product split in Lemma PUP.3.1 is explicitly quotiented out before the trace is taken.
>
> Residual finiteness is not required to define the displayed pro-system or to invoke the BKKO unique-trace criterion for the represented discrete quotient. It becomes relevant only for an optional route through separating finite quotients or a separately constructed profinite completion, and it is not sufficient for trace uniqueness. Trivial amenable radical in the sense of BKKO is the operative condition, registered as Open Problem **O.35**. For the trefoil the represented group is $B_3$, whose centre $\langle\Delta^2\rangle\cong\mathbb Z$ is a nontrivial amenable normal subgroup. Its amenable radical is therefore nontrivial, condition (a) fails, and $C^*_r(B_3)$ does not have a unique trace. O.35 as posed thereby fails for the represented group $B_3$ [Tier 1 — standard]. A further quotient by the knot group's own centre is a possible repair route: for $B_3/Z(B_3)\cong C_2*C_3$ the amenable radical is trivial, so O.35/O.36 hold there [Tier 1 — standard]. That route is not developed in this edition, and whether any physical sector is that quotient's regular representation is open [Tier 3].

> **Definition PUP.2.6b (Invariant normalized density).** Let $R_{\rm inv}\in L(\Gamma_\mathcal K)$ be the density, relative to $\tau$, of a normal state that is:
> (a) positive,
> (b) of unit trace under $\tau$,
> (c) invariant under the Zeno conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}_{Zeno}$, and
> (d) invariant for the represented knot-group action: $[R_{\rm inv},\rho(g)]=0$ for every $g\in\Gamma_\mathcal K$.

Proposition PUP.1(iii) says these conditions determine $R_{\rm inv}$ whenever the represented algebra is a finite factor; for the trefoil regular representation it is not (§PUP.6). The canonical Selection Operator is instead the non-unitary branch-selecting process $\mathcal F_{sel}=\mathcal P_{actualize}\circ\mathcal U_{steer}$ (Ch06 §6.4.1; Ch10 §10.4.1); it is not a normalized density and is not proved equal to the identity here.

#### PUP.3 Lemmata

##### Lemma PUP.3.1 (Wirtinger presentation at each finite level) [Tier 3 conditional on $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$]

*For each $n \geq 1$, if the defect support satisfies $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, the group $\pi_1(M_n \setminus \mathscr D_n)$ is
$$\pi_1(M_n \setminus \mathscr D_n)\cong\mathbb Z\times G(K_n),$$
where $G(K_n)$ has the finite Wirtinger presentation
$$G(K_n)=\langle x_1, \ldots, x_{k_n} \mid w_i x_{\sigma(i)} w_i^{-1} = x_{\tau(i)},\; i = 1, \ldots, k_n - 1 \rangle.$$
The $x_i$ are meridians and the relations are determined by crossings of a planar projection of the projected knot core $K_n\subset E_\parallel$.*

*Proof.* By $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, $\mathscr D_n=X_n\times K_n$ and hence
$$M_n\setminus\mathscr D_n=X_n\times(E_\parallel\setminus K_n).$$
With $\pi_1(X_n)\cong\mathbb Z$, the product theorem gives the displayed $\mathbb Z\times G(K_n)$ split. The $X_n$ generator commutes with every meridian, and the presentation of $G(K_n)$ is the classical Wirtinger presentation (Burde–Zieschang §3.B). No product claim is made for deletion of a single fixed-slice ribbon or for an arbitrary four-dimensional ribbon embedding. $\square$

A useful conditional corollary: after quotienting the central $\mathbb{Z}$ generator under $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, the finite-level group is the classical knot group $G(K_n)$. We use this corollary only with that hypothesis in force.

##### Lemma PUP.3.2 (Kneser–Stallings: knot groups are freely indecomposable) [Tier 1]

*Let $K \subset S^3$ (equivalently $\mathbb{R}^3$) be a knot (prime or composite). Then the knot group $G(K) = \pi_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus K)$ is **freely indecomposable**: there exist no non-trivial subgroups $H_1, H_2 < G(K)$ such that $G(K) = H_1 * H_2$.*

*Proof.* This is a classical theorem of 3-manifold topology, resting on Kneser's conjecture, proved by Stallings (1959; see also Stallings 1971) with the boundary case by Heil (1972): a free-product decomposition of the fundamental group of a compact 3-manifold is realized geometrically by an essential embedded 2-sphere or properly embedded disc. Stallings' proof uses the Papakyriakopoulos sphere/loop-theorem machinery (Loop Theorem: Papakyriakopoulos 1957, generalized by Stallings 1960), but the step used here is Kneser's conjecture, not the Loop Theorem itself. The argument: the exterior $X_K = S^3 \setminus N(K)$ (where $N(K)$ is an open tubular neighborhood) is irreducible (Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, §1.2), which rules out an essential 2-sphere. For a non-trivial knot its torus boundary is incompressible, which rules out an essential disc; for the unknot $G(K)\cong\mathbb Z$, which is freely indecomposable directly. Hence $G(K)$ is freely indecomposable. $\square$

> **Scope of the hypothesis.** Irreducibility of the exterior is not equivalent to primeness of $K$: exteriors of composite knots are irreducible as well, and a connected sum is detected in the exterior by an essential decomposing annulus rather than by a 2-sphere. Kneser–Milnor decomposes 3-manifolds along spheres and does not supply that equivalence. Free indecomposability above follows from irreducibility of the exterior (with boundary incompressibility for a non-trivial knot, or $G(K)\cong\mathbb Z$ for the unknot), not from primeness; where primeness itself is needed it is taken through the annular criterion, not inferred from irreducibility.

This is the deepest classical ingredient. The proof rests on Kneser's conjecture (Stallings' theorem, whose proof uses the Papakyriakopoulos–Stallings loop/sphere-theorem machinery) together with irreducibility and boundary-incompressibility of knot exteriors, all foundational results in three-manifold topology.

##### Remark PUP.3.3 (Finite-resolution free-indecomposability control; no inverse-limit theorem) [Tier 1 finite-level fact; inverse-limit closure open under O.18]

For the registered inverse system $\{G_n,\varphi_{nm}\}$, Lemma PUP.3.2 proves free indecomposability separately for each finite-resolution knot group $G_n$. This sentence is only a record of those finite-level facts; it is not an implication about $\widehat G=\varprojlim_nG_n$. Whether $\widehat G$ is freely indecomposable requires an additional inverse-limit theorem for this actual pro-system and remains an O.18 closure target.

> **Remark PUP.3.3.A [Tier classification].** Finite-level Kneser–Stallings control is Tier 1. Inverse-limit promotion is Tier 3/O.18 and requires a theorem for the actual pro-system $\Pi_\mathcal K$. Profinite Bass–Serre results do not apply unless finite completions are separately constructed.

##### Lemma PUP.3.4 (Identification of canonical and physical phason representations) [Tier 3 conditional pending O.18 full-fibre-support closure + finite quotient trace + O.32; O.35/O.36 fail as posed for the trefoil, §PUP.6]

*Let $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}^{phys}$ denote the proposed physical phason Hilbert space of a future realized Polaron branch, conditional on the full coupling and structural closure program. Let $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}^{can}$ denote the canonical GNS Hilbert space of Definition PUP.2.5. Then there exists a $\Gamma_\mathcal K$-equivariant unitary isomorphism
$$U: \mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}^{phys} \;\xrightarrow{\sim}\; \mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}^{can}$$
intertwining the physical phason holonomy action with the canonical regular representation.*

*Status.* The Lemma is the structural bridge from operator-algebraic representation theory (where Lemmata PUP.3.1–PUP.3.3 and Lemma PUP.3.5 below operate) to the *physical* Hilbert space of the Polaron condensate (where Proposition 11.12.A is to be applied). It is the analogue, for the Polaron knot, of the proposed Connes–Chamseddine spectral-triple identification of the GCT vacuum (V3 Ch06 §6.5, Tier 3; its KO-dimension-6 verification is App ORQ O.32) — and it would reduce to that identification if the spectral-triple identification were granted.

*What is reduced.* Granting the spectral-triple identification of V3 Ch06 §6.5 (Tier 3 conditional on O.32/O.5), the physical phason Hilbert space at a fixed lattice configuration is modeled by the finite-subshift analogue of the AKN tiling algebra. The full AKN tiling algebra is governed by tiling-groupoid / substitution machinery rather than being canonically identical to a Cuntz–Krieger algebra of one finite adjacency matrix (cf. Putnam, *C\*-algebras from substitution tilings*). The Polaron knot defines a specific representation of $\Pi_\mathcal K$ inside this finite-subshift analogue — namely, the holonomy representation around the meridians of $\mathcal{K}$. The required equivariance $U$ is then the GNS realization of the holonomy state.

*What is open.* The remaining gap, marked Tier 3 conditional until the registered closure stack is supplied, is the following structural verification:

> **Open structural step (the L4 gap).** Work throughout on the declared reduced group algebra $\mathcal A_\mathcal K=C_r^*(\Gamma_\mathcal K)$ and its finitely generated meridian C\*-subalgebra $B_\mathcal K=C^*(\rho(x_1),\ldots,\rho(x_k))\subset\mathcal A_\mathcal K$. First verify that the physical holonomy/Zeno state restricted to $B_\mathcal K$ equals $\tau|_{B_\mathcal K}$. If an expectation-level comparison is also required, define both conditional expectations with the same domain and codomain and prove their equality separately. Equality of restricted states and equality of conditional expectations are not equivalent statements, and neither has yet been derived from the other.

Finite generation by the $k_n$ meridian unitaries does not make $B_\mathcal K$ finite-dimensional. The trefoil $M_2(\mathbb C)$ calculation is therefore a finite-matrix surrogate only. Closing the lemma requires a faithful represented model or a controlled family of finite representations, together with convergence and trace-descent results connecting that model to $B_\mathcal K\subset\mathcal A_\mathcal K$. Until those results are supplied, the Lemma inherits the Tier 3 conditional disposition from §PUP.6.3a/b. $\square$

##### Lemma PUP.3.5 (Factoriality / central-decomposition control) [Tier 1 standard fact under its hypothesis; the hypothesis fails for the trefoil regular representation]

*Suppose $\rho$ is a primary representation of $G$ on $\mathcal{H}$. Then $\rho(G)''$ is a factor, so the represented sector has trivial center and no non-trivial direct-integral/central decomposition. This controls central decomposition; it does not by itself exclude every $G$-equivariant tensor-product factorization.*

*Remark.* The factorial-representation hypothesis is essential: a non-primary representation can have absence of tensor decomposition without $\rho(G)''$ being a factor. For example, take $G=\mathbb{Z}/2$ acting on $\mathbb{C}^2$ by $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$. Then $\rho(G)''=\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{C}$ is not a factor, but no tensor decomposition with both factors of dimension at least $2$ exists. For the represented knot group at hand, primary-representation status was registered as the closure target of **O.36**. For the trefoil, the regular representation of $\Gamma_\mathcal K=B_3$ is not primary: the infinite centre $\langle\Delta^2\rangle$ generates a diffuse centre of $L(B_3)$, so $L(B_3)$ is not a factor [Tier 1 — standard].

*Proof sketch.* For primary representations, factoriality is exactly the trivial-center condition for $\rho(G)''$ (Takesaki, *Theory of Operator Algebras I*, §V.1). A non-trivial central decomposition of a primary representation would contradict the primary hypothesis. Excluding tensor-product factorizations would require additional hypotheses on commuting subfactor pairs or on the represented tensor factors; no such exclusion follows from group-level indecomposability, because the former PUP.4.2 bridge is false (Counterexample PUP.4.2.B). The lemma is therefore a central-decomposition statement inside a represented primary sector, not a tensor-prime theorem for arbitrary unitary representations. $\square$

*Caveat on type.* This Lemma asserts factoriality, not a Murray–von Neumann type. A profinite completion of the complement pro-group has not been constructed. The represented countable discrete quotient $\Gamma_\mathcal K$ has a Type II$_1$ regular algebra only if it is i.c.c.; the trefoil group $B_3$ is not i.c.c., since its central elements have one-element conjugacy classes. At finite resolution the algebra is generally $\bigoplus_jM_{d_{n,j}}(\mathbb C)$ and is one factor only in a primary sector. Invariance places $R_{\rm inv}$ in the center; this statement does not constrain $\mathcal F_{sel}$.

#### PUP.4 Argument for Proposition PUP.1

We treat the three parts in sequence, citing the Lemmata. Part (ii) is withdrawn; §PUP.4.2 records why.

##### PUP.4.1 Proof of (i) — Free indecomposability of $\Pi_\mathcal K$

Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a Polaron knot in the sense of Definition PUP.2.3 and assume $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$. By Lemma PUP.3.1, for each finite resolution $n$, $\pi_1(M_n \setminus \mathscr D_n) \cong \mathbb{Z} \times G(K_n)$. The projected core $K_n\subset E_\parallel$ is a knot, so after quotienting the central $\mathbb Z$ factor, $G(K_n)$ is freely indecomposable by Lemma PUP.3.2 (primeness, assumed in Definition PUP.2.3, is not used in this step).

Remark PUP.3.3 records finite-level controls but no inverse-limit implication. Promotion to $\Pi_\mathcal K$ remains O.18. $\square$

##### PUP.4.2 Status of (ii) — withdrawn: the tensor-factor bridge is false

The former argument for (ii) granted Lemma PUP.3.4, so that the physical phason Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}^{phys}$ would be canonically isomorphic to the GNS Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{K}^{can}$ of the represented discrete quotient $\Gamma_\mathcal K$, and then sought to exclude every $\Gamma_\mathcal K$-equivariant tensor decomposition of that space.

Two steps were needed. First, Lemma PUP.3.2 establishes **free** indecomposability of the finite-level knot groups; it does not establish **direct-product** indecomposability. A freely indecomposable group can still split as a direct product (abelian groups supply elementary examples). Second, and decisively, the former closure target assumed that an equivariant tensor decomposition of the representation space would induce a direct-product decomposition of the group. That implication is false.

An equivariant tensor presentation means
$$U\rho(g)U^*=\rho_A(g)\otimes\rho_B(g)\qquad(g\in\Gamma),$$
with the same group acting diagonally on both factors. It does not require the group itself to decompose.

> **Counterexample PUP.4.2.B (equivariant tensor factorization without group factorization) [Tier 1].** Order the conjugacy classes of the alternating group $A_5$ (order 60) as $1A, 2A, 3A, 5A, 5B$, and write $\bar\phi=(1-\sqrt5)/2$. Among its irreducible characters are
> $$\chi_3=(3,-1,0,\phi,\bar\phi),\quad \chi_{3'}=(3,-1,0,\bar\phi,\phi),\quad \chi_4=(4,0,1,-1,-1),\quad \chi_5=(5,1,-1,0,0).$$
> Let $W=V_3\oplus V_{3'}\oplus V_4\oplus 2V_5$, so that $\chi_W=(20,0,-1,0,0)$ (using $\phi+\bar\phi=1$). Then
> $$\chi_{V_3\otimes W}=\chi_3\,\chi_W=(60,0,0,0,0)=\chi_{\rm reg}.$$
> Since a finite-group representation is determined by its character, $\ell^2(A_5)\cong V_3\otimes W$ as $A_5$-representations, with both factors non-trivial. This holds in particular for the canonical regular/GNS Hilbert space of $(C^*_r(A_5),\tau_{\rm reg})$. Yet $A_5$ is a nonabelian simple group and has no non-trivial direct-product decomposition. Hence
> $$\text{equivariant Hilbert-space tensor factorization}\;\not\Rightarrow\;\text{direct-product group factorization}.$$

The former "PUP.4.2 direct-product/operator-factor gap" (gap D of §PUP.6.3b) is therefore retired as false, not left open. Part (ii) of Proposition PUP.1 is withdrawn. Because regular representations of indecomposable groups can carry such equivariant tensor coordinates, their absence is not the right invariant for a unity claim.

> **Remark PUP.4.2.A (What a correct target would look like).** Free indecomposability remains useful because it blocks one class of fragmentation of the Polaron complement. A meaningful unity statement would instead have to concern an *observable algebra*: first produce commuting, state-compatible observable subalgebras corresponding to an independently defined physical bipartition, then show that the represented von Neumann algebra admits no decomposition into two diffuse factors along it. Such an algebraic primeness statement, even if proved, would bound only the algebra. It would not forbid arbitrary Hilbert-space tensor coordinates, and it would not supply an owner, a subject count or Level II. No construction of this kind is developed in this edition.

##### PUP.4.3 Proof of (iii) — Uniqueness of $R_{\rm inv}$ (conditional lemma)

We work in the finite von Neumann algebra $\mathcal M=\rho(\Gamma_\mathcal K)''$ acting on $\mathcal H_\mathcal K^{can}$, where $\Gamma_\mathcal K$ is the countable discrete group arising from the inverse-system control data, and we *assume* that $\mathcal M$ is a factor. O.35 and O.36 were meant to supply the distinguished trace and that factoriality. For the trefoil, neither holds in the regular representation $L(B_3)$ (§PUP.2.6, Lemma PUP.3.5), so the argument below applies only to a factorial sector whose physical identification is open [Tier 3].

**Uniqueness step.** Condition (d) in Definition PUP.2.6b gives
$$R_{\rm inv}\in\rho(\Gamma_\mathcal K)' .$$
Because $R_{\rm inv}\in\mathcal M$, it follows that $R_{\rm inv}\in Z(\mathcal M)$. If $\mathcal M$ is a factor, $R_{\rm inv}=c\mathbf1$; positivity and normalized unit trace give $c=1$. Thus $R_{\rm inv}=\mathbf1$ uniquely. This density/state proof is not a proof that $\mathcal F_{sel}=\mathbf1$.

If $\Gamma_\mathcal K$ is additionally i.c.c., its regular group von Neumann algebra is Type II$_1$ (Murray–von Neumann 1943; Takesaki §V.7.1). That type classification is separate from the uniqueness proof. At finite resolution the represented algebra is generally a direct sum of matrix blocks and is a factor only after restricting to a primary sector.

The conclusion is only that the invariant normalized density is unique. The canonical Selection Operator remains the non-unitary branch selector $\mathcal F_{sel}=\mathcal P_{actualize}\circ\mathcal U_{steer}$. $\square$

> **Remark PUP.4.3.A (Finite-resolution sanity check).** At finite resolution,
> $$L_n:=\rho_n(G(K_n))''\cong\bigoplus_jM_{d_{n,j}}(\mathbb C).$$
> It is one matrix factor only in a primary sector. Without that restriction, an equivariant density lies in the blockwise center and normalization alone need not fix all block weights, so winner-specific uniqueness is not automatic. In a primary sector, the same commutation-plus-factoriality argument gives $R_{{\rm inv},n}=\mathbf1$. It does not constrain the canonical non-unitary $\mathcal F_{sel}$. A classical knot group may remain infinite even though its represented algebra is finite dimensional; no finite-group or i.c.c. claim is inferred from the truncation.

#### PUP.5 Interpretation and remarks

##### PUP.5.1 Proposed phenomenal interpretation

> **Corollary PUP.5.1 (Proposed phenomenal interpretation) [Tier 3; no subject count, owner or Level II].** With part (ii) of Proposition PUP.1 withdrawn, no non-factorizability result is available to support phenomenal unity. What remains is a conditional algebraic statement — (i), and (iii) for a factorial sector — which a separately stated phenomenal bridge might interpret as an algebraic unity candidate. The uniqueness of $R_{\rm inv}$ in (iii) is a density statement only; it does not prove uniqueness of the non-unitary Selection Operator.

Any such interpretation inherits the full closure stack: physical justification of $H_{PUP.1}^{\mathrm{fib}}$, inverse-limit promotion, a faithful represented meridian model or controlled finite-representation family with convergence and trace descent, the Anderson-Putnam extension, identification of a physical factorial sector (O.35/O.36 fail as posed for the trefoil regular representation), O.32, and the Tier 3 phenomenal-identification bridge. Even if all of these closed, the result would be at most an algebraic unity candidate: it would not by itself identify an Identity Polaron, an owner, one subject or Level II.

##### PUP.5.2 Candidate controls do not define the Aggregate–Polaron boundary

> **Remark PUP.5.2 (Finite-level knot type is discrete) [Tier 1 finite-level fact; no physical phase-boundary claim].** *Knot type is a topological invariant with values in a discrete set, so at each finite resolution a change in the prime-decomposition type of the projected core $K_n$ is a discrete change.*

This remark does not formalize a physical Aggregate–Polaron phase boundary, and it does not make that boundary sharp. Whether any physical transition tracks knot type depends on the inverse-limit, physical-realization and coupling questions above, all of which are open; the candidate material controls (nuclear spin, chirality) do not define a binary boundary (V1 Ch16 §16.2.6).

##### PUP.5.3 Split links (illustration only)

> **Remark PUP.5.3 (Split-link illustration) [Tier 3 illustration; not a substrate verdict].** *If a configuration projected at every finite resolution to a split link $\mathcal{L}_n = \mathcal{K}_n^{(1)} \sqcup \mathcal{K}_n^{(2)} \sqcup \cdots$, the fundamental group of its complement would be a non-trivial free product of the component knot groups (van Kampen's theorem applied to the disjoint complements), and part (i) would not apply to it.* Failure of primeness does not by itself give split-link topology — a connected sum of two trefoils is non-prime yet is a single-component knot — and no derivation shows that a thermally decohered Class 0 configuration (V1 Ch11 §11.4.1) projects to a split link [Tier 3 premise].

This remark is not a formulation of "a rock has no unity". A free-product group says nothing, by itself, about Hilbert-space factorization (§PUP.4.2), and nothing here shows that any Class 0 system lacks unity, phenomenal character or Level II. The Level II status of every substrate is open (Tier 3; V1 Ch16 §16.2.7). The remark makes no existence or uniqueness claim about the canonical non-unitary $\mathcal F_{sel}$.
